# React Spectrum Charts for Spectrum 2

`@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` is React Spectrum Charts built on Spectrum 2. You describe a chart as a tree of components, like `Chart`, `Axis`, `Line`, and `Legend`, and the library draws it with Spectrum 2 colors, type, and interactions.

If you use `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` today, see [Migrating from S1](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/migrating-from-s1).

## Your first chart

`Chart` holds the data. Its children name the fields to draw: here, `visits` per `date`, with a line per `device`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={guideVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line dimension="date" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

```bash
npm install @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2
```

See [Getting started](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/getting-started) for peer dependencies and setup.

## Components

-   [Chart](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart): the container for every chart.
-   Charts: [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line), [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar), and [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut).
-   Lab charts: [Area](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/area), [Bullet](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bullet), [Combo](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/combo), and [Scatter](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter).
-   [Axis](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis), [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend), and [Title](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title).
-   [ChartInspect and ChartPopover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction): details on hover and click.
-   [ChartActionBar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar) (lab): actions for a selected point.

---

# Chart

**Stage:** Alpha

`Chart` is the container for every chart. It takes the data, size, colors, and locale, and holds state shared by its children, like hidden and highlighted series. Marks (`Line`, `Bar`, `Donut`, and others), `Axis`, `Legend`, and `Title` go inside it as children.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} title="Visits by channel">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `title` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `Visits by channel`.
-   `colors` on `Chart`: `s2Categorical20` or `blue-1000, blue-700, blue-400`. Shown: `s2Categorical20`.
-   `renderer` on `Chart`: `svg` or `canvas`. Shown: `svg`.
-   `loading` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

`Chart` needs at least one child, or a Vega spec in `UNSAFE_vegaSpec` (see [Advanced](#advanced)). It throws if it has neither, or both.

## Data

`data` is an array of objects, one per data point. Each mark reads the fields you name in its props. Every example on this page uses `chartTrafficData`:

```ts
const chartTrafficData = [
  { id: 1, datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4210 },
  { id: 2, datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4580 },
  { id: 3, datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4390 },
  { id: 4, datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4820 },
  { id: 5, datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5160 },
  { id: 6, datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4970 },
  { id: 7, datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5340 },
  { id: 8, datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5610 },
  { id: 9, datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5480 },
  { id: 10, datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5890 },
  { id: 11, datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 2840 },
  { id: 12, datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3120 },
  { id: 13, datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3460 },
  { id: 14, datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3210 },
  { id: 15, datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3580 },
  { id: 16, datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3920 },
  { id: 17, datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3740 },
  { id: 18, datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3410 },
  { id: 19, datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3650 },
  { id: 20, datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3880 },
  { id: 21, datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Email', value: 1620 },
  { id: 22, datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Email', value: 1480 },
  { id: 23, datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Email', value: 2390 },
  { id: 24, datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Email', value: 1710 },
  { id: 25, datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Email', value: 1560 },
  { id: 26, datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Email', value: 1830 },
  { id: 27, datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Email', value: 2610 },
  { id: 28, datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Email', value: 1790 },
  { id: 29, datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Email', value: 1680 },
  { id: 30, datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Email', value: 1940 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={chartTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
</Chart>
```

Here `Line` draws a line for each `series`, plotting `value` against `datetime`. `Line` reads `datetime` and `value` by default, so the code only needs to name the `color` field.

### idKey

`idKey` names the field that uniquely identifies each row. The chart adds its own row ID by default, so you only need `idKey` to refer to rows from outside the chart, as with `highlightedItem`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} idKey="id" highlightedItem={4}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none`, `4` or `4, 14, 24`. Shown: `4`.

### Empty and loading

When `data` is empty, the chart shows an icon and `emptyStateText` (default `No data found`) in place of the chart. `loading` shows a progress circle instead. Both fill the chart's height.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No visits yet">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No visits yet`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} loading>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

`EmptyState` and `LoadingState` are the components the chart renders for these states. They're exported so you can show the same placeholders outside a chart, for example while fetching data before you render one.

```tsx
<EmptyState height={300} text="No visits yet" />
<LoadingState height={300} />
```

## Size

`width` is a number of pixels, `auto` (the default) to fill the parent's width, or a percentage of the parent's width, like `'75%'`. `height` is a number of pixels (default `300`) or a percentage of the parent's height. The chart resizes when its parent does.

`minWidth` and `maxWidth` clamp an `auto` or percentage width, and `minHeight` and `maxHeight` clamp a percentage height. They don't affect pixel values. In the example below the chart sits in a 512 × 360 `div`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<div style={{ width: 512, height: 360 }}>
  <Chart data={chartTrafficData}>
    <Axis position="left" grid />
    <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
    <Line color="series" />
  </Chart>
</div>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `width` on `Chart`: `auto`, `75%` or `320`. Shown: `auto`.
-   `height` on `Chart`: `300`, `100%` or `50%`. Shown: `300`.
-   `minWidth` on `Chart`: 100 to 512, in steps of 20. Shown: `100`.
-   `maxWidth` on `Chart`: 100 to 512, in steps of 20. Shown: `512`.
-   `minHeight` on `Chart`: 100 to 360, in steps of 20. Shown: `100`.
-   `maxHeight` on `Chart`: 100 to 360, in steps of 20. Shown: `360`.

> **Note:**
> 
> A percentage `height` only works if the parent has an explicit height. Otherwise the chart has no height to measure against.

The size is the whole chart, including axes, legend, and title; the plot area gets what's left. Some marks also adapt to the chart's width: S below 400 px, M from 400 px, and L from 800 px. For example, line strokes are 1.5, 2, and 2.5 px wide at S, M, and L.

### Padding

`padding` adds space between the chart's edge and its contents, as one number or per side, like `{ top: 8, left: 16 }`. The default is `0`. The padding is inside `width` and `height`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} padding={24} backgroundColor="gray-100">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `padding` on `Chart`: 0 to 48, in steps of 4. Shown: `24`.

## Color and theme

### colorScheme and backgroundColor

`colorScheme` (`light` or `dark`, default `light`) picks the light or dark value of every Spectrum color token in the chart, including the mark colors, axes, and text. Set it to match your app's theme. The examples on this site follow the site's theme; see [Colors and theming](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/colors-and-theming#light-and-dark) for each color's light and dark values.

`backgroundColor` fills the chart and is a Spectrum color token, like `gray-25`, or a CSS color. The default is `transparent`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} backgroundColor="gray-25">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `backgroundColor` on `Chart`: `gray-25`, `gray-50`, `gray-100` or `transparent`. Shown: `gray-25`.

### colors

`colors` sets the palette for any mark's `color` field. It takes a named palette, or a list of Spectrum color tokens or CSS colors. The default palette is `s2Categorical20`; `s2Categorical6`, `s2Categorical12`, and `s2Categorical16` are its first 6, 12, and 16 colors. Colors are assigned to series in the order they appear in `data`, and repeat if there are more series than colors.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} colors={['blue-1000', 'blue-700', 'blue-400']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `colors` on `Chart`: `s2Categorical20`, `blue-1000, blue-700, blue-400` or `rgb(15, 181, 174), rgb(64, 70, 202), rgb(246, 133, 17)`. Shown: `blue-1000, blue-700, blue-400`.

`colors` also takes a 2D list, like `[['blue-1000', 'blue-700'], ['red-1000', 'red-700']]`: a group of colors per series, for marks that encode color with two fields.

### Other scales

Marks can also use a field for line type or opacity. The chart's `lineTypes` and `opacities` set the values for those encodings, the same way `colors` does for color. In the example below, `Line` sets `lineType` and `opacity` to `series`, so each series gets the next line type and opacity in the lists.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart
  data={chartTrafficData}
  lineTypes={['solid', 'dashed', 'dotted']}
  opacities={[1, 0.6, 0.3]}
>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line lineType="series" opacity="series" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `lineTypes` on `Chart`: `solid, dashed, dotted` or `solid, longDash, dotDash`. Shown: `solid, dashed, dotted`.
-   `opacities` on `Chart`: `1` or `1, 0.6, 0.3`. Shown: `1, 0.6, 0.3`.

`lineTypes` defaults to `['solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotDash', 'longDash', 'twoDash']` and `opacities` to `[1]`. `lineWidths`, `symbolShapes`, and `symbolSizes` work the same way for marks that encode those, like `Scatter`'s `lineWidth` and `size`, and for legend symbols.

### config

`config` is merged into the chart's [Vega config](https://vega.github.io/vega/docs/config/), so you can override styles the component props don't cover. Prefer props where they exist; config keys can change without notice.

## Locale

`locale` sets how numbers and dates are formatted in axes, labels, and default tooltip content. Pass a locale code, like `'de-DE'`, or separate number and time locales, like `{ number: 'de-DE', time: 'en-US' }`. You can also pass a Vega locale object. The default is `en-US`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} locale="de-DE">
  <Axis position="left" grid numberFormat="standardNumber" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `de-DE`.

The axis above uses `numberFormat="standardNumber"` so every tick shows the locale's grouping separator.

## Title and accessibility

`title` adds a title above the chart and is the default file name for `download()`. For more options, use a `Title` child instead. See [Title](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title).

`description` sets the chart's accessible label (`aria-label`). Describe what the chart shows.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart
  data={chartTrafficData}
  title="Visits by channel"
  description="Daily visits from March 2 to 11 by channel. Organic search leads and grows; email stays lowest."
>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `title` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `Visits by channel`.
-   `description` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `Daily visits from March 2 to 11 by channel. Organic search leads and grows; email stays lowest.`.

## Hiding and highlighting

`hiddenSeries` and `highlightedSeries` hide or highlight series from outside the chart, for example to sync the chart with a table. They're controlled: the chart shows what you pass and doesn't change them itself. `highlightedItem` highlights rows by ID (see [idKey](#idkey)).

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} highlightedSeries="Paid search">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Email` or `Paid search, Email`. Shown: `none`.
-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Organic search`, `Paid search` or `Email`. Shown: `Paid search`.

See [Highlighting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#highlighting) for how each mark shows highlighting.

## Tooltips

`tooltipAnchor` and `tooltipPlacement` set where `ChartInspect` content appears. By default it follows the cursor. With `tooltipAnchor="mark"` it attaches to the hovered mark, on the side given by `tooltipPlacement` (default `top`).

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData} tooltipAnchor="mark">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.series}: {datum.value.toLocaleString()} visits
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `tooltipAnchor` on `Chart`: `cursor` or `mark`. Shown: `mark`.
-   `tooltipPlacement` on `Chart`: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `top`.

See [ChartInspect and ChartPopover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction) for the content and behavior of tooltips and popovers.

## Animation

`animationTypes` lists the animations to play. The default, `['hover', 'drawIn']`, eases marks in and out of their faded state when the chart is hovered or highlighted, and animates marks in when the chart first renders. Set `animationTypes={['hover']}` to turn off draw-in only. `animations={false}` turns off every animation.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={chartTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.series}: {datum.value.toLocaleString()} visits
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `animations` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `hover`, `hover, drawIn` or `drawIn`. Shown: `hover, drawIn`.

If the user prefers reduced motion, draw-in is skipped; hover animation still plays.

> **Note:**
> 
> Line draws in on `time`, `linear`, and `point` scales only.

## Exporting images

Pass a `ref` to get a handle with these methods. Each returns a promise, and rejects if there's no chart to export, for example while loading or when there's no data.

-   `download(fileName?)`: downloads a PNG. The file is named `fileName`, or the `title` if you don't pass one, or `chart_export`, followed by `.png`.
-   `copy()`: copies a PNG to the clipboard.
-   `getBase64Png()`: resolves to the PNG as a base64 data URL.
-   `getSvg()`: resolves to the chart as an SVG string.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { ActionButton } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import { Axis, Chart, ChartHandle, Legend, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

const ref = useRef<ChartHandle>(null);

<Chart ref={ref} data={chartTrafficData} title="Visits by channel">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
<ActionButton onPress={() => ref.current?.download()}>Download PNG</ActionButton>
<ActionButton onPress={() => ref.current?.copy()}>Copy PNG</ActionButton>
<ActionButton onPress={async () => setSvg(await ref.current?.getSvg())}>Get SVG</ActionButton>
```

## Advanced

-   `renderer`: `svg` (default) or `canvas`. Canvas is faster for large datasets.
-   `debug`: logs the generated Vega spec and inspect data to the console.
-   `onVegaViewReady(view)`: called with the [Vega view](https://vega.github.io/vega/docs/api/view/) once per view. Data and size changes update the current view instead of creating a new one.
-   `UNSAFE_vegaSpec`: renders a Vega spec you write instead of building one from children. `data` can then also be a list of Vega datasets. You lose the Spectrum defaults the components apply.
-   `dataTestId`: sets `data-testid` on the chart's container.

## API

### Chart

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessibleNavigation` — Experimental keyboard navigation. Only basic bar charts are supported. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `animations` — Set to `false` to turn off every animation, including hover and draw-in. Draw-in is skipped for users who prefer reduced motion. | `boolean` | – |
| `animationTypes` — Animations to play: `hover`, `drawIn`, or both. | `AnimationType[]` | `['hover', 'drawIn']` |
| `backgroundColor` — Background color of the chart, as a Spectrum color token or CSS color. | `string` | `'transparent'` |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `ChartChild` | – |
| `colors` — Colors for series: a named palette, a list of Spectrum color tokens or CSS colors, or a list of lists when a mark's `color` uses two fields. | `ChartColors` | `'s2Categorical20'` |
| `colorScheme` — Light or dark colors. Set it to match your app, since the chart doesn't read your app's theme. | `"light" \| "dark"` | `'light'` |
| `config` — Vega config for low-level style overrides. @see https://vega.github.io/vega/docs/config/ | `Config` | – |
| `data`required — Rows of data to chart. | `ChartData[]` | – |
| `dataTestId` — Value for the chart container's `data-testid` attribute. | `string` | – |
| `debug` — Logs the generated Vega spec and inspected rows to the console. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `description` — Accessible name for the chart, read by screen readers. Describe what the chart shows. | `string` | – |
| `emptyStateText` — Text to display when the data set is empty and loading is complete. | `string` | `'No data found'` |
| `height` — Chart height in pixels, or a percentage of the container height. | `Height` | `300` |
| `hiddenSeries` — Names of series to hide. | `string[]` | `[]` |
| `highlightedItem` — ID or IDs of rows to highlight. Set `idKey` to a field with a unique value for each row. | `HighlightedItem` | – |
| `highlightedSeries` — Name of the series to highlight. | `string \| number` | – |
| `idKey` — Field with a unique ID for each row. Defaults to an ID the chart adds to each row. | `string` | – |
| `lineTypes` — Line types assigned to series when a mark's `lineType` uses a field. | `LineTypes` | `['solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotDash', 'longDash', 'twoDash']` |
| `lineWidths` — Line widths assigned to series when a mark's `lineWidth` uses a field. | `LineWidth[]` | `['M']` |
| `loading` — Shows a loading spinner in place of the chart. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `locale` — Number and time locales for formatting, as a locale code, separate number and time locales, or a Vega locale. | `Locale \| "ar-EG" \| "ar-SY" \| "ca-ES" \| …` | `'en-US'` |
| `maxHeight` — Maximum chart height in pixels when `height` is a percentage. | `number` | – |
| `maxWidth` — Maximum chart width in pixels when `width` is `auto` or a percentage. | `number` | – |
| `minHeight` — Minimum chart height in pixels when `height` is a percentage. | `number` | `100` |
| `minWidth` — Minimum chart width in pixels when `width` is `auto` or a percentage. | `number` | `100` |
| `onVegaViewReady` — Called with the Vega view each time the chart creates one, such as after data or props change. | `((view: View) => void)` | – |
| `opacities` — Opacities assigned to series when a mark's `opacity` uses a field. | `Opacities` | `[1]` |
| `padding` — Space around the chart contents in pixels, as one number or per side. | `Padding` | `0` |
| `ref` — Handle for exporting the chart with `copy`, `download`, `getBase64Png` and `getSvg`. | `Ref<ChartHandle>` | – |
| `renderer` — Draws the chart as `svg` or `canvas`. `canvas` is faster for large data sets but exposes less to screen readers. | `"svg" \| "canvas"` | `'svg'` |
| `symbolShapes` — Shapes assigned to series when a mark's `symbolShape` uses a field. | `SymbolShapes` | `['rounded-square']` |
| `symbolSizes` — Smallest and largest symbol size when a mark's `size` uses a field. | `[SymbolSize, SymbolSize]` | `['XS', 'XL']` |
| `title` — Title shown above the chart. A `Title` child replaces it. | `string` | – |
| `tooltipAnchor` — Whether `ChartInspect` content follows the cursor or anchors to the hovered mark. | `"cursor" \| "mark"` | `'cursor'` |
| `tooltipPlacement` — Where `ChartInspect` content sits relative to the mark when `tooltipAnchor` is `mark`. | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `'top'` |
| `UNSAFE_vegaSpec` — Vega spec to render instead of building one from children. Can't be combined with children. | `Spec` | – |
| `width` — Chart width in pixels, `auto` to fill the container, or a percentage of the container width. | `Width` | `'auto'` |

### EmptyState

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `height` — Height of the empty state in pixels. | `number` | – |
| `text` — Message shown under the icon. | `string` | – |

### LoadingState

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `height` — Height of the loading state in pixels. | `number` | – |

---

# Line

**Stage:** Alpha

Line charts show how values change over time. Each series becomes a line through its data points, plotted by `dimension` on the x-axis and `metric` on the y-axis.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Title text="Visits by channel" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
  <Legend position="bottom" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `interpolate` on `Line`: `linear`, `monotone` or `step`. Shown: `linear`.
-   `LineDirectLabel`: included or left out. Shown: left out.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `none`, `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Visits by channel`.

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per point. On `Line`, `dimension` names the x-axis field (default `datetime`), `metric` names the y-axis field (default `value`), and `color` names the field that splits the rows into series. Without `color`, every row belongs to one line. Time values are milliseconds since the epoch. Most examples on this page use `lineTrafficData`:

```ts
const lineTrafficData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4210 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4580 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4820 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5160 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4970 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5340 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5610 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5480 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5890 },
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 2840 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3120 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3460 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3210 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3580 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3920 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3740 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3410 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3650 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3880 },
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Email', value: 1620 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Email', value: 1480 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Email', value: 2390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Email', value: 1710 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Email', value: 1560 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Email', value: 1830 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Email', value: 2610 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Email', value: 1790 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Email', value: 1680 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Email', value: 1940 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
</Chart>
```

### Empty and loading

When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead of the plot. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No visits yet">
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No visits yet`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData} loading>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
</Chart>
```

## Lines

### Series

`color`, `lineType`, and `opacity` each take either a data field or a fixed value such as `{ value: 'dashed' }`. A field gives each series its own color, dash pattern, or opacity from the chart's `colors`, `lineTypes`, and `opacities` lists. `color` defaults to a single categorical color and `lineType` to solid.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `lineType` on `Line`: `none` or `series`. Shown: `none`.
-   `opacity` on `Line`: `none` or `series`. Shown: `none`.

### interpolate

`interpolate` sets the curve between points. The default, `linear`, draws straight segments.

-   `monotone` draws a smooth curve that never overshoots the data.
-   `basis`, `cardinal`, `catmull-rom`, and `natural` draw other kinds of splines. `basis` doesn't pass through the data, so it draws no points.
-   `step`, `step-before`, and `step-after` draw horizontal and vertical steps, with the vertical step centered between points, at the start of each interval, or at the end.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineMilestoneData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line interpolate="monotone" staticPoint="isMilestone" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `interpolate` on `Line`: `linear`, `monotone`, `basis`, `cardinal`, `catmull-rom`, `natural`, `step`, `step-before` or `step-after`. Shown: `monotone`.

### gradient

`gradient` fills the area under the line with its color, fading to transparent at the bottom. The gradient only draws when the chart has a single line. `opacity` fades the line and its gradient together.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line gradient />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `gradient` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `opacity` on `Line`: 0.2 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `1`.

### Size

Stroke width, point size, and hover rings scale with the chart's width: a chart under 400px wide uses the small size, one under 800px the medium size, and anything wider the large size. Use `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, and `maxWidth` on `Chart` to constrain it. Drag the width below 400 to see the small size.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineMilestoneData} width={480} height={300}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line staticPoint="isMilestone" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `width` on `Chart`: 240 to 500, in steps of 20. Shown: `480`.

## Points

### staticPoint

Points are hidden until hovered. `staticPoint` names a boolean field; rows where it's exactly `true` always show a point. Points scale with the chart; set `pointSize` to fix their area in square pixels.

```ts
const lineMilestoneData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, value: 4210 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, value: 4580 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, value: 4390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, value: 4820, isMilestone: true, annotation: 'Launch' },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, value: 5160 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, value: 4970 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, value: 5340 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, value: 5960, isMilestone: true, annotation: 'Record high' },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, value: 5480 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, value: 5710 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineMilestoneData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line staticPoint="isMilestone" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `staticPoint` on `Line`: `none` or `isMilestone`. Shown: `isMilestone`.
-   `pointSize` on `Line`: `auto`, `36`, `100` or `196`. Shown: `auto`.

### Sparklines

`isSparkline` with `isMethodLast` draws a point on the last row of the data. The sparkline shown has no axes and is 200 × 60px.

```jsx
import { Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineVisitsData}>
  <Line isSparkline isMethodLast gradient />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `isMethodLast` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `gradient` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Segments

### Alternate segments

`alternateSegmentKey` names a boolean field. Rows where it's truthy draw in `alternateSegmentLineType` (default `dotted`), for example to mark estimated or incomplete values.

```ts
const lineEstimatedData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4210, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4580, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4390, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4820, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5160, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Organic search', value: 4970, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5340, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5610, isEstimated: true },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5480, isEstimated: true },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Organic search', value: 5890, isEstimated: true },
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 2840, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3120, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3460, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3210, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3580, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3920, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3740, isEstimated: false },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3410, isEstimated: true },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3650, isEstimated: true },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Paid search', value: 3880, isEstimated: true },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartPopover,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={lineEstimatedData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" alternateSegmentKey="isEstimated">
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <Content>
          <Heading level={4} UNSAFE_style={{ margin: 0 }}>
            {datum.series}
          </Heading>
          <Text>{datum.value.toLocaleString()} visits</Text>
        </Content>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `alternateSegmentKey` on `Line`: `none` or `isEstimated`. Shown: `isEstimated`.
-   `alternateSegmentLineType` on `Line`: `dotted`, `dashed` or `shortDash`. Shown: `dotted`.

### primarySeries

`primarySeries` keeps some series in color and draws the rest in gray. Pass a number N to keep the first N series in color order (`2` keeps the first two), or a list of series names. `otherSeriesColor` changes the gray (default `gray-400`) to another Spectrum 2 color token. Gray series don't get `LineDirectLabel` labels.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Line,
  LineDirectLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" primarySeries={1}>
    <LineDirectLabel value="series" />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `primarySeries` on `Line`: `none`, `1`, `2` or `Email`. Shown: `1`.
-   `otherSeriesColor` on `Line`: `gray-400`, `gray-300` or `gray-600`. Shown: `gray-400`.

> **Note:**
> 
> Don't combine `alternateSegmentKey` with `LineForecast`. The line then ignores the forecast's `metric` field and dashes only the rows flagged by `alternateSegmentKey`, though the forecast's boundary rule and label still draw. `primarySeries` works with either one.

## Scales

### scaleType

`scaleType` sets the x scale. `time` (the default) is for timestamps, and `linear` for other numeric values such as minutes. Both keep the gaps between values to scale. `point` spaces ordered categories such as weekdays evenly; use it only when the x values aren't times or numbers.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline ticks labelFormat="time" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" dimension="datetime" scaleType="time" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `scaleType` on `Line`: `time`, `linear` or `point`. Shown: `time`.

### padding

`padding` adds space between the plot edges and the first and last points. Its unit depends on `scaleType`:

-   `time` and `linear`: pixels. The default is `0`, so the line touches both edges.
-   `point`: a ratio of the step between points, from 0 to 1. The default is `0.5`.

This example uses a time scale.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline ticks labelFormat="time" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" dimension="datetime" scaleType="time" padding={24} />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `padding` on `Line`: 0 to 48, in steps of 4. Shown: `24`.

### dualMetricAxis

`dualMetricAxis` compares the trends of two series whose values are far apart. On a shared y-axis, the smaller series, here purchases, is flattened near zero. `dualMetricAxis` plots the last series against its own y-scale, shown by an `Axis` with `position="right"`, so you can see purchases fall while visits rise. Turn it off to see the shared scale, where the right axis isn't needed.

The right axis labels take the color of the last series. When there are only two series, the left axis labels take the color of the first.

```ts
const lineDualAxisData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Visits', value: 4210 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Visits', value: 4580 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Visits', value: 4390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Visits', value: 4820 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Visits', value: 5160 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Visits', value: 4970 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Visits', value: 5340 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Visits', value: 5610 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Visits', value: 5480 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Visits', value: 5890 },
  { datetime: 1772409600000, series: 'Purchases', value: 142 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, series: 'Purchases', value: 138 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, series: 'Purchases', value: 131 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, series: 'Purchases', value: 127 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, series: 'Purchases', value: 119 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, series: 'Purchases', value: 114 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, series: 'Purchases', value: 106 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, series: 'Purchases', value: 101 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, series: 'Purchases', value: 94 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, series: 'Purchases', value: 88 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineDualAxisData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" />
  <Line color="series" dualMetricAxis>
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `dualMetricAxis` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Hover

Lines respond to the pointer when they have `ChartInspect`, `ChartPopover`, `ChartActionBar`, `onClick`, or `onContextMenu`. Hovering fades the other series, rings the hovered point, and shows its value next to it.

-   `interactionMode="nearest"` (the default) picks the point closest to the pointer anywhere in the plot. `item` picks a point only when the pointer is over it.
-   `dimensionHover` highlights every series at the hovered x value and labels each of them.
-   `showHoverLabel={false}` hides the value label. `ChartInspect` always hides it, since the inspect dialog shows the value. Set `hoverLabelKey` to show another field, such as a pre-formatted string.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartPopover,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <Content>
          <Heading level={4} UNSAFE_style={{ margin: 0 }}>
            {datum.series}
          </Heading>
          <Text>{datum.value.toLocaleString()} visits</Text>
        </Content>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `interactionMode` on `Line`: `nearest` or `item`. Shown: `nearest`.
-   `dimensionHover` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `showHoverLabel` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Metric ranges

`metricRanges` shades a band between two fields, such as the confidence interval of a forecast. Each object needs `metricStart` and `metricEnd`, and draws its own dashed line through `metric` (default `value`). This example pairs a range with [`LineForecast`](#lineforecast): the range's `metric` is the forecast field, and the band starts at the last actual value, where `low` and `high` equal `value`.

-   `rangeOpacity` sets the band's opacity (default `0.2`).
-   `lineType` and `lineWidth` style the range's line (default `dashed` and `S`).
-   `displayOnHover` shows the range only while its series is hovered.
-   `scaleAxisToFit` stretches the y-axis to include the whole band.

```ts
const lineRangeData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, value: 4210, forecast: 4210 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, value: 4580, forecast: 4580 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, value: 4390, forecast: 4390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, value: 4820, forecast: 4820 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, value: 5160, forecast: 5160 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, value: 4970, forecast: 4970 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, value: 5340, forecast: 5340 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, value: 5610, forecast: 5610 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, value: 5480, forecast: 5480 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, value: 5890, forecast: 5890, low: 5890, high: 5890 },
  { datetime: 1773273600000, value: null, forecast: 6020, low: 5780, high: 6260 },
  { datetime: 1773360000000, value: null, forecast: 6150, low: 5760, high: 6540 },
  { datetime: 1773446400000, value: null, forecast: 6240, low: 5700, high: 6780 },
  { datetime: 1773532800000, value: null, forecast: 6380, low: 5660, high: 7100 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineRangeData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line
    metricRanges={[{ metric: 'forecast', metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', scaleAxisToFit: true }]}
  >
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **rangeOpacity** (metricRanges): 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.2`.
-   **lineType** (metricRanges): `dashed`, `solid` or `dotted`. Shown: `dashed`.
-   **displayOnHover** (metricRanges): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   **scaleAxisToFit** (metricRanges): `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

With **lineType** set to `solid`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineRangeData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line
    metricRanges={[{ metric: 'forecast', metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', lineType: 'solid', scaleAxisToFit: true }]}
  >
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

With **lineType** set to `dotted`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineRangeData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line
    metricRanges={[{ metric: 'forecast', metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', lineType: 'dotted', scaleAxisToFit: true }]}
  >
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

With **displayOnHover** set to `true`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineRangeData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line
    metricRanges={[{ metric: 'forecast', metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', displayOnHover: true, scaleAxisToFit: true }]}
  >
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

With **scaleAxisToFit** set to `false`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineRangeData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line
    metricRanges={[{ metric: 'forecast', metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', scaleAxisToFit: false }]}
  >
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

> **Note:**
> 
> A metric range's `metric` defaults to `value`, not to the parent line's `metric`. Set it when your line uses another field.

## LineDirectLabel

`LineDirectLabel` labels each line at the right edge of the plot, which can replace a legend. Labels are colored like their series and spread apart when they would overlap.

-   `value` chooses the text: the `last` value (the default), the `average`, or the `series` name.
-   `position="start"` moves labels to the left edge and labels the first value instead.
-   `format` is a [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier for numeric values (default `,.2~f`). `prefix` adds text before the value.
-   `excludeSeries` skips the listed series.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Line,
  LineDirectLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <LineDirectLabel />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `value` on `LineDirectLabel`: `last`, `average` or `series`. Shown: `last`.
-   `position` on `LineDirectLabel`: `end` or `start`. Shown: `end`.
-   `format` on `LineDirectLabel`: `,.2~f`, `,.1f` or `.2s`. Shown: `,.2~f`.
-   `prefix` on `LineDirectLabel`: any text. Shown: empty.
-   `excludeSeries` on `LineDirectLabel`: `none` or `Email`. Shown: `none`.

## LineForecast

`LineForecast` continues a line with forecast values. Put the forecast in its own field, `metric`, and leave the line's `metric` empty for those rows. `start` is the x value (a timestamp on a time scale) where the forecast begins. From there on the line uses `alternateSegmentLineType` (default `dotted`), and a vertical rule marks the boundary with `label` (default `Forecast`).

```ts
const lineForecastData = [
  { datetime: 1772409600000, value: 4210 },
  { datetime: 1772496000000, value: 4580 },
  { datetime: 1772582400000, value: 4390 },
  { datetime: 1772668800000, value: 4820 },
  { datetime: 1772755200000, value: 5160 },
  { datetime: 1772841600000, value: 4970 },
  { datetime: 1772928000000, value: 5340 },
  { datetime: 1773014400000, value: 5610 },
  { datetime: 1773100800000, value: 5480 },
  { datetime: 1773187200000, value: 5890 },
  { datetime: 1773273600000, value: null, forecast: 6020 },
  { datetime: 1773360000000, value: null, forecast: 6150 },
  { datetime: 1773446400000, value: null, forecast: 6240 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  LineForecast,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineForecastData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line>
    <LineForecast metric="forecast" start={1773187200000} />
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `start` on `LineForecast`: `Mar 9`, `Mar 10`, `Mar 11` or `Mar 12`. Shown: `Mar 11`.
-   `label` on `LineForecast`: any text. Shown: `Forecast`.

## Axes

Line charts usually have a bottom `Axis` with `labelFormat="time"` and a left `Axis` with `grid`. Time labels follow the axis `granularity`, and number labels follow `numberFormat` (default `shortNumber`). Both use the chart's `locale`, which also applies to `ChartInspect`.

Add `ReferenceLine` inside the left `Axis` to mark a value, such as a target. See [Axis](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis) for every axis and reference line option.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Line,
  ReferenceLine,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid>
    <ReferenceLine value={5000} label="Target" />
  </Axis>
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `title` on `Axis`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `granularity` on `Axis`: `day` or `week`. Shown: `day`.
-   `numberFormat` on `Axis`: `shortNumber` or `standardNumber`. Shown: `shortNumber`.
-   `ReferenceLine`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Line` to list the series.

-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its series.
-   `highlight` highlights a series while its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend title="Channel" isToggleable highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

### Hiding series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. To start with series hidden but let users toggle them, set `defaultHiddenSeries` on a toggleable `Legend` instead.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData} hiddenSeries={['Email']}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Email` or `Paid search, Email`. Shown: `Email`.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Pass a function as children to render your own content.

-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect` sets what stays in color while inspecting: the hovered `item` (the default), its whole `series`, or every point at the same x value (`dimension`).
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover` opens it on right-click instead of click.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect />
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <Content>
          <Heading level={4} UNSAFE_style={{ margin: 0 }}>
            {datum.series}
          </Heading>
          <Text>{datum.value.toLocaleString()} visits</Text>
        </Content>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series` or `dimension`. Shown: `item`.
-   `children` on `ChartInspect`: `default` or `custom`. Shown: `default`.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

`onClick` and `onContextMenu` on `Line` run a callback with the clicked point's data. `ChartActionBar` shows actions for a selected point; see [ChartActionBar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar). See [Interaction](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction) for every `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` option.

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row. `highlightedItem` highlights points by row ID and can take a list; set `idKey` on `Chart` to the field it matches. In this example `idKey` is `datetime`, so one date highlights a point on every series.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Organic search`, `Paid search` or `Email`. Shown: `none`.
-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none` or `Mar 8`. Shown: `none`.

## Animation

The chart's `animationTypes` lists which animations play. By default, `hover` eases the other lines in and out of their faded state when you hover a line, and `drawIn` sweeps the lines in from left to right over 850ms when the chart mounts; static points appear as the sweep passes them. Draw-in works on time, linear, and point scales.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line color="series">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

Set `animationTypes={['hover']}` to turn off draw-in only, or `animations={false}` to turn off all animation. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation) for when draw-in replays.

## API

### Line

`name` identifies the line's marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `line0`, `line1`, and so on.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alternateSegmentKey` — Data field key whose truthy value marks a point as part of an alternate segment. Alternate segments render with a different line type (see `alternateSegmentLineType`). | `string` | – |
| `alternateSegmentLabel` — Text appended to the hover value label for alternate-segment points (e.g. `'(Estimated)'`). No default — omitting means no append. | `string` | – |
| `alternateSegmentLineType` — Line type used for alternate segments identified by `alternateSegmentKey`. | `LineType` | `''dotted''` |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `LineChild` | – |
| `color` — Line color or key in the data that is used as the color facet | `ColorFacet` | `{ value: 'categorical-100' }` |
| `contextMenuMode` — Controls which marks can trigger `onContextMenu`. | `"dimension" \| "item" \| "interaction"` | `'interaction'` |
| `dimension` — Data field that the value is trended against (x-axis) | `string` | `'datetime'` |
| `dimensionHover` — If `true`, all series at the hovered x-dimension highlight simultaneously instead of only the nearest series. Hover value labels show for every series at that dimension. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `dualMetricAxis` — Enables dual metric axis mode where the last series uses a secondary axis with independent scale | `boolean` | – |
| `gradient` — Fills the area under the line with its color, fading to transparent. Use on charts with a single line. | `boolean` | – |
| `hoverLabelKey` — Data field key to display in the hover value label. Defaults to the `metric` field. Use this to show a pre-formatted or alternate field (e.g. `'displayValue'`) instead of the raw metric. | `string` | – |
| `interactionMode` — Sets how hovering picks a point: `'nearest'` uses the closest point, `'item'` only the point under the pointer. | `"dimension" \| "item" \| "nearest"` | `'nearest'` |
| `interpolate` — Sets the interpolation method for the line. `basis` doesn't pass through the data, so it draws no points. | `InterpolationType` | – |
| `isMethodLast` — With `isSparkline`, draws a static point on the last row of the chart data. | `boolean` | – |
| `isSparkline` — Renders the line as a sparkline. With `isMethodLast`, draws a static point on the last data point. | `boolean` | – |
| `lineCap` — Sets the stroke line cap style for the line ends and gap boundaries. | `"square" \| "round"` | `'round'` |
| `lineType` — Line type or key in the data that is used as the line type facet | `LineTypeFacet` | `{ value: 'solid' }` |
| `metric` — Key in the data that is used as the metric | `string` | `'value'` |
| `metricAxis` — Axis that the metric is trended against (y-axis) | `string` | – |
| `metricRanges` — Shaded ranges drawn around the line, each between two data fields. | `MetricRangeOptions[]` | – |
| `name` — Sets the name of the component. | `string` | `'line0'` |
| `onClick` — Called with the row's data when a point is clicked. | `MarkCallback` | – |
| `onContextMenu` — Called with the event and the row's data when a point is right-clicked. Use it to show a custom context menu. Use `contextMenuMode` to control which marks can trigger it. | `ContextMenuCallback` | – |
| `opacity` — Opacity or key in the data that is used as the opacity facet | `OpacityFacet` | – |
| `otherSeriesColor` — Color for series outside `primarySeries`, as a Spectrum color token or CSS color. | `string` | – |
| `padding` — Sets the chart area padding, this is a ratio from 0 to 1 for categorical scales (point) and a pixel value for continuous scales (time, linear) | `number` | – |
| `pointSize` — Area of static points in square pixels. When omitted, points scale with chart width. | `number` | – |
| `primarySeries` — Series to keep in color; the rest turn gray and lose their direct labels. Pass a number N for the first N series, or a list of series names. | `number \| string[]` | – |
| `scaleType` — Sets the x scale type: `'time'`, `'linear'`, or `'point'`. | `"linear" \| "time" \| "point" \| "band"` | `'time'` |
| `showHoverLabel` — If `true`, shows the metric value as a label adjacent to the hovered data point. Suppressed when a `<ChartInspect>` child is present. | `boolean` | `true` |
| `staticPoint` — Data field that marks rows to highlight; a point is drawn on the line for each row where it's true. | `string` | – |
| `trendlines` | `TrendlineOptions[]` | – |

### LineDirectLabel

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `excludeSeries` — Series values to exclude from labeling. | `string[]` | – |
| `fontSize` — Override font size in pixels. When omitted, font size scales automatically with chart size. | `number` | – |
| `format` — d3 number format for the value. | `string` | `'',.2~f''` |
| `position` — Where to place the label along the line. - 'end': right side of the chart, y-positioned at the last data point - 'start': left side of the chart, y-positioned at the first data point | `"start" \| "end"` | `'end'` |
| `prefix` — Text prepended to the value, separated by a space. | `string` | – |
| `value` — Value to display. - 'last': value at last data point - 'average': average of all values in the line - 'series': series key/name | `"series" \| "last" \| "average"` | `'last'` |

### LineForecast

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` — Label text shown at the forecast boundary. | `string` | `'Forecast'` |
| `metric`required — Data field containing the forecasted metric values | `string` | – |
| `start`required — Dimension value (timestamp for time scale, number for linear) where the forecast begins | `number` | – |

---

# Bar

**Stage:** Alpha

Bars compare values across categories. Each category gets a bar sized by its `metric` value, and series within a category are stacked or placed side by side.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Title text="Visits by channel" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend position="bottom" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.
-   `color` on `Bar`: `by device` or `single`. Shown: `by device`.
-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `none`, `bottom`, `right`, `left` or `top`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Visits by channel`.

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per bar or bar segment. On `Bar`, `dimension` names the field for the categories (default `category`) and `metric` names the numeric field that sizes each bar (default `value`). Set `color` to a field to split each category into series; each row is one segment. Without a `color` field, every bar uses the first categorical color. Most examples on this page use `barChannelData` or `barChannelDeviceData`:

```ts
const barChannelData = [
  { channel: 'Search', visits: 12400 },
  { channel: 'Direct', visits: 9800 },
  { channel: 'Social', visits: 7300 },
  { channel: 'Email', visits: 5100 },
  { channel: 'Referral', visits: 3600 },
  { channel: 'Display', visits: 2200 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

```ts
const barChannelDeviceData = [
  { id: 'search-desktop', channel: 'Search', device: 'Desktop', visits: 6200, stackOrder: 3 },
  { id: 'search-mobile', channel: 'Search', device: 'Mobile', visits: 4800, stackOrder: 2 },
  { id: 'search-tablet', channel: 'Search', device: 'Tablet', visits: 1400, stackOrder: 1 },
  { id: 'direct-desktop', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5100, stackOrder: 3 },
  { id: 'direct-mobile', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3700, stackOrder: 2 },
  { id: 'direct-tablet', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Tablet', visits: 1000, stackOrder: 1 },
  { id: 'social-desktop', channel: 'Social', device: 'Desktop', visits: 1900, stackOrder: 3 },
  { id: 'social-mobile', channel: 'Social', device: 'Mobile', visits: 4600, stackOrder: 2 },
  { id: 'social-tablet', channel: 'Social', device: 'Tablet', visits: 800, stackOrder: 1 },
  { id: 'email-desktop', channel: 'Email', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2600, stackOrder: 3 },
  { id: 'email-mobile', channel: 'Email', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2000, stackOrder: 2 },
  { id: 'email-tablet', channel: 'Email', device: 'Tablet', visits: 500, stackOrder: 1 },
  { id: 'referral-desktop', channel: 'Referral', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2100, stackOrder: 3 },
  { id: 'referral-mobile', channel: 'Referral', device: 'Mobile', visits: 1200, stackOrder: 2 },
  { id: 'referral-tablet', channel: 'Referral', device: 'Tablet', visits: 300, stackOrder: 1 },
];
```

Categories appear in the order they first occur in the data. `Bar` has no sort prop, so sort your data before passing it in to change the order.

### Dates

To use dates as categories, set `dimensionDataType="time"` and give the category `Axis` `labelFormat="time"` and a `granularity`. Each date is still its own bar, evenly spaced; bars don't leave gaps for missing dates.

```ts
const barMonthlyData = [
  { month: '2025-01-01 00:00:00', visits: 11800 },
  { month: '2025-02-01 00:00:00', visits: 12600 },
  { month: '2025-03-01 00:00:00', visits: 14100 },
  { month: '2025-04-01 00:00:00', visits: 13400 },
  { month: '2025-05-01 00:00:00', visits: 15900 },
  { month: '2025-06-01 00:00:00', visits: 17200 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barMonthlyData}>
  <Axis
    position="bottom"
    baseline
    title="Month"
    labelFormat="time"
    granularity="month"
  />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="month" metric="visits" dimensionDataType="time" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

> **Tip:**
> 
> Write dates without a time zone, like `'2025-01-01 00:00:00'`, so they're read in the viewer's local time. A date-only string like `'2025-01-01'` is read as UTC and can show as the previous day or month west of UTC.

### Zero, empty, and loading

When every value is 0, the categories still show on the axis with no bars. When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```ts
const barZeroData = [
  { channel: 'Search', visits: 0 },
  { channel: 'Direct', visits: 0 },
  { channel: 'Social', visits: 0 },
  { channel: 'Email', visits: 0 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barZeroData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `all zeros`, `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `all zeros`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No visits yet`.

With **state** set to `empty`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No visits yet">
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData} loading>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

## Orientation

Bars are vertical by default. Set `orientation="horizontal"` to draw them left to right, which leaves more room for long category names. Swap the `Axis` positions to match: the category axis goes on the left and the value axis on the bottom.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="left" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" orientation="horizontal" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `horizontal`.

## Stacked and dodged

With more than one series, `type` controls how they share a category.

-   `stacked` (default) piles segments on top of each other, so the bar shows the category total.
-   `dodged` places one bar per series side by side, so series are easy to compare.

`order` names a numeric field that sets the stack order; segments with a higher value sit further from the baseline. Without it, segments stack in data order. Try `order="stackOrder"` to put Tablet at the bottom.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.
-   `order` on `Bar`: `none` or `stackOrder`. Shown: `none`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

### Dodged and stacked

Pass two fields to `color` to dodge by the first and stack by the second. Each dodged bar is then a stack. Give `Chart` a nested `colors` list, one list of shades per dodged group, so each group keeps its own hue. `groupedPadding` sets the space between bars in a group as a ratio of the bar width; it defaults to `paddingRatio`.

```ts
const barChannelVisitorData = [
  { channel: 'Search', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'New', visits: 3900 },
  { channel: 'Search', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 2300 },
  { channel: 'Search', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'New', visits: 3100 },
  { channel: 'Search', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 1700 },
  { channel: 'Direct', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'New', visits: 1600 },
  { channel: 'Direct', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 3500 },
  { channel: 'Direct', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'New', visits: 1300 },
  { channel: 'Direct', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 2400 },
  { channel: 'Social', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'New', visits: 1200 },
  { channel: 'Social', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 700 },
  { channel: 'Social', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'New', visits: 3200 },
  { channel: 'Social', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 1400 },
  { channel: 'Email', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'New', visits: 600 },
  { channel: 'Email', device: 'Desktop', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 2000 },
  { channel: 'Email', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'New', visits: 500 },
  { channel: 'Email', device: 'Mobile', visitor: 'Returning', visits: 1500 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart
  data={barChannelVisitorData}
  colors={[['blue-900', 'blue-500'], ['fuchsia-900', 'fuchsia-500']]}
>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar
    dimension="channel"
    metric="visits"
    color={['device', 'visitor']}
    type="dodged"
  />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `groupedPadding` on `Bar`: 0 to 0.9, in steps of 0.05. Shown: `0.4`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

`lineType` and `opacity` also accept two fields, and the same rule applies to them.

## Spacing

`paddingRatio` is the space between categories, as a share of each category's band: `0` makes bars touch and `0.9` makes them thin. The default is `0.4`. `paddingOuter` is the space before the first bar and after the last; it defaults to half of `paddingRatio`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `paddingRatio` on `Bar`: 0 to 0.9, in steps of 0.05. Shown: `0.4`.
-   `paddingOuter` on `Bar`: `auto`, `0`, `0.2`, `0.5` or `1`. Shown: `auto`.

Bar width comes from the chart width, the number of categories, and the padding. There's no prop to set a fixed bar width.

## Appearance

-   Bars have rounded corners at their ends. Set `hasSquareCorners` to square them.
-   `opacity` takes `{ value }` for a static opacity, or a field name to vary it by series.
-   `lineWidth` adds a border in the bar's own color, and `lineType` makes that border `dashed` or `dotted`. The border is easiest to see with reduced `opacity`. Like `opacity`, `lineType` can be a field name to vary it by series.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hasSquareCorners` on `Bar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `opacity` on `Bar`: 0.1 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `1`.
-   `lineWidth` on `Bar`: 0 to 6, in steps of 1. Shown: `0`.
-   `lineType` on `Bar`: `solid`, `dashed` or `dotted`. Shown: `solid`.

### colorOverride

`colorOverride` names a field that holds a CSS color for each row, like a status color. It sets the bar fill directly instead of going through the color scale. A `Legend` still uses the color scale, so if you show one, set `color` to the matching category field and pass the same colors to `Chart` `colors`.

```ts
const barGoalData = [
  { channel: 'Search', visits: 12400, status: 'Met goal', statusColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Direct', visits: 9800, status: 'Met goal', statusColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Social', visits: 7300, status: 'Missed goal', statusColor: '#d7373f' },
  { channel: 'Email', visits: 5100, status: 'Met goal', statusColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Referral', visits: 3600, status: 'Missed goal', statusColor: '#d7373f' },
  { channel: 'Display', visits: 2200, status: 'Missed goal', statusColor: '#d7373f' },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barGoalData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" colorOverride="statusColor" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `colorOverride` on `Bar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Diverging

For values that go both above and below zero, like a percent change, set `diverging`. The category axis moves to the zero line, and each label sits on the opposite side from its bar so labels never cover bars. Use `colorOverride` to color increases and decreases differently.

```ts
const barChangeData = [
  { channel: 'Search', change: 0.12, changeColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Direct', change: 0.05, changeColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Social', change: -0.08, changeColor: '#d7373f' },
```
