```ts
  { channel: 'Email', change: 0.03, changeColor: '#0d7a55' },
  { channel: 'Referral', change: -0.11, changeColor: '#d7373f' },
  { channel: 'Display', change: -0.02, changeColor: '#d7373f' },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChangeData}>
  <Axis position="left" baseline />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Change" labelFormat="percentage" />
  <Bar
    dimension="channel"
    metric="change"
    colorOverride="changeColor"
    diverging
    orientation="horizontal"
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `diverging` on `Bar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `horizontal`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `diverging` only works on a single-series bar: no `color`, `lineType`, or `opacity` field and not `type="dodged"`. It has no effect on trellised bars or when the axis has `subLabels`.

## Dual metric axis

When two series have very different scales, like sessions and orders, set `dualMetricAxis` to scale the last series on its own axis. Add an `Axis` with `position="right"` for it. The right axis title and labels take the last series' color. The left axis takes the first series' color when only one series is on it.

```ts
const barSessionsOrdersData = [
  { channel: 'Search', series: 'Sessions', value: 12400 },
  { channel: 'Direct', series: 'Sessions', value: 9800 },
  { channel: 'Social', series: 'Sessions', value: 7300 },
  { channel: 'Email', series: 'Sessions', value: 5100 },
  { channel: 'Referral', series: 'Sessions', value: 3600 },
  { channel: 'Search', series: 'Orders', value: 310 },
  { channel: 'Direct', series: 'Orders', value: 420 },
  { channel: 'Social', series: 'Orders', value: 95 },
  { channel: 'Email', series: 'Orders', value: 260 },
  { channel: 'Referral', series: 'Orders', value: 120 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barSessionsOrdersData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Sessions" />
  <Axis position="right" title="Orders" />
  <Bar
    dimension="channel"
    metric="value"
    color="series"
    type="dodged"
    dualMetricAxis
  >
    <ChartInspect />
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `dualMetricAxis` on `Bar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

`dualMetricAxis` only applies when `type="dodged"`, `color` is a single field, and there's no `trellis`.

## Trellis

`trellis` names a field to split the chart into small multiples, one per value. Each panel shares the same scales, so panels are easy to compare.

-   `trellisOrientation="horizontal"` (default) lays panels out in a row; `vertical` stacks them in a column.
-   `trellisPadding` is the space between panels as a ratio, `0.2` by default.

```ts
const barRegionData = [
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Search', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3400 },
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Search', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2600 },
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2800 },
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Mobile', visits: 1900 },
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Social', device: 'Desktop', visits: 900 },
  { region: 'Americas', channel: 'Social', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2300 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Search', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2500 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Search', device: 'Mobile', visits: 1800 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Desktop', visits: 1700 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Direct', device: 'Mobile', visits: 1200 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Social', device: 'Desktop', visits: 700 },
  { region: 'EMEA', channel: 'Social', device: 'Mobile', visits: 1600 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barRegionData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" trellis="region" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `trellisOrientation` on `Bar`: `horizontal` or `vertical`. Shown: `horizontal`.
-   `trellisPadding` on `Bar`: 0 to 0.6, in steps of 0.05. Shown: `0.2`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.
-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.

Trellised charts don't draw grid lines on the shared value axis.

## BarDirectLabel

Add `BarDirectLabel` as a child of `Bar` to print each bar's value on or next to it.

-   `position` places the label: `end-outside` (default) outside the tip, `end` inside near the tip, `middle` centered in the bar, or `start` inside near the baseline.
-   `overflow` sets what happens to an inside label that doesn't fit in its bar: `hide` it, or `spill` it outside the tip. The default is `spill` for `start` and `hide` otherwise.
-   `dataKey` labels only the rows where that field is truthy, for example to call out one bar.
-   `format` formats the value. It accepts `shortNumber`, `standardNumber`, `currency`, `shortCurrency`, `percentage`, or a [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier. The default is `,.2~f`.

Labels outside the bar use the bar's color; labels inside use the background color. Labels outside the bar are hidden if they would overlap a bar or another label. For negative values, labels flip to the other side of the baseline. Numbers follow the chart's `locale`, like axis labels do.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  BarDirectLabel,
  Chart,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits">
    <BarDirectLabel />
  </Bar>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `BarDirectLabel`: `end-outside`, `end`, `middle` or `start`. Shown: `end-outside`.
-   `format` on `BarDirectLabel`: `,.2~f`, `.3~s` or `,.1f`. Shown: `,.2~f`.
-   `overflow` on `BarDirectLabel`: `default`, `hide` or `spill`. Shown: `default`.
-   `dataKey` on `BarDirectLabel`: `none` or `callout`. Shown: `none`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

## Axis and ReferenceLine

Bars need two `Axis` children on `Chart`: one for the categories and one for the values. Typical settings are `baseline` on the category axis and `grid` on the value axis. Hovering a category label on an interactive bar highlights that category.

To mark a target or threshold, add a `ReferenceLine` as a child of the value `Axis`. For more axis options, see [Axis](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis).

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ReferenceLine,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits">
    <ReferenceLine value={8000} label="Goal" />
  </Axis>
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `value` on `ReferenceLine`: `5000`, `8000` or `10000`. Shown: `8000`.
-   `label` on `ReferenceLine`: any text. Shown: `Goal`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Bar` to list the series. The plot shrinks to make room for it.

-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its series. Stacks and value scales update to fit what's visible.
-   `highlight` highlights a series while its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend title="Device" isToggleable />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `right`, `left` or `top`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

See [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend) for more options.

### Hiding series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. To start with series hidden but let users toggle them, set `defaultHiddenSeries` on a toggleable `Legend` instead.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData} hiddenSeries={['Mobile']}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Mobile` or `Mobile, Tablet`. Shown: `Mobile`.
-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Pass a function as children that takes the bar's data row and returns the content; without children, neither shows anything, although the bar still responds to the pointer. `rightClick` on `ChartPopover` opens it on right-click instead. The bar with an open popover gets a selection ring.

-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect` sets what stays highlighted while the pointer is over a bar: `item` (default) for the bar, `series` for every bar in its series, or `dimension` for every bar in its category.
-   `targets={['dimensionArea', 'item']}` also shows the inspect when the pointer is in the empty space of a category's column.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Button,
  ButtonGroup,
  Content,
  Heading,
  Text,
} from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.channel}, {datum.device}: {datum.visits} visits
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover>
      {(datum, close) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.channel}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.device}: {datum.visits} visits</Text>
          </Content>
          <ButtonGroup UNSAFE_style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>
            <Button variant="secondary" size="S" onPress={close}>Close</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series` or `dimension`. Shown: `item`.
-   `targets` on `ChartInspect`: `item` or `dimensionArea, item`. Shown: `item`.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.

Hovering an interactive bar fades the other bars. A bar without `ChartInspect`, `ChartPopover`, `onClick`, `onContextMenu`, or highlighting doesn't respond to the pointer. See [Interaction](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction) for more about inspects and popovers.

### Callbacks

`Bar` calls `onClick` with the bar's data row when a bar is clicked, and `onMouseOver` and `onMouseOut` when the pointer enters and leaves a bar. `onContextMenu` is called on right-click with the native event and the row, so you can show your own menu.

```tsx
<Bar
  dimension="channel"
  metric="visits"
  onClick={(datum) => openReport(datum.channel)}
  onContextMenu={(event, datum) => showMenu(event.clientX, event.clientY, datum)}
/>
```

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row. `highlightedItem` does the same by row ID and can take a list; set `idKey` on `Chart` to the field that uniquely identifies each row. `Legend` with `highlight` highlights a series when its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Bar>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Desktop`, `Mobile` or `Tablet`. Shown: `none`.
-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none`, `social-mobile` or `search-desktop, email-desktop`. Shown: `none`.

## Animation

The chart's `animationTypes` lists which animations play. By default, `hover` eases bars in and out of their faded state, and `drawIn` grows bars from the baseline over 700ms. Stacked segments fill in order from the baseline outward, and direct labels fade in as their own segment finishes.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.
-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.

Draw-in plays once when the chart mounts. Set `animationTypes={['hover']}` to turn off draw-in only, or `animations={false}` to turn off all animation. When the user prefers reduced motion, draw-in is skipped. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).

## Not supported yet

> **Note:**
> 
> `Bar` doesn't take `BarAnnotation` or `Trendline` children yet. Use `BarDirectLabel` for value labels.

## API

### Bar

`name` identifies the bar's marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `bar0`, `bar1`, and so on. `metricAxis` gives the bar its own value scale, for combining it with other marks; see [Combo](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/combo).

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `BarAnnotation \| BarDirectLabel \| ChartPopover \| ChartInspect` | – |
| `color` — Bar color or key in the data that is used as the color facet; a two-key list dodges by the first key and stacks by the second. | `ColorFacet \| DualFacet` | `{ value: 'categorical-100' }` |
| `colorOverride` — Data field whose value is the CSS color for each bar; overrides the color scale for the bar fill. | `string` | – |
| `dimension` — Data field used for the bar categories (x-axis for a vertical bar). | `string` | `'category'` |
| `dimensionDataType` — Set to `time` when the dimension values are dates, so the axis can format them with `labelFormat="time"`. | `string` | – |
| `diverging` — Diverging bar chart (metric spans positive and negative): moves the dimension axis to the zero baseline and flips each label to the opposite side of its bar. Single-series bars only; a no-op on dodged or faceted bars. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `dualMetricAxis` — Whether to scale the last series separately on a secondary metric axis. Only applies to dodged bars with a single facet key and no trellis. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `groupedPadding` — Inner padding between dodged bars in a group, as a ratio between 0 and 1. | `number` | `'paddingRatio'` |
| `hasSquareCorners` — Whether the corners at the end of each bar are square instead of rounded. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `lineType` — Border line type or key in the data that is used as the line type facet. Only visible when `lineWidth` is greater than 0. | `DualFacet \| LineTypeFacet` | `{ value: 'solid' }` |
| `lineWidth` — Border width of the bar, drawn in the bar's color. | `LineWidth` | `0` |
| `metric` — Key in the data that is used as the metric. | `string` | `'value'` |
| `metricAxis` — Axis that the metric is trended against (y-axis for a vertical bar) | `string` | – |
| `name` — Name used for the bar's marks and signals in the Vega spec. Defaults to `bar0`, `bar1`, and so on. | `string` | – |
| `onClick` — Called with the row's data when a bar is clicked. | `MarkCallback` | – |
| `onContextMenu` — Called with the event and the row's data when a bar is right-clicked. Use it to show a custom context menu. | `ContextMenuCallback` | – |
| `onMouseOut` — Called with the row's data when the pointer leaves a bar. | `MarkCallback` | – |
| `onMouseOver` — Called with the row's data when the pointer enters a bar. | `MarkCallback` | – |
| `opacity` — Bar opacity, or a data field that assigns an opacity to each series. | `DualFacet \| OpacityFacet` | `{ value: 1 }` |
| `order` — Data field that sets the stack order; higher values stack on top. Defaults to data order. | `string` | – |
| `orientation` — Direction of the bars. | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `'vertical'` |
| `paddingOuter` — Space before the first bar and after the last, as a share of each category's width. Defaults to half of `paddingRatio`. | `number` | – |
| `paddingRatio` — Space between bars, as a share of each category's width from 0 to 1. | `number` | `0.4` |
| `trellis` — Data field that splits the chart into small multiples, one per value. | `string` | – |
| `trellisOrientation` — Whether trellis groups sit side by side or stacked. Only applies with `trellis`. | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `'horizontal'` |
| `trellisPadding` — Space between trellis groups, from 0 to 1. Only applies with `trellis`. | `number` | `0.2` |
| `trendlines` | `TrendlineOptions[]` | – |
| `type` — Whether series stack on top of each other or sit side by side (dodged). | `"dodged" \| "stacked"` | `'stacked'` |

### BarDirectLabel

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataKey` — Data key that selects which bars get a label; only rows where this field is truthy are labeled. | `string` | – |
| `format` — Number format for the label value — a named preset or custom d3-format specifier. | `string` | `'',.2~f''` |
| `overflow` — Inside positions: `hide` hides labels that don't fit inside the bar, `spill` moves them outside the bar tip. Outside labels are hidden if they would overlap a bar or another label. | `"hide" \| "spill"` | ``''spill' for `start`, otherwise 'hide''`` |
| `position` — Where to place the label: outside the tip (`end-outside`), inside near the tip (`end`), centered (`middle`), or inside near the baseline (`start`). | `"start" \| "end" \| "middle" \| "end-outside"` | `''end-outside''` |

---

# Donut

**Stage:** Alpha

Donuts show how categories contribute to a whole. Each data point becomes a segment sized by its `metric` value.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
  Legend,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Title text="Visitors by browser" />
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
  <Legend title="Browsers" position="right" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `variant` on `Donut`: `circle` or `semicircle`. Shown: `circle`.
-   `holeRatio` on `Donut`: 0 to 0.95, in steps of 0.05. Shown: `0.85`.
-   `DonutSummary`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `none`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` or `top`. Shown: `right`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Visitors by browser`.

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per segment. On `Donut`, `metric` names the numeric field that sizes each segment (default `value`) and `color` names the field that identifies it in the legend, labels, and tooltips (default `series`). Most examples on this page use `browserData`:

```ts
const browserData = [
  { count: 10390, browser: 'Chrome' },
  { count: 8281, browser: 'Firefox' },
  { count: 7045, browser: 'Safari' },
  { count: 6166, browser: 'Opera' },
  { count: 4201, browser: 'Other' },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser" />
</Chart>
```

### Boolean data

For a single rate, like a success rate, pass exactly two points whose values sum to 1 and set `isBoolean`. `DonutSummary` then shows the first point as a percentage instead of the total.

```ts
const booleanData = [
  { id: 'Success', value: 0.68 },
  { id: 'Failure', value: 0.32 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={booleanData} colors={['green-800', 'gray-200']}>
  <Donut metric="value" color="id" isBoolean>
    <DonutSummary label="Success rate" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `label` on `DonutSummary`: any text. Shown: `Success rate`.
-   `hideValue` on `DonutSummary`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

### Zero, empty, and loading

When every value is 0, the donut draws an empty gray ring and `DonutSummary` shows 0. When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```ts
const zeroData = [
  { count: 0, browser: 'Chrome' },
  { count: 0, browser: 'Firefox' },
  { count: 0, browser: 'Safari' },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={zeroData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `all zeros`, `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `all zeros`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No browser data`.

With **state** set to `empty`:

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No browser data">
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData} loading>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

## Shape

### holeRatio

`holeRatio` is the inner radius as a fraction of the outer radius. The default is `0.85`; `0` renders a pie chart.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser" holeRatio={0} />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `holeRatio` on `Donut`: 0 to 0.95, in steps of 0.05. Shown: `0`.

### Semicircle

`variant="semicircle"` draws the top half of the circle, from 9 o'clock to 3 o'clock. Full circles start at 12 o'clock.

Both variants sort segments largest-first by default. For ordered categories like survey responses, set `sortOrder="data"` to keep the source order. Boolean donuts always use the source order.

```ts
const surveyData = [
  { response: 'Strongly agree', count: 18 },
  { response: 'Agree', count: 32 },
  { response: 'Neutral', count: 24 },
  { response: 'Disagree', count: 16 },
  { response: 'Strongly disagree', count: 10 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={surveyData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="response" variant="semicircle" sortOrder="data">
    <DonutSummary label="Responses" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `sortOrder` on `Donut`: `data` or `valueDescending`. Shown: `data`.

> **Note:**
> 
> Semicircles don't support `SegmentLabel`.

### Size

`Chart` fills the width of its container and is 300px tall by default. The donut grows to fit the smaller of the two, so a semicircle in a wide container can be much larger than a full circle at the same height. Use `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, and `maxWidth` on `Chart` to constrain it. Ring width and `DonutSummary` text change with the donut's size; see [Responsive](#responsive).

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData} width={400} height={300}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `width` on `Chart`: 120 to 520, in steps of 10. Shown: `400`.
-   `height` on `Chart`: 80 to 400, in steps of 10. Shown: `300`.
-   `variant` on `Donut`: `circle` or `semicircle`. Shown: `circle`.

## DonutSummary

`DonutSummary` shows a label and the sum of all segments in the center of the donut.

-   `numberFormat` formats the value. It accepts `shortNumber`, `standardNumber`, or a [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier.
-   `delta` adds a change below the label, green when zero or positive and red when negative (`0.025` shows as `+2.5%`).
-   `hideValue` shows only the label.

Numbers follow the chart's `locale`, which also applies to segment labels, `ChartInspect`, and `ChartPopover`.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `label` on `DonutSummary`: any text. Shown: `Visitors`.
-   `numberFormat` on `DonutSummary`: `shortNumber`, `standardNumber` or `,.2f`. Shown: `shortNumber`.
-   `delta` on `DonutSummary`: `none`, `0.025` or `-0.04`. Shown: `none`.
-   `hideValue` on `DonutSummary`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

## SegmentLabel

`SegmentLabel` labels each segment with its name and value.

-   `value` and `percent` choose what follows the name; format them with `valueFormat` and `percentFormat`.
-   `swatch` adds the segment color before the name.
-   `showValueRow` adds a smaller row below with the segment's value, and `showTotal` adds the total to that row, like `10,390 / 36,083`.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  SegmentLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <SegmentLabel />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `value` on `SegmentLabel`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `percent` on `SegmentLabel`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `swatch` on `SegmentLabel`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `showValueRow` on `SegmentLabel`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `showTotal` on `SegmentLabel`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `valueFormat` on `SegmentLabel`: `standardNumber`, `shortNumber` or `,.0f`. Shown: `standardNumber`.
-   `percentFormat` on `SegmentLabel`: `.0%` or `.1%`. Shown: `.0%`.

Labels sit at the middle of each segment. A label is hidden when it would overlap a label for a larger segment or when its segment is narrower than about 17°. Hovering a segment always shows its label and hides any labels that overlap it.

### labelKey

Labels show the `color` field by default. To show different text, such as a longer display name, set `labelKey` to another field in the data.

```ts
const browserLabelData = [
  { count: 10390, browser: 'Chrome', label: 'Chrome' },
  { count: 8281, browser: 'Firefox', label: 'Mozilla Firefox' },
  { count: 7045, browser: 'Safari', label: 'Apple Safari' },
  { count: 6166, browser: 'Opera', label: 'Opera' },
  { count: 4201, browser: 'Other', label: 'Other browsers' },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  SegmentLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserLabelData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <SegmentLabel labelKey="label" />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `labelKey` on `SegmentLabel`: `none` or `label`. Shown: `label`.

### Emphasized segments

`emphasizedItems` on `Donut` keeps the listed segments in color and grays out the rest. Add two `SegmentLabel` children with `labelMode="emphasized"` and `labelMode="deemphasized"` to label each group differently, or set `hideDeemphasizedLabels` to label only the emphasized segments.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  SegmentLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser" emphasizedItems={['Chrome']}>
    <SegmentLabel labelMode="emphasized" percent value={false} showValueRow />
    <SegmentLabel labelMode="deemphasized" value />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `emphasizedItems` on `Donut`: `Chrome`, `Chrome, Firefox` or `Safari, Opera`. Shown: `Chrome`.
-   `hideDeemphasizedLabels` on `Donut`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Responsive

The Spectrum 2 donut comes in five sizes: XS, S, M, L, and XL. You don't pick a size directly. The chart picks it from the space you give it, and updates it as the chart resizes. Each size changes the ring thickness, the gap between segments, the text sizes, and how much label detail is shown.

The example is this chart in a resizable container. Change `width` and `height` to see each size, and remove `SegmentLabel` to see the sizes without segment labels.

```ts
const browserLongTailData = [
  { count: 10390, browser: 'Chrome' },
  { count: 8281, browser: 'Firefox' },
  { count: 7045, browser: 'Safari' },
  { count: 6166, browser: 'Opera' },
  { count: 4201, browser: 'Other' },
  { count: 3261, browser: 'Brave' },
  { count: 1021, browser: 'Unknown' },
];
```

```jsx
import { Chart, Donut, DonutSummary, SegmentLabel } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserLongTailData} width={472} height={472}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
    <SegmentLabel percent value={false} swatch showValueRow />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

### How size affects the donut

The size is set by the chart's shorter side. To show a donut at a given size, make the chart at least this tall and this wide:

| Size | Donut diameter | Chart size without segment labels | Chart size with segment labels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XS | Under 120px | Under 140px | Under 206px |
| S | 120–200px | 140px | 206px |
| M | 200–280px | 220px | 344px |
| L | 280–400px | 300px | 472px |
| XL | 400px and up | 420px | 674px |

-   Without segment labels, the donut has 10px of padding on every side.
-   With segment labels, the donut leaves room on each side for its labels: the size's label gap (see [Segment labels](#segment-labels)) plus 30% of the donut's diameter. The donut stops growing once it reaches the next size's diameter, and stays there until the chart is large enough to switch sizes. Room is reserved even at XS, where labels are hidden.
-   A semicircle only needs half the height, because it's half as tall as a full donut. A semicircle that's 300px wide and 150px tall is size L.
-   Semicircles and boolean donuts don't show segment labels, so they always use the sizes without labels.

### Ring

| Size | Ring thickness | Gap between segments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XS | 16px | 1px |
| S | 18px | 2px |
| M | 20px | 2px |
| L | 22px | 2px |
| XL | 40px | 2px |

-   These ring thicknesses apply at the default `holeRatio` of `0.85`. With another `holeRatio`, the ring stays proportional to the donut instead.
-   Pies (`holeRatio={0}`) always use a 1px gap.

### DonutSummary

| Size | Value (extra bold) | Label | Delta | Delta on a semicircle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XS | 18px | 12px | 12px | Hidden |
| S | 20px | 14px | 14px | Hidden |
| M | 22px | 16px | 16px | 16px |
| L | 36px | 20px | 20px | 20px |
| XL | 50px | 24px | 24px | 24px |

-   The summary is hidden when the hole is under 80px across. At the default `holeRatio`, that's a chart under 132px without segment labels, or under 194px with them.
-   Text that doesn't fit in the hole is truncated with an ellipsis.

### Segment labels

Labels appear at size S and show more detail as the donut grows.

| Size | Gap to ring | Name / value (default) | Name / value / value row (`swatch` or `showValueRow`) | Swatch | Value row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XS | — | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden |
| S | 5px | 9 / 12px | 10 / 13.5px | Hidden | Hidden |
| M | 10px | 10.5 / 14px | 12 / 15.75px | 16px | Hidden |
| L | 10px | 12 / 16px | 14 / 18 / 11px | 16px | Shown |
| XL | 15px | 15 / 20px | 16 / 22.5 / 13.75px | 16px | Shown |

-   **Default labels** show the name (regular) above the percent or value (bold), both gray-700.
-   **With `swatch` or `showValueRow`**, labels use larger text: the name (regular, gray-700), then 4px below it the percent or value (extra bold, gray-800). The swatch is a 16px rounded square, 8px from the name. The value row shows the segment's value (extra bold, gray-700), followed by the total (regular) with `showTotal`. If a label is too tall for the donut, the space between its lines shrinks but the text sizes don't.
-   When a segment is hovered, its label's percent or value takes the segment's color.
-   Segments smaller than about 17° of the ring aren't labeled until they're hovered.
-   Labels stay at least 4px apart. When labels would overlap, the hovered segment's label is kept first, then labels for larger segments.
-   Labels stay at least 10px from the chart's left and right edges, and are truncated with an ellipsis if needed.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Donut` to list the segments. The donut shrinks to make room for it.

-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its segment. The remaining segments fill the circle and `DonutSummary` updates its total.
-   `highlight` highlights a segment while its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
  <Legend title="Browsers" position="right" isToggleable />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `right`, `bottom`, `left` or `top`. Shown: `right`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

### Hiding segments

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides segments from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. The remaining segments fill the circle and `DonutSummary` totals only what's visible. To start with segments hidden but let users toggle them, set `defaultHiddenSeries` on a toggleable `Legend` instead.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  DonutSummary,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData} hiddenSeries={['Chrome']}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <DonutSummary label="Visitors" />
  </Donut>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Chrome` or `Chrome, Firefox`. Shown: `Chrome`.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Without children, both show the segment's color, name, share of the total, and value (for Chrome, `28.8% (10.4K)`), formatted with the chart's `locale`. Pass a function as children to render your own content.

`rightClick` on `ChartPopover` opens it on right-click instead of click.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Donut,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <ChartInspect />
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.browser}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.count.toLocaleString()} visitors</Text>
          </Content>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `children` on `ChartPopover`: `default` or `custom`. Shown: `custom`.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

Hovering an interactive segment fades the other segments and their labels. A donut without `ChartInspect`, `ChartPopover`, `SegmentLabel`, or a `Legend` with `highlight` doesn't respond to the pointer.

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a segment from outside the chart, for example from a table row. `highlightedItem` does the same by row ID and can take a list; set `idKey` on `Chart` to the field that uniquely identifies each row. `Legend` with `highlight` highlights a segment when its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Donut,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Donut>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Chrome`, `Firefox`, `Safari`, `Opera` or `Other`. Shown: `none`.
-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none`, `Safari` or `Chrome, Safari`. Shown: `none`.

## Animation

The chart's `animationTypes` lists which animations play. By default, `hover` eases segments in and out of their faded state on hover, and `drawIn` sweeps the segments in over 750ms when the chart mounts. Labels fade in as their segment finishes; `DonutSummary` stays visible throughout.

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Donut,
  SegmentLabel,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser">
    <ChartInspect />
    <SegmentLabel value />
  </Donut>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `variant` on `Donut`: `circle` or `semicircle`. Shown: `circle`.
-   `SegmentLabel`: included or left out. Shown: included.

Draw-in plays once when the chart mounts; re-renders, data updates, and resizing don't replay it. Set `animationTypes={['hover']}` to turn off draw-in only, or `animations={false}` to turn off all animation. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).

## API

### Donut

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `ChartPopover \| ChartInspect \| DonutSummary \| SegmentLabel` | – |
| `color` — Key in the data that is used as the color facet | `string` | `'series'` |
| `emphasizedItems` — Designates which segments (by their `color` facet value) render with full categorical color. Remaining segments render as a solid color swap to gray at full opacity. Their labels stay fully visible and normally colored, unlike Line's `primarySeries` which suppresses non-primary direct labels entirely. | `(string \| number)[]` | – |
| `hideDeemphasizedLabels` — Hides labels for segments not in `emphasizedItems`. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `holeRatio` — Inner radius as a share of the outer radius. `0` draws a pie. | `number` | `0.85` |
| `isBoolean` — Shows the first row's value as a percent in the center. Use with two rows whose values sum to 1. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `metric` — Key in the data that is used as the metric | `string` | `'value'` |
| `name` — Sets the name of the component. | `string` | – |
| `sortOrder` — Categorical segment ordering. Use `data` to preserve source order; boolean donuts always preserve source order. | `"data" \| "valueDescending"` | `'valueDescending'` |
| `variant` — Renders a top-half arc instead of a full circle. Data is automatically sorted descending by `metric` so the largest segment always renders leftmost. `segmentLabels` are not supported and are silently omitted when set to `'semicircle'`. | `"circle" \| "semicircle"` | `'circle'` |

### DonutSummary

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delta` — Sentiment-colored delta (e.g. 0.025 renders as "+2.5%") shown below the label; hidden at XS/S for semicircles. | `number` | – |
| `hideValue` — Hides the value portion of the donut summary, only showing the label | `boolean` | `false` |
| `label` — Label for the metric summary | `string` | – |
| `numberFormat` — d3 number format specifier. Sets the number format for the summary value. see {@link https://d3js.org/d3-format#locale\_format} | `string` | `'shortNumber'` |

### SegmentLabel

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `labelKey` — Data field with the segment label text. Defaults to the `Donut` `color` field. | `string` | – |
| `labelMode` — Selects whether the label applies to emphasized or de-emphasized segments. | `"emphasized" \| "deemphasized"` | – |
| `percent` — Shows the donut segment percentage | `boolean` | `false` |
| `percentFormat` — d3 format specifier for the percentage value displayed when `percent` is true. | `string` | `'.0%'` |
| `showTotal` — Appends the total value to the segment value row | `boolean` | `false` |
| `showValueRow` — Shows an additional segment value row below the label | `boolean` | `false` |
| `swatch` — Shows a color swatch before the segment label | `boolean` | `false` |
| `value` — Shows the donut segment metric value | `boolean` | `true` |
| `valueFormat` — d3 number format specifier. Sets the number format for the segment metric value. | `string` | `'standardNumber'` |

---

# Area

**Stage:** Lab

Areas show how a value changes across a continuous dimension, usually time. With one `metric`, each series is stacked on the series below it, so the top edge shows the total. With `metricStart` and `metricEnd`, each series fills the range between two values instead.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Title text="Sessions by channel" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.channel}: {datum.sessions} sessions
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Area>
  <Legend title="Channel" position="bottom" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `opacity` on `Area`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.8`.
-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `none`, `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Sessions by channel`.

`Area` is a lab component. Import it from the `lab` subpath:

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per point. On `Area`:

-   `dimension` names the field for the x position (default `datetime`).
-   `metric` names the numeric field for the y position (default `value`).
-   `color` names the field that splits the data into series (default `series`). Each series gets its own color and legend entry.

Most examples on this page use `channelSessionsData`, three channels over eight weeks:

```ts
const channelSessionsData = [
  { datetime: 1736164800000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4200, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1736769600000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4350, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1737374400000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4480, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1737979200000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4400, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1738584000000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4620, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1739188800000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4810, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1739793600000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4760, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1740398400000, channel: 'Organic search', sessions: 4950, stackOrder: 3 },
  { datetime: 1736164800000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 2600, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1736769600000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 2750, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1737374400000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 2900, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1737979200000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 3400, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1738584000000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 3650, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1739188800000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 3300, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1739793600000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 3100, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1740398400000, channel: 'Paid search', sessions: 2950, stackOrder: 2 },
  { datetime: 1736164800000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1200, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1736769600000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1850, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1737374400000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1150, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1737979200000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1250, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1738584000000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1900, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1739188800000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1180, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1739793600000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 1300, stackOrder: 1 },
  { datetime: 1740398400000, channel: 'Email', sessions: 2050, stackOrder: 1 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The default time scale reads the dimension as a date, so it can be a timestamp or a date string. Every series should have a point at every dimension value. Missing points aren't filled in, so series with different dimension values don't stack cleanly.

### Missing values

A stacked area treats a missing `metric` value as 0 and drops to the baseline. A floating area leaves a gap instead, so missing data isn't mistaken for a value.

```ts
const temperatureGapData = [
  { datetime: 1740830400000, low: 41, high: 52 },
  { datetime: 1740916800000, low: 43, high: 55 },
  { datetime: 1741003200000, low: undefined, high: undefined },
  { datetime: 1741089600000, low: 42, high: 53 },
  { datetime: 1741176000000, low: 40, high: 50 },
  { datetime: 1741262400000, low: undefined, high: undefined },
  { datetime: 1741348800000, low: 42, high: 56 },
  { datetime: 1741435200000, low: 44, high: 58 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={temperatureGapData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline />
  <Area metric="high" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `metricStart` on `Area`: `metric` or `metricStart, metricEnd`. Shown: `metric`.

### Empty and loading

When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No sessions in this range">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No sessions in this range`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData} loading>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
</Chart>
```

## Stacking

With `metric`, series stack in data order: the first series sits on the baseline and each following series sits on top of the one before. The y axis always starts at 0. Negative values stack downward from 0, separately from positive values.

### order

To stack in a different order, set `order` to a numeric field. Series with higher values stack on top. In `channelSessionsData`, `stackOrder` puts Organic search on top and Email on the baseline.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" order="stackOrder" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `order` on `Area`: `none` or `stackOrder`. Shown: `stackOrder`.

### opacity

`opacity` sets the fill opacity, from 0 to 1. The default is `0.8`. Stacked series don't overlap, so lower opacity only lightens them; it matters most for floating areas.

## Floating areas

Set `metricStart` and `metricEnd` instead of `metric` to fill between two fields, such as a daily low and high. Each series starts at its own `metricStart` value, so floating areas don't stack and can overlap. Use a lower `opacity` so overlapping series stay visible.

```ts
const temperatureData = [
  { datetime: 1740830400000, city: 'Seattle', low: 41, high: 52 },
  { datetime: 1740916800000, city: 'Seattle', low: 43, high: 55 },
  { datetime: 1741003200000, city: 'Seattle', low: 44, high: 57 },
  { datetime: 1741089600000, city: 'Seattle', low: 42, high: 53 },
  { datetime: 1741176000000, city: 'Seattle', low: 40, high: 50 },
  { datetime: 1741262400000, city: 'Seattle', low: 39, high: 51 },
  { datetime: 1741348800000, city: 'Seattle', low: 42, high: 56 },
  { datetime: 1740830400000, city: 'Denver', low: 28, high: 54 },
  { datetime: 1740916800000, city: 'Denver', low: 31, high: 60 },
  { datetime: 1741003200000, city: 'Denver', low: 35, high: 64 },
  { datetime: 1741089600000, city: 'Denver', low: 30, high: 49 },
  { datetime: 1741176000000, city: 'Denver', low: 24, high: 41 },
  { datetime: 1741262400000, city: 'Denver', low: 27, high: 52 },
  { datetime: 1741348800000, city: 'Denver', low: 33, high: 61 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={temperatureData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Temperature (°F)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline />
  <Area metricStart="low" metricEnd="high" color="city" opacity={0.5}>
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.city}: {datum.low}° to {datum.high}°
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Area>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `opacity` on `Area`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.5`.

`metricStart` and `metricEnd` must be set together. If only one is set, `Area` logs an error and falls back to `metric`.

### With a line

A floating area behind a [`Line`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line) shows a range around a value, like a forecast with its confidence band. Put `Area` before `Line` so the line draws on top.

```ts
const forecastData = [
  { datetime: 1736164800000, visits: 8000, low: 7040, high: 8960 },
  { datetime: 1736769600000, visits: 8950, low: 7880, high: 10020 },
  { datetime: 1737374400000, visits: 8530, low: 7510, high: 9550 },
  { datetime: 1737979200000, visits: 9050, low: 7960, high: 10140 },
  { datetime: 1738584000000, visits: 10170, low: 8950, high: 11390 },
  { datetime: 1739188800000, visits: 9290, low: 8180, high: 10400 },
  { datetime: 1739793600000, visits: 9160, low: 8060, high: 10260 },
  { datetime: 1740398400000, visits: 9950, low: 8760, high: 11140 },
  { datetime: 1741003200000, visits: 9420, low: 8290, high: 10550 },
  { datetime: 1741608000000, visits: 9630, low: 8470, high: 10790 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={forecastData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metricStart="low" metricEnd="high" opacity={0.3} />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `opacity` on `Area`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.3`.
-   `Line`: included or left out. Shown: included.

## Scale types

`scaleType` sets how `dimension` values map to the x axis:

-   `time` (default): dates and timestamps, spaced by time. Use `labelFormat="time"` on the bottom `Axis`.
-   `linear`: numbers, spaced by value.
-   `point`: categories, spaced evenly in data order.

```ts
const installsData = [
  { day: 1, platform: 'iOS', installs: 1200 },
  { day: 2, platform: 'iOS', installs: 1850 },
  { day: 3, platform: 'iOS', installs: 2300 },
  { day: 7, platform: 'iOS', installs: 3100 },
  { day: 14, platform: 'iOS', installs: 3900 },
  { day: 30, platform: 'iOS', installs: 4600 },
  { day: 1, platform: 'Android', installs: 900 },
  { day: 2, platform: 'Android', installs: 1500 },
  { day: 3, platform: 'Android', installs: 2100 },
  { day: 7, platform: 'Android', installs: 2900 },
  { day: 14, platform: 'Android', installs: 3500 },
  { day: 30, platform: 'Android', installs: 4300 },
];
```

```ts
const weekdayVisitsData = [
  { day: 'Mon', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5200 },
  { day: 'Tue', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5600 },
  { day: 'Wed', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5400 },
  { day: 'Thu', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5800 },
  { day: 'Fri', device: 'Desktop', visits: 5100 },
  { day: 'Sat', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2300 },
  { day: 'Sun', device: 'Desktop', visits: 2100 },
  { day: 'Mon', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3100 },
  { day: 'Tue', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3300 },
  { day: 'Wed', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3200 },
  { day: 'Thu', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3500 },
  { day: 'Fri', device: 'Mobile', visits: 3900 },
  { day: 'Sat', device: 'Mobile', visits: 4800 },
  { day: 'Sun', device: 'Mobile', visits: 4600 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `scaleType` on `Area`: `time`, `linear` or `point`. Shown: `time`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `scaleType="band"` isn't supported for areas yet and draws a broken chart. Use `point` for categories.

### padding

`padding` adds space between the plot edges and the first and last points. Its unit depends on `scaleType`:

-   `point`: a ratio of the step between points, from 0 to 1. The default is `0.5`.
-   `time` and `linear`: pixels. The default is `0`, so the area touches both edges.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={weekdayVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Area dimension="day" metric="visits" color="device" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `scaleType` on `Area`: `time` or `point`. Shown: `point`.
-   `padding` on `Area`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.5`.
-   `padding` on `Area`: 0 to 48, in steps of 4. Shown: `0`.

## Axis

Add an `Axis` for each edge that needs labels. Use `labelFormat="time"` and `granularity` on the bottom axis for time data; `granularity` sets the tick interval and label format. On the left axis, `numberFormat` formats values and `grid` adds horizontal grid lines. Add a `ReferenceLine` as a child of `Axis` to mark a value, like a goal.

Axis labels follow the chart's `locale`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ReferenceLine,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Sessions">
    <ReferenceLine value={9000} label="Goal" />
  </Axis>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `granularity` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `day`, `week` or `month`. Shown: `week`.
-   `numberFormat` on `Axis` (Left axis): `shortNumber` or `standardNumber`. Shown: `shortNumber`.
-   `grid` on `Axis` (Left axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `title` on `Axis` (Left axis): any text. Shown: `Sessions`.
-   `ReferenceLine`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Area` to list the series.

-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its series. The remaining series restack to close the gap.
-   `highlight` highlights a series while its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
  <Legend title="Channel" position="bottom" isToggleable highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

### Hiding series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. The remaining series restack from the baseline. To start with series hidden but let users toggle them, set `defaultHiddenSeries` on a toggleable `Legend` instead.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData} hiddenSeries={['Organic search']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Organic search` or `Paid search, Email`. Shown: `Organic search`.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` as a child of `Area` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Both take a function as children that receives the hovered point and returns the content. Without children, they highlight the area but show no content.

Hovering follows the nearest dimension value: it adds a point on the top edge of the hovered series, draws a vertical rule, and fades the other series. `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect` changes what stays highlighted:

-   `item` (default): the hovered point, with a rule.
-   `series`: the whole hovered series, without a rule.
-   `dimension`: a point on every series at the hovered x value, with a rule.
-   A list of data keys: every series that matches the hovered point on those keys.

Clicking a series with `ChartPopover` outlines it and fades the others. `rightClick` opens the popover on right-click instead.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.channel}: {datum.sessions} sessions
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.channel}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.sessions.toLocaleString()} sessions</Text>
          </Content>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Area>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series` or `dimension`. Shown: `item`.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

`excludeDataKeys` on `ChartInspect` turns off hover details for rows with a truthy value in any of the listed fields. See [Interaction](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction) for more about `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover`.

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row, by fading the others. `Legend` with `highlight` does the same when its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={channelSessionsData} highlightedSeries="Paid search">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="sessions" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.channel}: {datum.sessions} sessions
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Area>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Organic search`, `Paid search` or `Email`. Shown: `Paid search`.

`highlightedItem` highlights a single point by row ID. Set `idKey` on `Chart` to the field that uniquely identifies each row. Hovering the chart replaces the controlled highlight.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Area } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={forecastData} idKey="datetime" highlightedItem={1739188800000}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" granularity="week" baseline />
  <Area metric="visits">
    <ChartInspect />
  </Area>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none`, `Jan 13`, `Feb 10` or `Mar 10`. Shown: `Feb 10`.

## Animation

Areas don't animate yet. `animationTypes` and `animations` on `Chart` have no effect on `Area`.

## API

### Area

`name` identifies the area's marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `area0`, `area1`, and so on.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` children that add hover and click details. | `AreaChild` | – |
| `color` — Data field that splits the data into series, each with its own color. | `string` | `'series'` |
| `dimension` — Data field plotted along the x-axis. | `string` | `'datetime'` |
| `metric` — Data field for each series' value; series stack from zero. | `string` | `'value'` |
| `metricEnd` — Data field for the top edge of a floating area; requires `metricStart` and replaces `metric`. | `string` | – |
| `metricStart` — Data field for the bottom edge of a floating area; requires `metricEnd` and replaces `metric`. | `string` | – |
| `name` — Name used for the area's marks and signals in the Vega spec. Defaults to `area0`, `area1`, and so on. | `string` | – |
| `opacity` — Fill opacity of the areas, from 0 to 1. | `number` | `0.8` |
| `order` — Data field that sets the stack order; higher values stack on top. Defaults to data order. | `string` | – |
| `padding` — Space before the first and after the last x value: a ratio from 0 to 1 for `point` scales (default `0.5`), pixels for `time` and `linear` (default `0`). | `number` | – |
| `scaleType` — Scale for `dimension`: `time`, `linear`, or `point`. | `"linear" \| "time" \| "point" \| "band"` | `'time'` |

---

# Bullet

**Stage:** Lab

Bullets compare a metric against a target. Each data point becomes one bullet: a bar for the metric, a line for the target, and a label with the formatted value.

```jsx
import { Chart, Title } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Title text="Customer health" />
  <Bullet metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" track />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `direction` on `Bullet`: `column` or `row`. Shown: `column`.
-   `labelPosition` on `Bullet`: `top` or `side`. Shown: `top`.
-   `color` on `Bullet`: `blue-900`, `purple-900` or `green-900`. Shown: `blue-900`.
-   `showTargetValue` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `track` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Customer health`.

`Bullet` is a lab component. Import it from the `lab` subpath:

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per bullet. On `Bullet`, `metric` names the field for the bar (default `currentAmount`), `target` names the field for the target line (default `target`), and `dimension` names the field for each bullet's label (default `graphLabel`). Most examples on this page use `bulletScoreData`:

```ts
const bulletScoreData = [
  { kpi: 'Satisfaction', score: 82, goal: 90 },
  { kpi: 'Retention', score: 74, goal: 70 },
  { kpi: 'Task success', score: 58, goal: 75 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" />
</Chart>
```

All bullets in a chart share one scale, so their bars and targets can be compared directly. Use separate charts for metrics in different units.

### Empty and loading

When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No KPI data">
  <Bullet track metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No KPI data`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData} loading>
  <Bullet track metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" />
</Chart>
```

## Layout

`direction` stacks bullets in a `column` (the default) or places them side by side in a `row`.

In a column, `labelPosition="side"` moves each bullet's label to its left and its value to its right, so bullets take less height. Rows always show labels on top.

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet
    track
    metric="score"
    dimension="kpi"
    target="goal"
    labelPosition="side"
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `direction` on `Bullet`: `column` or `row`. Shown: `column`.
-   `labelPosition` on `Bullet`: `top` or `side`. Shown: `side`.

The examples on this page are 480px wide and exactly as tall as their bullets. Bullets keep a fixed height and spacing, so a taller `Chart` leaves empty space below them rather than stretching them.

## Target

`showTarget` draws the target line (on by default). `showTargetValue` adds the target value below the line, formatted like the metric value. A data point without a target has no target line, and its target value reads "No Target".

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet track metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" showTargetValue />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `showTarget` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `showTargetValue` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Scale

The scale always starts at 0. `scaleType` sets its maximum:

-   `normal` (default) fits the data: the largest metric or 105% of the largest target.
-   `fixed` uses `maxScaleValue`. Bars and targets beyond it stop at the end of the scale.
-   `flexible` uses `maxScaleValue` until the data needs more room, then fits the data.

`maxScaleValue` defaults to `100`, which suits percentages and scores. `metricAxis` adds a value axis below the bullets.

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet
    track
    metric="score"
    dimension="kpi"
    target="goal"
    scaleType="fixed"
    metricAxis
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `scaleType` on `Bullet`: `normal`, `fixed` or `flexible`. Shown: `fixed`.
-   `maxScaleValue` on `Bullet`: 50 to 150, in steps of 10. Shown: `100`.
-   `metricAxis` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `metricAxis` only applies to column bullets and isn't shown with `showTargetValue`. Bullets draw their own labels and axis; they don't use `Axis` or `Legend`.

## Thresholds and track

`thresholds` draws background bands behind each bar, such as red, orange, and green performance zones. Each band takes a `fill` CSS color and optional `thresholdMin` and `thresholdMax`; an omitted bound extends the band to the edge of the scale. Bands are drawn at 20% opacity.

```ts
const bulletScoreThresholds = [
  { thresholdMax: 60, fill: 'rgb(234, 56, 41)' },
  { thresholdMin: 60, thresholdMax: 80, fill: 'rgb(249, 137, 23)' },
  { thresholdMin: 80, fill: 'rgb(21, 164, 110)' },
];
```

-   `thresholdBarColor` colors each bar with the full-strength `fill` of the band its value falls in. Values below the first band keep `color`.
-   `track` draws a plain gray track behind each bar instead. It's ignored when `thresholds` is set.

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet
    metric="score"
    dimension="kpi"
    target="goal"
    thresholds={bulletScoreThresholds}
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `thresholds` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `thresholdBarColor` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `track` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Color

`color` sets the bar color as a Spectrum color name, such as `purple-900`, or a CSS color. The default is `blue-900`. Target lines and labels are always gray.

## Labels and number format

### numberFormat

`numberFormat` formats the metric values, target values, and metric axis. It accepts `standardNumber` (default), `shortNumber`, `currency`, `shortCurrency`, or a [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier. Numbers follow the chart's `locale`.

```ts
const bulletRevenueData = [
  { region: 'Americas', revenue: 4215000, target: 4000000 },
  { region: 'EMEA', revenue: 2930000, target: 3500000 },
  { region: 'APAC', revenue: 1785000, target: 2200000 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletRevenueData}>
  <Bullet
    track
    metric="revenue"
    dimension="region"
    target="target"
    numberFormat="shortCurrency"
    showTargetValue
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `numberFormat` on `Bullet`: `standardNumber`, `shortNumber`, `shortCurrency`, `currency` or `$,.0f`. Shown: `shortCurrency`.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

### metricLabel and targetLabel

To show text you've already formatted, such as values with units, set `metricLabel` to a field holding the metric text and `targetLabel` to a field holding the target text. `targetLabel` only shows with `showTargetValue`.

```ts
const bulletStorageData = [
  { volume: 'Primary', used: 750, usedLabel: '750 GB', quota: 1000, quotaLabel: '1 TB' },
  { volume: 'Backups', used: 420, usedLabel: '420 GB', quota: 500, quotaLabel: '500 GB' },
  { volume: 'Archive', used: 1200, usedLabel: '1.2 TB', quota: 1500, quotaLabel: '1.5 TB' },
];
```

```jsx
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletStorageData}>
  <Bullet
    track
    metric="used"
    dimension="volume"
    target="quota"
    metricLabel="usedLabel"
    targetLabel="quotaLabel"
    showTargetValue
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `metricLabel` on `Bullet`: `none` or `usedLabel`. Shown: `usedLabel`.
-   `targetLabel` on `Bullet`: `none` or `quotaLabel`. Shown: `quotaLabel`.

## Title

Add [`Title`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title) as a sibling of `Bullet` to label the chart. The main example at the top of this page has one.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect

Add `ChartInspect` with a function as children to show details when a bullet is hovered. The function receives the bullet's data row. Hovering the bar or target line shows the details; with `thresholds` or `track`, hovering anywhere along the band does too.

```jsx
import { Chart, ChartInspect } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Bullet } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={bulletScoreData}>
  <Bullet metric="score" dimension="kpi" target="goal" track>
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.kpi}: {datum.score} (goal {datum.goal})
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Bullet>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `track` on `Bullet`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

> **Note:**
> 
> Bullets don't support `ChartPopover` or highlighting (`highlightedSeries`, `highlightedItem`) yet, and `ChartInspect` without children shows nothing.

## Animation

Bullets don't animate; `animationTypes` has no effect on them.

## API

### Bullet

`name` identifies the bullet's marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `bullet0`, `bullet1`, and so on.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — `ChartInspect` to show details when a bullet is hovered. | `ChartInspect` | – |
| `color` — Color of the metric bars, as a Spectrum color name or CSS color. | `string` | `'blue-900'` |
| `dimension` — Key in the data for each bullet's label. | `string` | `'graphLabel'` |
| `direction` — Stacks bullets in a `column` or places them side by side in a `row`. | `"row" \| "column"` | `'column'` |
| `labelPosition` — Shows each bullet's label and value above it (`top`) or on either side (`side`, column direction only). | `"top" \| "side"` | `'top'` |
| `maxScaleValue` — Scale maximum when `scaleType` is `fixed` or `flexible`; must be greater than zero. | `number` | `100` |
| `metric` — Key in the data for the metric bar's value. | `string` | `'currentAmount'` |
| `metricAxis` — Adds a value axis below the bullets in column direction; not shown with `showTargetValue`. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `metricLabel` — Key in the data for preformatted text shown instead of the formatted metric value. | `string` | – |
| `name` — Names the bullet's marks and signals in the Vega spec. Defaults to `bullet0`, `bullet1`, and so on. | `string` | `'bullet0'` |
| `numberFormat` — Format for values, target values, and the metric axis: `standardNumber`, `shortNumber`, `currency`, `shortCurrency`, or a d3-format specifier. | `string` | `''` |
