| `scaleType` — Sets the scale maximum from the data (`normal`), from `maxScaleValue` (`fixed`), or the larger of the two (`flexible`). | `"normal" \| "fixed" \| "flexible"` | `'normal'` |
| `showTarget` — Shows the target line. | `boolean` | `true` |
| `showTargetValue` — Shows the target value below the target line. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `target` — Key in the data for the target value. | `string` | `'target'` |
| `targetLabel` — Key in the data for preformatted text shown instead of the formatted target value when `showTargetValue` is set. | `string` | – |
| `thresholdBarColor` — Colors each metric bar with the `fill` of the threshold band its value falls in. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `thresholds` — Background bands `{ thresholdMin?, thresholdMax?, fill }`; an omitted bound extends to the edge of the scale and `fill` is a CSS color. | `ThresholdBackground[]` | – |
| `track` — Draws a gray track behind each metric bar; ignored when `thresholds` is set. | `boolean` | `false` |

---

# Combo

**Stage:** Lab

Combos draw bars and a line against the same x-axis, for example daily sessions as bars with the conversion rate as a line. `Combo` has no styling of its own. It renders its `Bar` and `Line` children the way they render on their own, so see [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar) and [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line) for their full props.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Line,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboTrafficData}>
  <Title text="Sessions and conversion" />
  <Axis position="left" title="Sessions" grid />
  <Axis
    position="right"
    name="rate"
    title="Conversion rate"
    numberFormat=".1%"
  />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `metricAxis` on `Line`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `scaleType` on `Line`: `point` or `time`. Shown: `point`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Sessions and conversion`.

`Combo` is a lab component. Import it from the `lab` subpath. `Bar` and `Line` come from the main package:

```tsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per x-axis value (or one per x-axis value and series). Each child reads its own `metric` from the same rows. Most examples on this page use `comboTrafficData`:

```ts
const comboTrafficData = [
  { datetime: 1772452800000, sessions: 4200, orders: 126, conversionRate: 0.03 },
  { datetime: 1772539200000, sessions: 4650, orders: 149, conversionRate: 0.032 },
  { datetime: 1772625600000, sessions: 5100, orders: 168, conversionRate: 0.033 },
  { datetime: 1772712000000, sessions: 4800, orders: 139, conversionRate: 0.029 },
  { datetime: 1772798400000, sessions: 5600, orders: 196, conversionRate: 0.035 },
  { datetime: 1772884800000, sessions: 3900, orders: 101, conversionRate: 0.026 },
  { datetime: 1772971200000, sessions: 3500, orders: 84, conversionRate: 0.024 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={comboTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line metric="conversionRate" metricAxis="rate" color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }} scaleType="point" />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

### dimension

`dimension` on `Combo` names the x-axis field for every child. The default is `datetime`. A child that sets its own `dimension` uses that instead, but children should share a field so their marks line up.

### Empty and loading

When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={emptyData} emptyStateText="No traffic data">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.
-   `emptyStateText` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `No traffic data`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboTrafficData} loading>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

## Axes

Bars always place each x value in a band, so the bottom axis shows one label per row. `labelFormat="time"` on that axis formats the timestamps as days, with the month as a sub-label.

By default, both children plot against the left axis. That works when the metrics are in the same units, like sessions and orders. When they aren't, set `metricAxis` on a child and add an `Axis` with a matching `name`, usually on the right. That child then gets its own scale and axis.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="secondary" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line
      metric="orders"
      metricAxis="secondary"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `metric` on `Line`: `orders` or `conversionRate`. Shown: `orders`.
-   `metricAxis` on `Line`: `none` or `secondary`. Shown: `secondary`.

> **Note:**
> 
> A child with `metricAxis` still counts toward the left axis's range. If the line's values are larger than the bars', the left axis grows to fit them and the bars get shorter.

Leave the left axis unnamed. It shows every child that doesn't set `metricAxis`.

## Bar and Line children

`Combo` accepts any number of `Bar` and `Line` children. Each child keeps its own props, including `metric`, `color`, `type`, `lineType`, `opacity`, and their own `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover`. Children are named `combo0Bar0`, `combo0Line0`, and so on unless you set `name` on them.

Set `scaleType="point"` on each `Line`. That puts each point in the center of its bar's band. The `Line` default, `time`, spreads points across the full width instead, so they don't line up with the bars.

To show a series per category, set the same `color` field on both children. Bars stack by default; set `type="dodged"` on `Bar` to place them side by side. Lines still pass through the center of each band, not the center of each dodged bar.

```ts
const comboDeviceData = [
  { datetime: 1772452800000, device: 'Desktop', sessions: 2400, conversionRate: 0.034 },
  { datetime: 1772452800000, device: 'Mobile', sessions: 1500, conversionRate: 0.021 },
  { datetime: 1772452800000, device: 'Tablet', sessions: 300, conversionRate: 0.028 },
  { datetime: 1772539200000, device: 'Desktop', sessions: 2550, conversionRate: 0.036 },
  { datetime: 1772539200000, device: 'Mobile', sessions: 1700, conversionRate: 0.022 },
  { datetime: 1772539200000, device: 'Tablet', sessions: 400, conversionRate: 0.027 },
  { datetime: 1772625600000, device: 'Desktop', sessions: 2700, conversionRate: 0.037 },
  { datetime: 1772625600000, device: 'Mobile', sessions: 1900, conversionRate: 0.024 },
  { datetime: 1772625600000, device: 'Tablet', sessions: 500, conversionRate: 0.03 },
  { datetime: 1772712000000, device: 'Desktop', sessions: 2600, conversionRate: 0.033 },
  { datetime: 1772712000000, device: 'Mobile', sessions: 1800, conversionRate: 0.02 },
  { datetime: 1772712000000, device: 'Tablet', sessions: 400, conversionRate: 0.026 },
  { datetime: 1772798400000, device: 'Desktop', sessions: 2900, conversionRate: 0.039 },
  { datetime: 1772798400000, device: 'Mobile', sessions: 2200, conversionRate: 0.026 },
  { datetime: 1772798400000, device: 'Tablet', sessions: 500, conversionRate: 0.031 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" color="device" type="stacked" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color="device"
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `type` on `Bar`: `stacked` or `dodged`. Shown: `stacked`.
-   `scaleType` on `Line`: `point` or `time`. Shown: `point`.

Both children use the `categorical-100` color by default. When neither uses a `color` field, give the line a different static color, like `color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}`, so it stands out from the bars.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Combo` to list series. Entries come from the `color` field, so a legend appears only when the children use one. Bars and line share an entry when they use the same `color` field.

-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show that series in both the bars and the line.
-   `highlight` highlights the series in both marks while its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" color="device" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color="device"
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
  <Legend position="bottom" isToggleable highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `right`, `left` or `top`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

### Hiding series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. It hides the matching bars and lines.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboDeviceData} hiddenSeries={['Desktop']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" color="device" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color="device"
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Desktop` or `Desktop, Tablet`. Shown: `Desktop`.

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row. The bars and line for other series fade.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboDeviceData} highlightedSeries="Mobile">
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" color="device" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color="device"
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Desktop`, `Mobile` or `Tablet`. Shown: `Mobile`.

> **Note:**
> 
> When the line has `ChartInspect` or `ChartPopover`, `highlightedSeries` and `Legend` `highlight` only highlight the bars. `highlightedItem` only highlights bars, and only works when both children have `ChartInspect` or `ChartPopover`. Otherwise the chart fails to render.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Each goes inside the child it describes, so bars and line can show different content. Pass a function as children to render your own content. `rightClick` on `ChartPopover` opens it on right-click instead of click.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={comboTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="left" title="Sessions" grid />
  <Axis
    position="right"
    name="rate"
    title="Conversion rate"
    numberFormat=".1%"
  />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions">
      <ChartInspect />
      <ChartPopover width="auto">
        {(datum) => (
          <>
            <Heading level={4}>Sessions</Heading>
            <Content>
              <Text>{datum.sessions.toLocaleString()}</Text>
            </Content>
          </>
        )}
      </ChartPopover>
    </Bar>
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    >
      <ChartInspect />
      <ChartPopover width="auto">
        {(datum) => (
          <>
            <Heading level={4}>Conversion rate</Heading>
            <Content>
              <Text>{(datum.conversionRate * 100).toFixed(1)}%</Text>
            </Content>
          </>
        )}
      </ChartPopover>
    </Line>
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `children` on `ChartPopover`: `default` or `custom`. Shown: `custom`.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

Hovering a bar fades the other bars.

> **Warning:**
> 
> Give both children the same interactivity. If only one child has `ChartInspect` or `ChartPopover`, the chart fails to render.

## Locale

The chart's `locale` formats axis numbers and dates, along with `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` content. Use `numberFormat` on each `Axis` to choose the format.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Combo } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={comboTrafficData} locale="de-DE">
  <Axis position="left" numberFormat="standardNumber" grid />
  <Axis position="right" name="rate" numberFormat=".1%" />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Combo>
    <Bar metric="sessions" />
    <Line
      metric="conversionRate"
      metricAxis="rate"
      color={{ value: 'categorical-200' }}
      scaleType="point"
    />
  </Combo>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `de-DE`.
-   `numberFormat` on `Axis`: `shortNumber` or `standardNumber`. Shown: `standardNumber`.

## Animation

The chart's `animationTypes` and `animations` apply to the bars and lines in a `Combo`. By default they draw in together, finishing at the same time, and bars and lines ease in and out of their faded state on hover. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).

## API

### Combo

`name` prefixes the names of the child marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `combo0`.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Bar and Line marks to draw against the shared dimension. | `ComboChild` | – |
| `dimension` — Data field for the x-axis, used by child marks that don't set their own `dimension`. | `string` | `'datetime'` |
| `name` — Prefix for child mark names, like `combo0Bar0`. | `string` | `'combo0'` |

For child props, see [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#api) and [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#api).

---

# Scatter

**Stage:** Lab

Scatter plots show how two numeric values relate. Each data point becomes a point positioned by its `dimension` (x) and `metric` (y) values. Color, size, opacity, and outline can each encode another field.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Title text="Campaign revenue by spend" />
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `color` on `Scatter`: `channel` or `static`. Shown: `channel`.
-   `size` on `Scatter`: `M` or `reach`. Shown: `M`.
-   `method` on `Trendline`: `none`, `linear` or `average`. Shown: `none`.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `none`, `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Campaign revenue by spend`.

`Scatter`, `ScatterAnnotation`, `ScatterPath`, `Trendline`, and `TrendlineAnnotation` are lab components. Import them from the `lab` subpath:

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter, Trendline } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

## Data

`data` goes on `Chart` as an array of objects, one per point. On `Scatter`, `dimension` names the field for the x position (default `x`) and `metric` names the field for the y position (default `value`). Most examples on this page use `scatterCampaignData`, one row per marketing campaign:

```ts
const scatterCampaignData = [
  { id: 1, campaign: 'Brand terms', channel: 'Search', audience: 'Returning', spend: 12, revenue: 58, reach: 40, roi: 4.8 },
  { id: 2, campaign: 'Competitor terms', channel: 'Search', audience: 'New', spend: 18, revenue: 61, reach: 55, roi: 3.4 },
  { id: 3, campaign: 'Product terms', channel: 'Search', audience: 'New', spend: 25, revenue: 96, reach: 72, roi: 3.8 },
  { id: 4, campaign: 'Shopping ads', channel: 'Search', audience: 'Returning', spend: 31, revenue: 118, reach: 90, roi: 3.8 },
  { id: 5, campaign: 'Generic terms', channel: 'Search', audience: 'New', spend: 40, revenue: 132, reach: 120, roi: 3.3 },
  { id: 6, campaign: 'Spring video', channel: 'Social', audience: 'New', spend: 8, revenue: 19, reach: 150, roi: 2.4 },
  { id: 7, campaign: 'Influencer kit', channel: 'Social', audience: 'New', spend: 15, revenue: 41, reach: 210, roi: 2.7 },
  { id: 8, campaign: 'Retargeting', channel: 'Social', audience: 'Returning', spend: 22, revenue: 74, reach: 60, roi: 3.4 },
  { id: 9, campaign: 'Carousel ads', channel: 'Social', audience: 'New', spend: 29, revenue: 70, reach: 180, roi: 2.4 },
  { id: 10, campaign: 'Holiday promo', channel: 'Social', audience: 'Returning', spend: 36, revenue: 103, reach: 95, roi: 2.9 },
  { id: 11, campaign: 'Welcome series', channel: 'Email', audience: 'New', spend: 4, revenue: 22, reach: 30, roi: 5.5 },
  { id: 12, campaign: 'Cart reminder', channel: 'Email', audience: 'Returning', spend: 6, revenue: 35, reach: 25, roi: 5.8 },
  { id: 13, campaign: 'Newsletter', channel: 'Email', audience: 'Returning', spend: 9, revenue: 38, reach: 80, roi: 4.2 },
  { id: 14, campaign: 'Win-back', channel: 'Email', audience: 'Returning', spend: 14, revenue: 47, reach: 45, roi: 3.4 },
  { id: 15, campaign: 'Launch announce', channel: 'Email', audience: 'New', spend: 19, revenue: 66, reach: 110, roi: 3.5 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

Add `Axis` siblings to label the x and y scales. Both scales are linear and fit the data, so they don't have to start at 0. Use `range` on `Axis` to fix a scale's domain.

### Time dimension

To plot points over time, put timestamps (milliseconds) in the `dimension` field and set `dimensionScaleType="time"`. Pair it with `labelFormat="time"` and a `granularity` on the bottom `Axis`. With the default `linear` scale, the axis shows raw timestamps.

```ts
const scatterSignupData = [
  { datetime: 1767571200000, signups: 42, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1767571200000, signups: 30, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1767657600000, signups: 48, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1767657600000, signups: 34, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1767744000000, signups: 45, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1767744000000, signups: 31, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1767830400000, signups: 51, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1767830400000, signups: 37, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1767916800000, signups: 58, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1767916800000, signups: 40, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1768003200000, signups: 36, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1768003200000, signups: 44, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1768089600000, signups: 33, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1768089600000, signups: 47, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1768176000000, signups: 55, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1768176000000, signups: 39, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1768262400000, signups: 61, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1768262400000, signups: 43, platform: 'Mobile' },
  { datetime: 1768348800000, signups: 64, platform: 'Web' },
  { datetime: 1768348800000, signups: 46, platform: 'Mobile' },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterSignupData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" granularity="day" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="datetime"
    dimensionScaleType="time"
    metric="signups"
    color="platform"
  />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `dimensionScaleType` on `Scatter`: `time` or `linear`. Shown: `time`.

### Empty and loading

When `data` is an empty array, `Chart` shows `emptyStateText` instead. Set `loading` on `Chart` to show a spinner while data loads.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={emptyData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **state**: `empty` or `loading`. Shown: `empty`.

With **state** set to `loading`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData} loading>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
</Chart>
```

## Encodings

`color`, `size`, `opacity`, `lineType`, `lineWidth`, and `stroke` each take either a field name in the data, which maps each value through a scale, or a static value like `{ value: 'L' }`.

### Color

By default every point uses one static color, `categorical-100`. Set `color` to a field name to color points by category; each value gets the next color in the chart's `colors` and an entry in the `Legend`. Use `{ value: 'gray-700' }` for a different static color.

For a numeric field, set `colorScaleType="linear"` and pass a sequential scheme such as `sequentialViridis5` to `colors` on `Chart`. `Legend` then shows a gradient.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
  <Legend title="Channel" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `color` on `Scatter`: `channel`, `roi` or `static`. Shown: `channel`.
-   `color` on `Scatter`: `categorical-100`, `categorical-200` or `gray-700`. Shown: `categorical-100`.
-   `colors` on `Chart`: `sequentialViridis5`, `sequentialMagma5` or `sequentialRose5`. Shown: `sequentialViridis5`.

### Size

`size` sets the width of each point. It accepts `XS` (6px), `S` (8px), `M` (10px, default), `L` (12px), `XL` (16px), or a number of pixels.

Set `size` to a numeric field to size points by value, as in a bubble chart. Sizes range linearly from the smallest to the largest value, between the two sizes in `symbolSizes` on `Chart` (default `['XS', 'XL']`). `Legend` shows a size legend for the field.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" />
  <Legend position="right" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `size` on `Scatter`: `M`, `XS`, `S`, `L`, `XL`, `24` or `reach`. Shown: `M`.
-   `symbolSizes` on `Chart`: `XS`, `S` or `M`. Shown: `XS`.
-   `symbolSizes` on `Chart`: `L`, `XL` or `32`. Shown: `XL`.

### Opacity

`opacity` sets point opacity from 0 to 1 (default `1`). Set it to a field name to give each value its own opacity. Opacities are evenly spaced unless you list them in `opacities` on `Chart`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="spend"
    metric="revenue"
    color="channel"
    size={{ value: 'L' }}
  />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `opacity` on `Scatter`: `1`, `0.5` or `audience`. Shown: `1`.
-   `opacities` on `Chart`: `default`, `1, 0.4` or `1, 0.15`. Shown: `default`.

### Outline

Points have no outline by default (`lineWidth` is `0`). `lineWidth` takes `XS` (1px), `S` (1.5px), `M` (2px), `L` (3px), `XL` (4px), or a number of pixels. `lineType` sets the outline dash pattern, and `stroke` sets its color, which defaults to the point's `color`. A translucent fill with a solid outline keeps overlapping points readable.

Each of these can also be a field name. A `lineWidth` field maps through `lineWidths` on `Chart`, a `lineType` field through `lineTypes`, and a `stroke` field through the color scale.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="spend"
    metric="revenue"
    color="channel"
    size={{ value: 'XL' }}
    opacity={{ value: 0.4 }}
  />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `lineWidth` on `Scatter`: `0`, `XS`, `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL` or `audience`. Shown: `0`.
-   `lineType` on `Scatter`: `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted` or `audience`. Shown: `solid`.
-   `stroke` on `Scatter`: `none`, `gray-800` or `audience`. Shown: `none`.
-   `opacity` on `Scatter`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.4`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `lineWidths` defaults to `['M']`, so a `lineWidth` field gives every point the same 2px outline until you set `lineWidths` on `Chart`.

### Blend

Overlapping points blend so dense areas look darker: `multiply` in light mode and `screen` in dark mode. Set `blend="normal"` to turn blending off so later points cover earlier ones, or pass another [Vega blend mode](https://vega.github.io/vega/docs/marks/#blend).

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData} symbolSizes={['S', 48]}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel" size="reach" />
  <Legend position="right" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `blend` on `Scatter`: `default`, `normal`, `multiply`, `screen` or `darken`. Shown: `default`.

### Clip

When an `Axis` `range` is smaller than the data, points outside the range still draw past the plot edge. Set `clip` to hide them.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" range={[0, 100]} />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="spend"
    metric="revenue"
    color="channel"
    size={{ value: 'XL' }}
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `clip` on `Scatter`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## ScatterPath

`ScatterPath` connects points that share the same values, in data order, to show how something moved over time. By default it groups points by the fields used for `color`, `size`, `opacity`, and `lineType`; set `groupBy` to a list of fields to group differently.

Paths draw behind the points in `gray-500` at 50% opacity. A static `pathWidth` takes a line width from `XS` (1px) to `XL` (4px), defaulting to `M` (2px), or a number of pixels. A numeric field varies the width from point to point, scaled between the chart's `symbolSizes`.

```ts
const scatterTrajectoryData = [
  { product: 'Analytics', month: 'Jan', share: 12, growth: 4 },
  { product: 'Analytics', month: 'Feb', share: 15, growth: 9 },
  { product: 'Analytics', month: 'Mar', share: 19, growth: 12 },
  { product: 'Analytics', month: 'Apr', share: 21, growth: 7 },
  { product: 'Analytics', month: 'May', share: 20, growth: 2 },
  { product: 'Commerce', month: 'Jan', share: 30, growth: 11 },
  { product: 'Commerce', month: 'Feb', share: 28, growth: 6 },
  { product: 'Commerce', month: 'Mar', share: 25, growth: 1 },
  { product: 'Commerce', month: 'Apr', share: 27, growth: 5 },
  { product: 'Commerce', month: 'May', share: 31, growth: 10 },
  { product: 'Design', month: 'Jan', share: 6, growth: 14 },
  { product: 'Design', month: 'Feb', share: 9, growth: 16 },
  { product: 'Design', month: 'Mar', share: 13, growth: 15 },
  { product: 'Design', month: 'Apr', share: 16, growth: 11 },
  { product: 'Design', month: 'May', share: 17, growth: 13 },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  ScatterAnnotation,
  ScatterPath,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterTrajectoryData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Growth (%)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Market share (%)" />
  <Scatter dimension="share" metric="growth" color="product">
    <ScatterPath />
    <ScatterAnnotation textKey="month" />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `color` on `ScatterPath`: `gray-500` or `gray-800`. Shown: `gray-500`.
-   `pathWidth` on `ScatterPath`: `M`, `S`, `XL` or `share`. Shown: `M`.
-   `opacity` on `ScatterPath`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `0.5`.
-   `ScatterAnnotation`: included or left out. Shown: included.

## ScatterAnnotation

`ScatterAnnotation` labels each point. `textKey` names the field to show (default: the scatter's `metric`).

`anchor` sets where the label sits relative to its point. With a list, each position is tried in order until one fits inside the chart without overlapping another label or point. Labels that don't fit anywhere are hidden. The default tries `right`, `top`, `bottom`, then `left`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  ScatterAnnotation,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <ScatterAnnotation />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `textKey` on `ScatterAnnotation`: `revenue`, `campaign` or `channel`. Shown: `revenue`.
-   `anchor` on `ScatterAnnotation`: `right, top, bottom, left`, `right`, `top` or `left, bottom`. Shown: `right, top, bottom, left`.

## Trendline

`Trendline` draws a statistical trend through the scatter's points, one per color series. Its `method` sets the calculation (default `linear`):

-   `average` and `median` draw a flat line at that value.
-   `linear`, `quadratic`, `polynomial-N` (for example `polynomial-3`), `exponential`, `logarithmic`, and `power` fit a regression curve.
-   `movingAverage-N` averages each point with the N - 1 points before it.

Trendlines are dashed, `M` width, and the color of their series. `lineType`, `lineWidth`, `opacity`, and `color` change that. `orientation="vertical"` calculates the trend of the dimension across the metric instead, for example a vertical line at the average x.

`dimensionRange` limits the calculation to points between two dimension values; `null` leaves a side unbounded. `dimensionExtent` sets how far the line draws and defaults to `dimensionRange`. Use `'domain'` to extend the line to the edge of the axis.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <Trendline />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `method` on `Trendline`: `linear`, `average`, `median`, `quadratic`, `exponential`, `logarithmic` or `power`. Shown: `linear`.
-   `lineType` on `Trendline`: `dashed`, `solid` or `dotted`. Shown: `dashed`.
-   `lineWidth` on `Trendline`: `M`, `XS`, `S`, `L` or `XL`. Shown: `M`.
-   `opacity` on `Trendline`: 0 to 1, in steps of 0.1. Shown: `1`.
-   `color` on `Trendline`: `series` or `gray-700`. Shown: `series`.
-   `orientation` on `Trendline`: `horizontal` or `vertical`. Shown: `horizontal`.
-   `dimensionRange` on `Trendline`: `none` or `10, 30`. Shown: `none`.
-   `dimensionExtent` on `Trendline`: `dimensionRange`, `domain, domain` or `0, 50`. Shown: `dimensionRange`.
-   `color` on `Scatter`: `channel` or `static`. Shown: `channel`.

### Moving averages

Moving averages work best on evenly spaced data like a time series. Set `hidePartialWindows` to hide the first points, which average fewer than N values.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterSignupData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" granularity="day" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="datetime"
    dimensionScaleType="time"
    metric="signups"
    color="platform"
  >
    <Trendline method="movingAverage-3" />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `method` on `Trendline`: `movingAverage-3`, `movingAverage-5` or `linear`. Shown: `movingAverage-3`.
-   `hidePartialWindows` on `Trendline`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

### Excluding points

`excludeDataKeys` leaves out rows where any of the listed fields is truthy, so known outliers don't skew the trend. The points still draw.

```ts
const scatterOutlierData = [
  { day: 1, visits: 120, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 2, visits: 135, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 3, visits: 128, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 4, visits: 410, isBotTraffic: true },
  { day: 5, visits: 152, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 6, visits: 160, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 7, visits: 149, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 8, visits: 171, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 9, visits: 455, isBotTraffic: true },
  { day: 10, visits: 182, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 11, visits: 190, isBotTraffic: false },
  { day: 12, visits: 186, isBotTraffic: false },
];
```

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterOutlierData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Day" />
  <Scatter dimension="day" metric="visits">
    <Trendline color="gray-700" excludeDataKeys={['isBotTraffic']} />
  </Scatter>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `excludeDataKeys` on `Trendline`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

### Trendline interaction

Add `ChartInspect` as a child of `Trendline` to show its value on hover. The hovered datum has the trend's value in `rscTrendlineValue`. `highlightRawPoint` also highlights the data point at the hovered position.

`displayOnHover` hides the trendline until a point in its series is hovered. It needs a `ChartInspect` on the `Scatter`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.campaign}: ${datum.revenue}K revenue on ${datum.spend}K spend
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <Trendline>
      <ChartInspect>
        {(datum) => <div>Trend: ${datum.rscTrendlineValue.toFixed(1)}K</div>}
      </ChartInspect>
    </Trendline>
  </Scatter>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect` (Trendline): included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightRawPoint` on `Trendline`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `displayOnHover` on `Trendline`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## TrendlineAnnotation

`TrendlineAnnotation` labels a trendline with its value. `dimensionValue` sets where along the line: `end` (default), `start`, or a dimension value. `numberFormat` takes a [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier and follows the chart's `locale`; `prefix` adds text before the value. `badge` draws the label in a filled badge in the trendline's color.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
  TrendlineAnnotation,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue">
    <Trendline method="average" dimensionExtent={['domain', 'domain']}>
      <TrendlineAnnotation numberFormat=",.1f" />
    </Trendline>
  </Scatter>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `method` on `Trendline`: `average` or `median`. Shown: `average`.
-   `badge` on `TrendlineAnnotation`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `dimensionValue` on `TrendlineAnnotation`: `end`, `start` or `20`. Shown: `end`.
-   `numberFormat` on `TrendlineAnnotation`: `,.1f`, `$,.0f` or `none`. Shown: `,.1f`.
-   `prefix` on `TrendlineAnnotation`: any text. Shown: empty.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `TrendlineAnnotation` only works with the `average` and `median` methods. With regression or moving-average methods the chart fails to render.

## Legend

Add `Legend` as a sibling of `Scatter` to list its series. The plot shrinks to make room for it.

-   `highlight` highlights a series, including its trendline and paths, while its entry is hovered.
-   `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its series. To start with series hidden, set `defaultHiddenSeries`.
-   `legendLabels` replaces the label shown for a series.

When a scatter encodes several fields, such as `color` and `opacity`, one legend lists every combination.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <Trendline method="average" />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend title="Channel" highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `right`, `top` or `left`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `title` on `Legend`: any text. Shown: `Channel`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `legendLabels` on `Legend`: `none` or `Paid search, Paid social, Email`. Shown: `none`.

### Size, gradient, and opacity legends

A numeric `size` field gets a size legend, listed after any category entries, and a linear `color` field gets a gradient legend. When points share one color and `opacity` is a field, set `opacity` on `Legend` to that field so the legend symbols match.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" size="reach" />
  <Legend position="right" title="Reach (K)" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Scatter facet**: `size`, `color` or `opacity`. Shown: `size`.

With **Scatter facet** set to `color`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData} colors="sequentialViridis5">
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="spend"
    metric="revenue"
    size={{ value: 'L' }}
    color="roi"
    colorScaleType="linear"
  />
  <Legend position="right" title="ROI" />
</Chart>
```

With **Scatter facet** set to `opacity`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter
    dimension="spend"
    metric="revenue"
    size={{ value: 'L' }}
    opacity="audience"
  />
  <Legend position="right" title="Audience" opacity="audience" />
</Chart>
```

### Hiding series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. Their trendlines hide too.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Legend } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Scatter,
  Trendline,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData} hiddenSeries={['Social']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <Trendline />
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Social` or `Social, Email`. Shown: `Social`.

## Interaction

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

Add `ChartInspect` to show details on hover and `ChartPopover` to show details on click. Pass a function as children to render content from the hovered point's datum; `Scatter` has no default content.

Hovering highlights the nearest point and fades the rest. `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect` highlights more: `series` highlights the hovered point's series, `dimension` highlights points with the same x value, and a list of fields highlights points that share those values. `excludeDataKeys` skips rows where any of the listed fields is truthy.

`ChartPopover` rings the clicked point. `rightClick` opens it on right-click instead.

`tooltipAnchor="mark"` on `Chart` places inspect content next to the hovered point instead of following the cursor; `tooltipPlacement` picks the side.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.campaign}: ${datum.revenue}K revenue on ${datum.spend}K spend
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.campaign}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.channel}, {datum.reach}K reach</Text>
          </Content>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Scatter>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series`, `dimension` or `audience`. Shown: `item`.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `tooltipAnchor` on `Chart`: `cursor` or `mark`. Shown: `cursor`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `Scatter` doesn't support `onClick`, `onContextMenu`, `onMouseOver`, or `onMouseOut` yet.

### Highlighting

`highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row. `highlightedItem` does the same by row ID and can take a list; set `idKey` on `Chart` to the field that uniquely identifies each row. `Legend` with `highlight` highlights a series when its entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={scatterCampaignData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Revenue ($K)" />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Spend ($K)" />
  <Scatter dimension="spend" metric="revenue" color="channel">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.campaign}: ${datum.revenue}K revenue on ${datum.spend}K spend
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Scatter>
  <Legend highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Search`, `Social` or `Email`. Shown: `none`.
-   `highlightedItem` on `Chart`: `none`, `3` or `3, 12`. Shown: `none`.

## Animation

`Scatter` doesn't animate yet: `animationTypes` on `Chart` has no effect on points, paths, or trendlines.

## API

### Scatter

`name` identifies the scatter's marks and signals in the rendered Vega spec. It defaults to `scatter0`, `scatter1`, and so on.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blend` — CSS blend mode where points overlap. `normal` turns blending off. Defaults to `multiply` in light mode and `screen` in dark mode. | `"normal" \| Blend` | – |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `ScatterChild` | – |
| `clip` — Restricts scatter plot contents to the plot boundaries. | `boolean` | – |
| `color` — Point fill color: a data key mapped to the color scale, or a static color. | `ColorFacet` | `'series'` |
| `colorScaleType` — Color scale type: `ordinal` for category keys, `linear` for numeric keys. | `"linear" \| "ordinal"` | `'ordinal'` |
| `dimension` — Data key for the x position. | `string` | `'x'` |
| `dimensionScaleType` — Scale type for the x position; use `time` for timestamps. | `"linear" \| "time" \| "point" \| "band"` | `'linear'` |
| `lineType` — Outline dash pattern: a data key mapped to the chart's `lineTypes`, or a static line type. | `LineTypeFacet` | `{ value: 'solid' }` |
| `lineWidth` — Outline width: a data key mapped to the chart's `lineWidths`, or a static width. | `LineWidthFacet` | `{ value: 0 }` |
| `metric` — Key in the data that is used as the metric | `string` | `'value'` |
| `name` — Sets the name of the component. | `string` | – |
| `opacity` — Point opacity: a data key mapped to the chart's `opacities`, or a static value. | `OpacityFacet` | `{ value: 1 }` |
| `size` — Point width: a numeric data key scaled between the chart's `symbolSizes`, or a static size. | `SymbolSizeFacet` | `{ value: DEFAULT_SYMBOL_SIZE }` |
| `stroke` — Outline color: a data key mapped to the color scale, or a static color. | `ColorFacet` | `'color'` |

### ScatterPath

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` — The color of the links. | `string` | `'gray-500'` |
| `groupBy` — Data fields that group points; each group's points are connected by a path. | `string[]` | – |
| `opacity` — The opacity of the links. | `number` | `0.5` |
| `pathWidth` — The width on the links. Link width can vary by point. | `PathWidthFacet` | `{ value: 'M' }` |

### ScatterAnnotation

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` — Specifies where to position the annotation relative to the data point. When an array is provided, each position is tried in order until one fits within the chart bounds and doesn't overlap with other annotations or points. If no position fits, the annotation is not displayed. | `LabelAnchor \| LabelAnchor[]` | `['right', 'top', 'bottom', 'left']` |
| `textKey` — Data field with the label text. | `string` | `'annotation'` |

### Trendline

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Supported child components. | `TrendlineChild` | – |
| `color` — Trendline color. Defaults to the color of its series. | `string` | – |
| `dimensionExtent` — Range of `dimension` to draw the trendline over. `domain` extends it to the edge of the chart; `null` stops at the first or last row. | `[number \| "domain" \| null, number \| "domain" \| null]` | `'dimensionRange'` |
| `dimensionRange` — Range of `dimension` the trendline is calculated from; `null` leaves that end unbounded. | `[number \| null, number \| null]` | `[null, null]` |
| `displayOnHover` — Whether the trendline should only be visible when hovering over the parent line | `boolean` | `false` |
| `excludeDataKeys` — Data points where these keys have truthy values will not be included in the trendline calculation | `string[]` | – |
| `hidePartialWindows` — Hides the first points of a moving average, which are calculated from less than a full window. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `highlightRawPoint` — If there is an inspect on this trendline, then this will highlight the raw point in addition to the hovered trendline point. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `lineType` — Line type of the trendline. | `LineType` | `'dashed'` |
| `lineWidth` — Line width of the trendline. | `LineWidth` | `'M'` |
| `method` — Statistical method used to calculate the trendline. | `TrendlineMethod` | `'linear'` |
| `opacity` — Opacity of the trendline. | `number` | `1` |
| `orientation` — Orientation of the trendline; `vertical` calculates the dimension across the metric. Only supported on scatter plots. | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `'horizontal'` |

### TrendlineAnnotation

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `badge` — Adds a badge around the annotation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `dimensionValue` — Where along the trendline to place the label: `start`, `end`, or a `dimension` value. | `number \| "start" \| "end"` | `'end'` |
| `numberFormat` — d3 number format specifier. Only valid if labelFormat is linear or undefined. @see https://d3js.org/d3-format#locale\_format | `string` | `''` |
| `prefix` — Text shown before the trendline value. | `string` | `''` |

---

# Axis

**Stage:** Alpha

An `Axis` labels one side of the chart. Add one `Axis` per side you want labeled, alongside the mark, as a child of `Chart`. A chart with no `Axis` draws only the plot.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" title="Visits" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `title` on `Axis` (Left axis): any text. Shown: `Visits`.
-   `grid` on `Axis` (Left axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `numberFormat` on `Axis` (Left axis): `shortNumber`, `standardNumber` or `shortCurrency`. Shown: `shortNumber`.
-   `title` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): any text. Shown: empty.
-   `baseline` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `ticks` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `labelFormat` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `time` or `linear`. Shown: `time`.

## Data

Axes don't take data. Each axis reads the scale of the mark it sits beside, so its labels come from the mark's `dimension` and `metric` fields. Line charts on this page use `axisVisitsData`, one row per day with `datetime` in epoch milliseconds:

```ts
const axisVisitsData = [
  { datetime: 1741003200000, visits: 2300 },
  { datetime: 1741089600000, visits: 2490 },
  { datetime: 1741176000000, visits: 2400 },
  { datetime: 1741262400000, visits: 2580 },
  { datetime: 1741348800000, visits: 2490 },
  { datetime: 1741435200000, visits: 1780 },
  { datetime: 1741521600000, visits: 1690 },
  { datetime: 1741608000000, visits: 2500 },
  { datetime: 1741694400000, visits: 2680 },
  { datetime: 1741780800000, visits: 2590 },
  { datetime: 1741867200000, visits: 2780 },
  { datetime: 1741953600000, visits: 2690 },
  { datetime: 1742040000000, visits: 1980 },
  { datetime: 1742126400000, visits: 1880 },
  { datetime: 1742212800000, visits: 2690 },
  { datetime: 1742299200000, visits: 2880 },
  { datetime: 1742385600000, visits: 2790 },
  { datetime: 1742472000000, visits: 2980 },
  { datetime: 1742558400000, visits: 2880 },
  { datetime: 1742644800000, visits: 2170 },
  { datetime: 1742731200000, visits: 2080 },
];
```

Bar charts use `axisBrowserData`:

```ts
const axisBrowserData = [
  { browser: 'Chrome', downloads: 27000, thumbnail: 'https://opensource.adobe.com/react-spectrum-charts/chrome.png' },
  { browser: 'Firefox', downloads: 8000, thumbnail: 'https://opensource.adobe.com/react-spectrum-charts/firefox.png' },
  { browser: 'Safari', downloads: 7750, thumbnail: 'https://opensource.adobe.com/react-spectrum-charts/safari.png' },
  { browser: 'Edge', downloads: 7600, thumbnail: 'https://opensource.adobe.com/react-spectrum-charts/edge.png' },
  { browser: 'Explorer', downloads: 1000, thumbnail: 'https://opensource.adobe.com/react-spectrum-charts/explorer.png' },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visits" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

## Scales

`position` decides which scale the axis labels. `bottom` and `top` label the x scale, and `left` and `right` label the y scale. The scale type comes from the mark:

-   **Time**: `Line` uses a time scale by default (`scaleType="time"`). Set `labelFormat="time"` on the axis. Without it, the axis shows a few long, truncated date strings such as `Wed Mar 05 2025 00:00:…`.
-   **Linear**: `Line` with `scaleType="linear"` and a numeric `dimension`, and every value (`metric`) axis.
-   **Point**: `Line` with `scaleType="point"` spaces categories evenly.
-   **Band**: `Bar` puts its `dimension` on a band scale, at the bottom by default or on the left with `orientation="horizontal"`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Chart**: `Line, time`, `Line, linear`, `Line, point`, `Bar, vertical` or `Bar, horizontal`. Shown: `Line, time`.

With **Chart** set to `Line, linear`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisConversionData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid labelFormat="percentage" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Week" />
  <Line dimension="week" metric="rate" scaleType="linear" />
</Chart>
```

With **Chart** set to `Line, point`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="browser" metric="downloads" scaleType="point" />
</Chart>
```

With **Chart** set to `Bar, vertical`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

With **Chart** set to `Bar, horizontal`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" baseline />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" orientation="horizontal" />
</Chart>
```

Some props only apply to some scales. `range` works on linear and time scales, `tickMinStep` on linear scales, `granularity` on time scales, and `truncateLabels` and `AxisThumbnail` on band scales.

## Position and titles

Use two axes on the same scale, such as `left` and `right`, to repeat the labels on both sides. `title` takes a string, or an array of strings for a multi-line title.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Axis` (Value axis): `left`, `right` or `both`. Shown: `left`.
-   `title` on `Axis` (Value axis): `none`, `Downloads` or `Downloads, Last 30 days`. Shown: `Downloads`.
-   `position` on `Axis` (Category axis): `bottom` or `top`. Shown: `bottom`.

## Gridlines, ticks, and baseline

-   `grid` draws a gridline at each tick across the plot. It also spaces ticks about 100px apart; without it, a value axis falls back to Vega's default tick count, which can crowd the labels.
-   `ticks` draws a short tick mark at each label.
-   `baseline` draws a solid line along the axis. When the opposite scale is linear, as with the bottom axis of a bar chart, the baseline is drawn at that scale's `baselineOffset` value (default `0`). `baselineOffset` is ignored when the opposite scale is categorical.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `grid` on `Axis` (Left axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `ticks` on `Axis` (Left axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `baseline` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `baselineOffset` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): 0 to 20000, in steps of 2500. Shown: `0`.
-   `ticks` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Label formats

`labelFormat` sets how values are written:

| `labelFormat` | Values | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linear` (default) | Numbers, formatted with `numberFormat` | `1.2M` |
| `percentage` | Fractions, where `0.05` is 5% | `5%` |
| `duration` | Seconds, written as minutes and seconds or hours | `16:40`, `1:06:40` |
| `time` | Dates, labeled by `granularity` | `Mar`, `2025` |

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `labelFormat` on `Axis`: `linear`, `percentage` or `duration`. Shown: `linear`.

The data and charts used here are `axisConversionData` and `axisDurationData`:

```ts
const axisConversionData = [
  { week: 1, rate: 0.021 },
  { week: 2, rate: 0.024 },
  { week: 3, rate: 0.023 },
  { week: 4, rate: 0.028 },
  { week: 5, rate: 0.031 },
  { week: 6, rate: 0.029 },
  { week: 7, rate: 0.034 },
  { week: 8, rate: 0.036 },
  { week: 9, rate: 0.033 },
  { week: 10, rate: 0.038 },
];
```

```ts
const axisDurationData = [
  { page: 'Home', seconds: 95 },
  { page: 'Pricing', seconds: 210 },
  { page: 'Docs', seconds: 1260 },
  { page: 'Tutorials', seconds: 3020 },
  { page: 'Webinars', seconds: 4410 },
];
```

### Number formats

`numberFormat` formats `linear` labels. It takes a preset or any [d3-format](https://d3js.org/d3-format) specifier:

| `numberFormat` | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `shortNumber` (default) | `1.2M` |
| `standardNumber` | `1,200,000` |
| `shortCurrency` | `$1.2M` |
| `currency` | `$1,200,000.00` |
| `,.0f`, `.2s`, `$,.0f` | `1,200,000`, `1.2M`, `$1,200,000` |

`locale` on `Chart` changes the separators and currency symbol, so `de-DE` writes `1.200.000,00 €`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisRevenueData}>
  <Axis position="left" baseline />
  <Axis position="bottom" grid title="Revenue" />
  <Bar dimension="region" metric="revenue" orientation="horizontal" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `numberFormat` on `Axis`: `shortNumber`, `standardNumber`, `shortCurrency`, `currency`, `,.0f`, `.2s` or `$,.0f`. Shown: `shortNumber`.
-   `currencyCode` on `Axis`: `none`, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP` or `JPY`. Shown: `none`.
-   `currencyLocale` on `Axis`: `none`, `en-US`, `de-DE`, `fr-FR` or `ja-JP`. Shown: `none`.
-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE` or `fr-FR`. Shown: `en-US`.

```ts
const axisRevenueData = [
  { region: 'North America', revenue: 1284500 },
  { region: 'Europe', revenue: 942300 },
  { region: 'Asia Pacific', revenue: 615800 },
  { region: 'Latin America', revenue: 238400 },
  { region: 'Middle East and Africa', revenue: 129900 },
];
```

> **Limited support:**
> 
> `currencyCode` and `currencyLocale` override the chart locale's currency symbol and its position. Both are required, and they only apply with `numberFormat="currency"` or a fixed-decimal specifier such as `,.0f`. Support for these props is limited; prefer the chart `locale` when it gives the right currency.

`numberFormat="percentage"` multiplies values by 100. For rates stored as fractions, use `labelFormat="percentage"` instead.

### Time and granularity

With `labelFormat="time"`, `granularity` sets the unit for each tick (default `day`). A bottom or top time axis shows two rows: the unit on the first row and the next larger unit on the second, written once each time it changes.

| `granularity` | First row | Second row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `second` | `:05` | `9:00 AM` |
| `minute` | `9:10 AM` | `Mar 3` |
| `hour` | `6 PM` | `Mar 3` |
| `day` | `14` | `Mar` |
| `week` | `14` | `Mar` |
| `month` | `Mar` | `2025` |
| `quarter` | `Q1` | `2025` |
| `year` | `2025` |  |

Labels use the browser's time zone. A `Bar` with a `datetime` dimension gets the same labels on its band axis. A left or right time axis, as on a horizontal bar chart, uses one row, such as `Mar 3`, `4`, `5`.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `granularity` on `Axis`: `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter` or `year`. Shown: `day`.
-   **mark** (Chart): `Line` or `Bar`. Shown: `Line`.

With **mark** set to `Bar`:

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Bar dimension="datetime" metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

> **Caution:**
> 
> `tickCountLimit` and `tickCountMinimum` on a time axis replace the granularity's tick interval and can repeat labels, such as `Q1 Q1 Q2`. Match the tick count to the data if you set them.

## Range

`range` fixes the minimum and maximum of a linear or time axis, such as `[0, 0.05]`, instead of fitting the data. It is ignored on band scales.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisConversionData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid labelFormat="percentage" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Week" />
  <Line dimension="week" metric="rate" scaleType="linear" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `range` on `Axis`: `none`, `0, 0.05`, `0, 0.1` or `0.02, 0.04`. Shown: `none`.

## Tick count

These props apply when ticks are spaced automatically:

-   `tickCountMinimum` sets the minimum number of ticks.
-   `tickCountLimit` sets the maximum, not counting the base tick: `0, 1, 2, 3` counts as 3.
-   `tickMinStep` sets the smallest step between ticks in data units, so `1` keeps a week axis on whole weeks. It only applies to linear scales.

Vega rounds to readable values, so the final count can differ slightly.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisConversionData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid labelFormat="percentage" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline ticks title="Week" />
  <Line dimension="week" metric="rate" scaleType="linear" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `tickCountMinimum` on `Axis` (Left axis): 0 to 12, in steps of 1. Shown: `0`.
-   `tickCountLimit` on `Axis` (Left axis): 0 to 12, in steps of 1. Shown: `0`.
-   `tickMinStep` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): 0 to 5, in steps of 1. Shown: `0`.

## Label layout

-   `labelOrientation="vertical"` rotates labels 90° to fit long category names.
-   `labelAlign` sets the label's alignment to its tick (default `center`). On a band axis, `start` and `end` move labels to the edges of the band.
-   `labelFontWeight` sets `normal` or `bold`.
-   `truncateLabels` cuts category labels that are wider than their band, ending them with an ellipsis. It works on bottom and top band axes with horizontal labels.
-   `labelLimit` sets the maximum label length in pixels (default `180`).

Labels that would overlap are hidden, so long names without truncation can lose every other label.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisRevenueData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Bar dimension="region" metric="revenue" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `labelOrientation` on `Axis`: `horizontal` or `vertical`. Shown: `horizontal`.
-   `labelAlign` on `Axis`: `start`, `center` or `end`. Shown: `center`.
-   `labelFontWeight` on `Axis`: `normal` or `bold`. Shown: `normal`.
-   `truncateLabels` on `Axis`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `labelLimit` on `Axis`: 40 to 180, in steps of 20. Shown: `180`.

## Custom labels

`labels` replaces the automatic labels with your own list. Pass values to label specific ticks, or `{ value, label, align, fontWeight }` objects to also change the text and style. `numberFormat` isn't applied to custom labels, so write the text you want in `label`.

`hideDefaultLabels` hides an axis's labels while keeping its gridlines and title.

`subLabels` adds a second row under specific labels as `{ value, subLabel, align, fontWeight }` objects. Labels with no sublabel show nothing on the second row. Sublabels only appear when labels are horizontal.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis
    position="bottom"
    baseline
    subLabels={[{ value: 'Chrome', subLabel: 'Blink' }, { value: 'Edge', subLabel: 'Blink' }, { value: 'Firefox', subLabel: 'Gecko' }, { value: 'Safari', subLabel: 'WebKit' }, { value: 'Explorer', subLabel: 'Trident' }]}
  />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `labels` on `Axis` (Left axis): `none`, `values` or `label objects`. Shown: `none`.
-   `hideDefaultLabels` on `Axis` (Left axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `subLabels` on `Axis` (Bottom axis): `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

> **Note:**
> 
> `hideDefaultLabels` also hides labels set with `labels`. Use one or the other.

## ReferenceLine

`ReferenceLine` is a child of a value `Axis`, such as a line chart's left axis. It draws a line across the plot at a `value`, with an optional `label`, to mark a threshold like a target. The line has carets at both ends.

-   `size` sets the stroke and caret size: `XS`, `S`, `M`, or `L`. When it isn't set, the size follows the chart width.
-   `secondary` draws a thin 1px line without carets. With `size="XS"`, its line and label are also a lighter gray.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Line,
  ReferenceLine,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid>
    <ReferenceLine value={2500} label="Target" />
  </Axis>
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `value` on `ReferenceLine`: 0 to 3000, in steps of 100. Shown: `2500`.
-   `label` on `ReferenceLine`: any text. Shown: `Target`.
-   `size` on `ReferenceLine`: `auto`, `XS`, `S`, `M` or `L`. Shown: `auto`.
-   `secondary` on `ReferenceLine`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## AxisThumbnail

`AxisThumbnail` is a child of `Axis` that shows an image next to each label on a band axis. The image URL comes from the data field named by `urlKey` (default `thumbnail`). Images are up to 42px square, shrink with the band, and are hidden when the band is narrower than 16px. Combine with `hideDefaultLabels` to show images only.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  AxisThumbnail,
  Bar,
  Chart,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline>
    <AxisThumbnail />
  </Axis>
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `orientation` on `Bar`: `vertical` or `horizontal`. Shown: `vertical`.
-   `hideDefaultLabels` on `Axis`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Interaction

### Label tooltips

`hasTooltip` shows a tooltip with the full label value when a label is hovered, which helps with `truncateLabels` or `labelLimit`. `tooltipText` overrides the text for listed values as `{ value, text }` objects; set `text` to `null` to show no tooltip for a value.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisRevenueData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis
    position="bottom"
    baseline
    truncateLabels
    hasTooltip
    tooltipText={[{ value: 'Middle East and Africa', text: 'Middle East and Africa (EMEA South)' }, { value: 'Europe', text: null }]}
  />
  <Bar dimension="region" metric="revenue" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hasTooltip` on `Axis`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `tooltipText` on `Axis`: `none` or `custom`. Shown: `custom`.

### Label clicks and hover

`onClick` runs when a label is clicked, with the mouse event, the label's value, and its index. It doesn't run when `hideDefaultLabels` is set.

When a `Bar` is interactive, for example with `ChartInspect`, hovering a label on its category axis highlights that category's bars and fades the other labels.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={axisBrowserData}>
  <Title text="Selected: none" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis
    position="bottom"
    baseline
    onClick={(event, value) => setSelected(value)}
  />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.browser}: {datum.downloads.toLocaleString()} downloads
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Bar>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `onClick` on `Axis`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.

> **Note:**
> 
> Time axes (`labelFormat="time"`) don't support `labels`, `hasTooltip`, or `onClick`.

## API

### Axis

> **Caution:**
> 
> Don't set `name` on `Axis`. It's currently used as the axis's scale name, which stops the chart from rendering.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axisAnnotations` | `AxisAnnotationOptions[]` | – |
| `baseline` — Draws a solid baseline along the axis. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `baselineOffset` — Value on the opposite linear scale where the baseline is drawn; ignored without `baseline` or when that scale is categorical. | `number` | `0` |
| `children` — Child components that add supplemental content to the axis | `AxisChild` | – |
| `currencyCode` — Limited support: currency code, such as `EUR`, that overrides the chart locale's symbol; requires `currencyLocale`. | `string` | – |
| `currencyLocale` — Limited support: locale for the currency symbol's position, such as `de-DE`; requires `currencyCode` and `numberFormat="currency"` or a `,.Nf` specifier. | `string` | – |
| `granularity` — Time unit for the ticks and labels of a time axis; ignored on other axes. | `Granularity` | `'day'` |
| `grid` — Draws a gridline across the plot at each tick. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `hasTooltip` — Shows a tooltip with the full label value when a label is hovered; not supported on time axes. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `hideDefaultLabels` — Hides the axis labels, including any set with `labels`. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `labelAlign` — Alignment of each label relative to its tick. | `"center" \| "start" \| "end"` | `'center'` |
| `labelFontWeight` — Font weight of the axis labels. | `FontWeight` | `'normal'` |
| `labelFormat` — How label values are written: `linear` numbers, `percentage` fractions, `duration` seconds, or `time` dates. | `"duration" \| "linear" \| "percentage" \| "time"` | `'linear'` |
| `labelLimit` — Maximum label length in pixels; longer labels end with an ellipsis. | `number` | `180` |
| `labelOrientation` — Orientation of the axis labels; `vertical` rotates them 90°. | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `'horizontal'` |
| `labels` — Labels to show instead of the automatic ones, as values or `{ value, label, align, fontWeight }` objects; not supported on time axes. | `(string \| number \| Label)[]` | – |
| `name` — Sets the name of the component. | `string` | – |
| `numberFormat` — Format for `linear` labels: `shortNumber`, `standardNumber`, `currency`, `shortCurrency`, or a d3-format specifier. | `string` | `'shortNumber'` |
