| `onClick` — Called with the mouse event, label value, and label index when an axis label is clicked; not supported on time axes. | `AxisLabelClickCallback` | – |
| `position`required — Side of the chart the axis is drawn on; bottom and top label the x scale, left and right the y scale. | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | – |
| `range` — Fixed minimum and maximum axis values, such as `[-10, 10]`; only for linear and time scales. | `[number, number]` | `'undefined'` |
| `subLabels` — Second row of labels under specific values, as `{ value, subLabel, align, fontWeight }` objects; horizontal labels only. | `SubLabel[]` | – |
| `tickCountLimit` — Maximum number of ticks, not counting the base tick; on time axes it replaces the granularity interval and can repeat labels. | `number` | `'undefined'` |
| `tickCountMinimum` — Minimum number of ticks when ticks are spaced automatically. | `number` | `'undefined'` |
| `tickMinStep` — Smallest step between ticks in data units, such as `1` for whole numbers; only for linear scales. | `number` | `'undefined'` |
| `ticks` — Draws a tick mark at each label. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `title` — Axis title; an array of strings makes a multi-line title. | `string \| string[]` | `'undefined'` |
| `tooltipText` — Tooltip text for specific values as `{ value, text }` objects; `text: null` hides that value's tooltip. | `AxisTooltip[]` | `'undefined'` |
| `truncateLabels` — Cuts category labels wider than their band on bottom and top band axes. | `boolean` | `false` |

### ReferenceLine

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` — Label shown below the line at the right edge. | `string` | – |
| `position` — Places the line on a category's center, or before or after it; only for band scales. | `"center" \| "before" \| "after"` | `'center'` |
| `secondary` — Draws the line without carets, in a lighter color at `XS` size. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `size` — Stroke and caret size; when omitted, the size follows the chart width. | `"XS" \| "S" \| "M" \| "L"` | – |
| `value`required — The value on the axis where the reference line should be drawn. | `string \| number` | – |

### AxisThumbnail

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `urlKey` — Data field that holds each category's image URL. | `string` | `'thumbnail'` |

> **Note:**
> 
> `AxisAnnotation` from the Spectrum 1 package isn't available in Spectrum 2.

---

# Legend

**Stage:** Alpha

A legend names each series in a chart and shows the color and symbol that represents it. Add `Legend` as a child of `Chart`, next to the marks. The plot shrinks to make room for it. `isToggleable` lets users click an entry to hide or show its series, and `highlight` fades the other series while an entry is hovered.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend title="Channel" isToggleable highlight />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `top`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `title` on `Legend`: any text. Shown: `Channel`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Data

The legend reads its entries from the chart's data and marks, so it has no data of its own. Most examples on this page draw one line per marketing channel from `legendVisitsData`:

```ts
const legendVisitsData = [
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Search', visits: 820 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Search', visits: 932 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Search', visits: 901 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Search', visits: 934 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Search', visits: 1290 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Social', visits: 620 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Social', visits: 732 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Social', visits: 701 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Social', visits: 834 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Social', visits: 1090 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Email', visits: 320 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Email', visits: 332 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Email', visits: 401 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Email', visits: 334 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Email', visits: 390 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Direct', visits: 220 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Direct', visits: 282 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Direct', visits: 191 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Direct', visits: 234 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Direct', visits: 290 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

Donut legends work the same way; see [Donut legends](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#legend) for how they interact with `DonutSummary` and segment hiding.

## Position and alignment

`position` puts the legend on the `bottom` (default), `top`, `left`, or `right` of the plot. Bottom and top legends lay their entries out in rows and wrap onto more rows when they don't fit. Left and right legends stack their entries in a column.

`align` anchors the legend along its edge. Its meaning depends on `position`:

| `position` | `align: 'start'` | `align: 'middle'` | `align: 'end'` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `'bottom'` / `'top'` | left-aligned (default) | centered | right-aligned |
| `'left'` / `'right'` | top-aligned | centered (default) | bottom-aligned |

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom`, `top`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `align` on `Legend`: `default`, `start`, `middle` or `end`. Shown: `default`.

## Title

`title` adds a heading above the entries. Long titles widen a side legend, which narrows the plot; `titleLimit` caps the title's width in pixels and truncates it with an ellipsis.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend
    position="right"
    title="Marketing channel (last 7 days)"
    titleLimit={120}
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom` or `right`. Shown: `right`.
-   `title` on `Legend`: any text. Shown: `Marketing channel (last 7 days)`.
-   `titleLimit` on `Legend`: `none`, `80`, `120` or `160`. Shown: `120`.

## Entries

The legend has one entry for each unique value of the fields the marks use for color, line type, opacity, or symbol shape. When a mark uses more than one of these fields, each combination gets an entry, named with the values joined by `|`, for example `Search | This week`.

### Hiding entries

`hiddenEntries` removes entries from the legend by name. The series still draws in the chart. To hide the series itself, see [Hiding series](#hiding-series).

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend hiddenEntries={['Direct']} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenEntries` on `Legend`: `none`, `Direct` or `Email, Direct`. Shown: `Direct`.

### Labels

Entries show the series name by default. `legendLabels` replaces it with a display label, matched by `seriesName`. Series without a label keep their name.

```ts
const legendChannelLabels = [
  { seriesName: 'Search', label: 'Organic and paid search' },
  { seriesName: 'Social', label: 'Social media referrals' },
  { seriesName: 'Email', label: 'Email campaigns' },
  { seriesName: 'Direct', label: 'Direct traffic' },
];
```

`labelLimit` caps a label's width in pixels (default 184) and truncates longer labels with an ellipsis. In bottom and top legends it also sets the column width, so a smaller limit fits more entries per row.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend legendLabels={legendChannelLabels} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `legendLabels` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom` or `right`. Shown: `bottom`.
-   `labelLimit` on `Legend`: `default`, `80`, `100` or `140`. Shown: `default`.

### keys

`keys` limits the entries to the fields you list. Here, `legendPeriodData` has a line for each channel and week: `color` is set by channel and `lineType` by week. Without `keys` the legend lists all four combinations. `keys={['channel']}` lists only the channels, and `keys={['period']}` lists only the weeks.

```ts
const legendPeriodData = [
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Search', period: 'This week', visits: 820 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Search', period: 'This week', visits: 932 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Search', period: 'This week', visits: 901 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Search', period: 'This week', visits: 934 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Search', period: 'This week', visits: 1290 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Search', period: 'Last week', visits: 760 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Search', period: 'Last week', visits: 810 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Search', period: 'Last week', visits: 845 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Search', period: 'Last week', visits: 880 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Search', period: 'Last week', visits: 1010 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Email', period: 'This week', visits: 320 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Email', period: 'This week', visits: 332 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Email', period: 'This week', visits: 401 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Email', period: 'This week', visits: 334 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Email', period: 'This week', visits: 390 },
  { day: 'Mon', channel: 'Email', period: 'Last week', visits: 290 },
  { day: 'Tue', channel: 'Email', period: 'Last week', visits: 305 },
  { day: 'Wed', channel: 'Email', period: 'Last week', visits: 350 },
  { day: 'Thu', channel: 'Email', period: 'Last week', visits: 318 },
  { day: 'Fri', channel: 'Email', period: 'Last week', visits: 342 },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendPeriodData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line
    dimension="day"
    metric="visits"
    color="channel"
    lineType="period"
    scaleType="point"
  />
  <Legend keys={['channel']} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `keys` on `Legend`: `none`, `channel` or `period`. Shown: `channel`.

## Symbols

Each entry's symbol matches its series: the color, line type, and opacity of the mark it represents. Symbol props on `Legend` override that for the legend only. Each takes a field name from the data or a static value such as `{ value: 'circle' }`:

-   `symbolShape` sets the shape. The default is a rounded square. A field name picks shapes from the chart's `symbolShapes` list, in order; set `symbolShapes` on `Chart` to use more than one shape.
-   `color` sets the fill color, for example `{ value: 'gray-700' }`.
-   `opacity` sets the fill opacity. A low opacity makes the outline easier to see.
-   `lineType` and `lineWidth` set the symbol's outline.

To change the colors, line types, or shapes for the whole chart, use `colors`, `lineTypes`, and `symbolShapes` on `Chart` instead.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend symbolShape={{ value: 'circle' }} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `symbolShape` on `Legend`: `default`, `circle`, `diamond` or `channel`. Shown: `circle`.
-   `color` on `Legend`: `default` or `gray-700`. Shown: `default`.
-   `opacity` on `Legend`: `default`, `0.25` or `0.5`. Shown: `default`.
-   `lineType` on `Legend`: `default`, `dashed` or `dotted`. Shown: `default`.
-   `lineWidth` on `Legend`: `default`, `S`, `M`, `L` or `XL`. Shown: `default`.

## Hiding series

### Toggleable legends

With `isToggleable`, clicking an entry hides its series and clicking again shows it. The hidden entry's symbol turns into a crossed-out eye icon and its label stays at full strength, so the entry still reads clearly. `defaultHiddenSeries` lists series to hide when the chart first renders; after that, the legend tracks hidden series itself.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend isToggleable defaultHiddenSeries={['Email']} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `defaultHiddenSeries` on `Legend`: `none`, `Email` or `Email, Direct`. Shown: `Email`.

### Controlled hidden series

`hiddenSeries` on `Chart` hides series from outside the chart, for example from a filter control. The legend shows the eye icon and grays the label for each hidden series. Don't combine it with `isToggleable`: a toggleable legend tracks its own hidden series and ignores `hiddenSeries`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData} hiddenSeries={['Email']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`: `none`, `Email` or `Email, Direct`. Shown: `Email`.

To let users toggle series from the legend while your app owns the state, handle `onClick` and pass the result to `hiddenSeries`:

```tsx
const [hiddenSeries, setHiddenSeries] = useState<string[]>([]);

const toggleSeries = (seriesName: string) =>
  setHiddenSeries((hidden) =>
    hidden.includes(seriesName) ? hidden.filter((name) => name !== seriesName) : [...hidden, seriesName]
  );

<Chart data={legendVisitsData} hiddenSeries={hiddenSeries}>
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend onClick={toggleSeries} />
</Chart>;
```

## Highlighting

`highlight` fades the other series and their entries while an entry is hovered. The legend also follows highlighting from elsewhere:

-   `highlightedSeries` on `Chart` highlights a series from outside the chart, for example from a table row.
-   With `ChartInspect` on a mark, hovering a series fades the other legend entries.

In this example the table below the chart drives `highlightedSeries`: hover a row to highlight that channel, or select a row to keep it highlighted. Hovering a legend entry bolds its row, using the legend's `onMouseOver` and `onMouseOut`. The code panel shows only the chart.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend
    highlight
    onMouseOver={(seriesName) => setHoveredSeries(seriesName)}
    onMouseOut={() => setHoveredSeries(undefined)}
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `highlight` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: left out.

## Descriptions

`descriptions` shows a tooltip when an entry is hovered. Each description is matched by `seriesName` and can have an optional `title`, which replaces the series name as the tooltip heading.

```ts
const legendChannelDescriptions = [
  { seriesName: 'Search', description: 'Visits from search engine results.' },
  { seriesName: 'Social', title: 'Social media', description: 'Visits from links shared on social networks.' },
  { seriesName: 'Email', description: 'Visits from newsletter and campaign links.' },
  { seriesName: 'Direct', description: 'Visits with no referrer, like typed URLs and bookmarks.' },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend descriptions={legendChannelDescriptions} />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `descriptions` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `position` on `Legend`: `bottom` or `right`. Shown: `bottom`.

> **Note:**
> 
> Give every entry a description. An entry without one shows an empty tooltip ([#1011](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum-charts/issues/1011)).

## Events

`onClick`, `onMouseOver`, and `onMouseOut` receive the entry's series name. Use them to sync the legend with other parts of your app. Entries show a pointer cursor when the legend has `onClick`, a popover, or `isToggleable`. With `isToggleable`, `onClick` fires in addition to the toggle.

In this example the table below the chart shows the last event each entry received. Clicking an entry selects its row and sets `highlightedSeries`; selecting a row does the same from the table side. Turn the event controls off to see which events stop reaching the table.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend
    onClick={(seriesName) => setSelectedSeries(seriesName)}
    onMouseOver={(seriesName) => setHoveredSeries(seriesName)}
    onMouseOut={() => setHoveredSeries(undefined)}
  />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `onClick` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `onMouseOver` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `onMouseOut` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## ChartPopover

Add a `ChartPopover` as a child of `Legend` to open a popover from an entry. Its children function receives a datum whose `value` is the series name, and a `close` function. Clicking an entry with a popover opens the popover instead of toggling the series; set `rightClick` on `ChartPopover` to open it on right-click and keep left-click for `isToggleable`. Build the content from Spectrum 2 components such as `Heading`, `Content`, `Text`, and `Button`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Button,
  ButtonGroup,
  Content,
  Heading,
  Text,
} from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={legendVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="day" metric="visits" color="channel" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend>
    <ChartPopover width="auto">
      {(datum, close) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.value}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>Open the {datum.value} channel report</Text>
          </Content>
          <ButtonGroup UNSAFE_style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>
            <Button variant="secondary" size="S" onPress={close}>Close</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Legend>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.
-   `isToggleable` on `Legend`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Sizing

The legend takes its space from the chart, so the plot gets smaller as the legend grows. Long labels, titles, and extra rows all shrink the plot. On small charts, keep labels short, set `labelLimit` and `titleLimit`, or move the legend to the bottom. Very small charts can still clip the legend or leave little room for the plot ([#1010](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum-charts/issues/1010)).

> **Note:**
> 
> The S2 `Legend` doesn't support these S1 props yet: `_preferredColumns` and `_maxRows` (row limits with pagination) and `_labelWrap`.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `align` — Alignment along the legend's edge: left to right for bottom/top legends, top to bottom for left/right legends. Defaults to `'start'` for bottom/top and `'middle'` for left/right. | `"start" \| "end" \| "middle"` | – |
| `chartPopovers` | `ChartPopoverOptions[]` | – |
| `children` — `ChartPopover` to open when an entry is clicked. | `ChartPopover` | – |
| `color` — Symbol color: a data field to facet by, or a static value like `{ value: 'gray-700' }`. Defaults to the marks' color. | `ColorFacet` | – |
| `defaultHiddenSeries` — Series hidden when the chart first renders, for a toggleable legend (uncontrolled). | `string[]` | – |
| `descriptions` — Tooltip text for each entry, matched by `seriesName`; `title` replaces the series name as the heading. | `LegendDescription[]` | – |
| `hiddenEntries` — Series names to leave out of the legend. Their marks still render. | `string[]` | – |
| `highlight` — Fades the other series while an entry is hovered. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `isToggleable` — Lets users click an entry to hide or show its series (uncontrolled). | `boolean` | `false` |
| `keys` — Data fields to generate entries from. Defaults to every field the marks facet by. | `string[]` | – |
| `labelLimit` — Max label width in pixels before truncating; also sets the column width of bottom/top legends. | `number` | `184` |
| `legendLabels` — Display labels for entries, matched by `seriesName`. | `LegendLabel[]` | – |
| `lineType` — Symbol outline line type: a data field to facet by, or a static value like `{ value: 'dashed' }`. | `LineTypeFacet` | – |
| `lineWidth` — Symbol outline width: a data field to facet by, or a static value like `{ value: 'L' }`. | `LineWidthFacet` | – |
| `name` — Sets the name of the component. | `string` | – |
| `onClick` — Called with the entry's series name when an entry is clicked. | `((seriesName: string) => void)` | – |
| `onMouseOut` — Called with the entry's series name when the pointer leaves an entry. | `((seriesName: string) => void)` | – |
| `onMouseOver` — Called with the entry's series name when the pointer enters an entry. | `((seriesName: string) => void)` | – |
| `opacity` — Symbol fill opacity: a data field to facet by, or a static value like `{ value: 0.5 }`. | `OpacityFacet` | – |
| `position` — Side of the plot the legend is placed on. | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `'bottom'` |
| `symbolShape` — Symbol shape: a data field that picks from the chart's `symbolShapes`, or a static value like `{ value: 'circle' }`. Defaults to a rounded square. | `SymbolShapeFacet` | – |
| `title` — Heading shown above the entries. | `string` | – |
| `titleLimit` — Max title width in pixels before truncating. | `number` | – |

---

# Title

**Stage:** Alpha

`Title` adds a title to a chart. Add it as a child of `Chart`, alongside the marks; it works with every chart type.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Title text="Visitors by browser" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="count" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `text` on `Title`: any text. Shown: `Visitors by browser`.
-   `position` on `Title`: `start`, `middle` or `end`. Shown: `start`.
-   `orient` on `Title`: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `top`.
-   `fontWeight` on `Title`: `300`, `400`, `700` or `900`. Shown: `700`.
-   `fontSize` on `Title`: 12 to 32, in steps of 1. Shown: `24`.

## Data

`Title` doesn't read the chart's data. The examples on this page use a `Bar` chart of `browserData`:

```ts
const browserData = [
  { count: 10390, browser: 'Chrome' },
  { count: 8281, browser: 'Firefox' },
  { count: 7045, browser: 'Safari' },
  { count: 6166, browser: 'Opera' },
  { count: 4201, browser: 'Other' },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Title text="Visitors by browser" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="count" />
</Chart>
```

## Placement

-   `orient` picks the side of the chart the title is on: `top` (default), `bottom`, `left`, or `right`. Left and right titles are rotated to read along the side.
-   `position` aligns the title along that side: `start` (default), `middle`, or `end`. On a top or bottom title, `start` is the left edge of the plot.

The title is aligned to the plot area, not the whole chart, so a `start` title lines up with the left edge of the plot rather than the axis labels.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Title text="Visitors by browser" position="middle" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="count" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `orient` on `Title`: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `top`.
-   `position` on `Title`: `start`, `middle` or `end`. Shown: `middle`.

## Font

`fontWeight` and `fontSize` set the title's text style. The defaults are `700` and `24`. Any CSS font weight works, such as `400`, `'normal'`, or `'bold'`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Title,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Title text="Visitors by browser" fontWeight={400} fontSize={18} />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="count" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `fontWeight` on `Title`: `300`, `400`, `700` or `900`. Shown: `400`.
-   `fontSize` on `Title`: 12 to 32, in steps of 1. Shown: `18`.

## Size

The title takes space from the chart, so the plot shrinks to fit it. A larger `fontSize`, or a title on the left or right, leaves less room for the plot.

## Chart title prop

`title` on `Chart` also draws a title, using a smaller theme style you can't change. A `Title` child replaces it. Use `Title` when you need to set the title's placement or font.

```jsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData} title="Visitors">
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="count" />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `title` on `Chart`: any text. Shown: `Visitors`.
-   `Title`: included or left out. Shown: left out.

> **Note:**
> 
> A chart shows one title. If there's more than one `Title`, only the first is used. Subtitles, title color, and the spacing between the title and the plot aren't supported.

## API

### Title

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fontSize` — Font size of the title text in pixels. | `number` | `24` |
| `fontWeight` — Font weight of the title text. | `FontWeight` | `'bold'` |
| `orient` — Side of the chart the title is drawn on. | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `'top'` |
| `position` — Where the title sits along its side of the chart: `'start'`, `'middle'`, or `'end'`. | `"start" \| "end" \| "middle"` | `'middle'` |
| `text`required — Title text. | `string` | – |

---

# ChartInspect and ChartPopover

**Stage:** Alpha

`ChartInspect` shows a tooltip with details about the data point under the pointer. `ChartPopover` opens a popover when a data point is clicked, for content the user can interact with, like links or buttons. Neither renders anything itself: add them as children of a mark, and pass a function as children that returns the content for a data point.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Button,
  ButtonGroup,
  Content,
  Heading,
  Text,
} from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visitors" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Month" />
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.device}, {datum.month}: {datum.visitors} visitors
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover>
      {(datum, close) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.device}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.month}: {datum.visitors} visitors</Text>
          </Content>
          <ButtonGroup UNSAFE_style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>
            <Button variant="secondary" size="S" onPress={close}>Close</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Mark** (Example): `Line` or `Bar`. Shown: `Line`.
-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series` or `dimension`. Shown: `item`.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Data

Most examples on this page use a line chart of `interactionVisitorsData` or a stacked bar chart of `interactionDownloadsData`. Each row has an `id` field, used in [Highlighting](#highlighting).

```ts
const interactionVisitorsData = [
  { id: 'Desktop-Jan', month: 'Jan', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 4200 },
  { id: 'Desktop-Feb', month: 'Feb', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 4800 },
  { id: 'Desktop-Mar', month: 'Mar', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 4500 },
  { id: 'Desktop-Apr', month: 'Apr', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 5300 },
  { id: 'Desktop-May', month: 'May', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 5900 },
  { id: 'Desktop-Jun', month: 'Jun', device: 'Desktop', visitors: 6400 },
  { id: 'Mobile-Jan', month: 'Jan', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 2600 },
  { id: 'Mobile-Feb', month: 'Feb', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 3100 },
  { id: 'Mobile-Mar', month: 'Mar', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 3900 },
  { id: 'Mobile-Apr', month: 'Apr', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 3700 },
  { id: 'Mobile-May', month: 'May', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 4600 },
  { id: 'Mobile-Jun', month: 'Jun', device: 'Mobile', visitors: 5200 },
];
```

```ts
const interactionDownloadsData = [
  { id: 'Chrome-Windows', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Windows', downloads: 5000 },
  { id: 'Chrome-Mac', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Mac', downloads: 3000 },
  { id: 'Chrome-Linux', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Linux', downloads: 1200 },
  { id: 'Firefox-Windows', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Windows', downloads: 2700 },
  { id: 'Firefox-Mac', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Mac', downloads: 1500 },
  { id: 'Firefox-Linux', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Linux', downloads: 1800 },
  { id: 'Safari-Windows', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Windows', downloads: 300 },
  { id: 'Safari-Mac', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Mac', downloads: 4200 },
  { id: 'Safari-Linux', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Linux', downloads: 150 },
  { id: 'Edge-Windows', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Windows', downloads: 2400 },
  { id: 'Edge-Mac', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Mac', downloads: 600 },
  { id: 'Edge-Linux', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Linux', downloads: 200 },
];
```

```tsx
<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData}>
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point">
    <ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{datum.visitors} visitors</div>}</ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover>
      {(datum, close) => (
        <Button variant="secondary" size="S" onPress={close}>
          Close
        </Button>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Line>
</Chart>
```

## Content

`ChartInspect` children are a function that takes the hovered data point, `datum`, and returns React content. `ChartPopover` children take the clicked `datum` and a `close` function that closes the popover.

The content can be any React content. The popovers on this page use Spectrum 2 components from `@react-spectrum/s2`, like `Heading`, `Content`, `Text`, and `Button`, except the [Size](#size) example, which uses custom HTML.

`datum` is the row from `data`, plus fields the chart adds:

-   `rscComponentName`: the name of the mark that was hovered or clicked, like `line0` or `bar0`. Use it to tell marks apart when a chart has more than one.
-   `rscMarkId` and `rscSeriesId`: the row's ID and series.
-   `rscGroupData`: the rows in the highlighted group, when [`highlightBy`](#highlightby) isn't `'item'` or the inspect is over a [dimension area](#targets).

Other internal fields, like stack offsets on bars, may also appear. Use **raw datum** below to see everything a mark passes.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visitors" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Month" />
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => <pre>{JSON.stringify(datum, null, 2)}</pre>}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Mark** (Example): `Line` or `Bar`. Shown: `Line`.
-   `children` on `ChartInspect`: `formatted`, `raw datum` or `none`. Shown: `raw datum`.

### Default content

Only [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#chartinspect-and-chartpopover) has default content: without children, its inspect and popover show the segment's color, name, share of the total, and value. On other marks, an inspect or popover without children shows nothing, although the mark still responds to the pointer.

On `Line`, adding `ChartInspect` turns off the line's built-in hover label, which shows the hovered value on the axis.

## ChartInspect

### Placement

The inspect follows the cursor by default. Set `tooltipAnchor="mark"` on `Chart` to anchor it to the hovered mark instead, and `tooltipPlacement` to place it on the `top` (default), `bottom`, `left`, or `right` of the mark. `tooltipPlacement` only applies when the inspect is anchored to the mark.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData} tooltipAnchor="mark">
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visitors" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Month" />
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.device}, {datum.month}: {datum.visitors} visitors
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Mark** (Example): `Line` or `Bar`. Shown: `Line`.
-   `tooltipAnchor` on `Chart`: `cursor` or `mark`. Shown: `mark`.
-   `tooltipPlacement` on `Chart`: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. Shown: `top`.

### highlightBy

While the inspect is visible, the hovered point stays at full opacity and other points fade. `highlightBy` sets what stays highlighted:

-   `'item'` (default): the hovered point.
-   `'series'`: every point in the hovered point's series (the `color` field).
-   `'dimension'`: every point at the hovered dimension value, like a month or a browser.
-   A list of field names: every point that matches the hovered point on all of those fields, like `['browser', 'os']`.

With any value other than `'item'`, `datum.rscGroupData` holds the rows in the highlighted group, so the inspect can summarize them. The example below counts and totals the group.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visitors" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Month" />
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point">
    <ChartInspect highlightBy="series">
      {(datum) => {
        const group = datum.rscGroupData ?? [datum];
        const total = group.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.visitors, 0);
        return <div>{group.length} points, {total} visitors</div>;
      }}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **Mark** (Example): `Line` or `Bar`. Shown: `Line`.
-   `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `series` or `dimension`. Shown: `series`.

### targets

On stacked or dodged bars, `targets` sets what shows the inspect. `'item'` (default) is a single bar. `'dimensionArea'` is the whole column for a dimension value, including the padding around its bars; hovering the empty space in a column shows the inspect for that column, with its bars in `datum.rscGroupData`. Pass both to inspect bars and columns.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionDownloadsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Browser" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" color="os">
    <ChartInspect targets={['dimensionArea', 'item']}>
      {(datum) => {
        const group = datum.rscGroupData ?? [datum];
        const total = group.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.downloads, 0);
        return <div>{group.length} bars, {total} downloads</div>;
      }}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `targets` on `ChartInspect`: `item`, `dimensionArea` or `dimensionArea, item`. Shown: `dimensionArea, item`.

`targets` only applies to `Bar`. Hovering a bar shows its own inspect even when `targets` leaves out `'item'`.

### excludeDataKeys

`excludeDataKeys` lists fields that turn off the inspect for a row: rows with a truthy value in any of these fields don't show an inspect or fade the rest of the chart. Below, Linux downloads are estimates, flagged with `isEstimate`:

```ts
const interactionEstimatesData = [
  { id: 'Chrome-Windows', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Windows', downloads: 5000, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Chrome-Mac', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Mac', downloads: 3000, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Chrome-Linux', browser: 'Chrome', os: 'Linux', downloads: 1200, isEstimate: true },
  { id: 'Firefox-Windows', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Windows', downloads: 2700, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Firefox-Mac', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Mac', downloads: 1500, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Firefox-Linux', browser: 'Firefox', os: 'Linux', downloads: 1800, isEstimate: true },
  { id: 'Safari-Windows', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Windows', downloads: 300, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Safari-Mac', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Mac', downloads: 4200, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Safari-Linux', browser: 'Safari', os: 'Linux', downloads: 150, isEstimate: true },
  { id: 'Edge-Windows', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Windows', downloads: 2400, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Edge-Mac', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Mac', downloads: 600, isEstimate: false },
  { id: 'Edge-Linux', browser: 'Edge', os: 'Linux', downloads: 200, isEstimate: true },
];
```

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionEstimatesData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Browser" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" color="os">
    <ChartInspect excludeDataKeys={['isEstimate']}>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.browser} on {datum.os}: {datum.downloads} downloads
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `excludeDataKeys` on `ChartInspect`: `none` or `isEstimate`. Shown: `isEstimate`.

## ChartPopover

### Opening and closing

Clicking a data point opens the popover above it. It closes when the user clicks outside it, presses `Escape`, or your content calls `close`. While a popover is open, the clicked point stays highlighted and `ChartInspect` doesn't show.

Set `rightClick` to open the popover on right-click instead of click, for example to show a context menu. A mark can have one click popover and one right-click popover.

> **Note:**
> 
> The popover always opens above the clicked point and moves only to stay on screen. There's no `placement` prop. `UNSAFE_highlightBy` sets what stays highlighted while the popover is open, like `highlightBy` on `ChartInspect`; it's incomplete and may change.

### Size

Without `width`, the popover fits its content. Set `width` to a number of pixels or `'auto'`, and limit it with `minWidth` (default `0`) and `maxWidth`. `height`, `minHeight`, and `maxHeight` work the same way. `contentMargin` (default `12`) is the space between the popover's edge and its content. `containerPadding` (default `12`) is the closest the popover gets to the edge of the window.

This example's popover content is custom HTML with inline styles rather than Spectrum 2 components, to show that the popover takes any React content.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={interactionDownloadsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Browser" />
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" color="os">
    <ChartPopover width={320}>
      {(datum, close) => (
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8 }}>
          <strong>{datum.browser} on {datum.os}</strong>
          <span>{datum.downloads} downloads this quarter. …</span>
          <button onClick={close}>Close</button>
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `width` on `ChartPopover` (Width): `none`, `auto`, `200` or `320`. Shown: `320`.
-   `minWidth` on `ChartPopover` (Width): 0 to 400, in steps of 20. Shown: `0`.
-   `maxWidth` on `ChartPopover` (Width): `none`, `240` or `400`. Shown: `none`.
-   `height` on `ChartPopover` (Height): `none`, `auto`, `120` or `200`. Shown: `none`.
-   `minHeight` on `ChartPopover` (Height): `none`, `160` or `240`. Shown: `none`.
-   `maxHeight` on `ChartPopover` (Height): `none`, `100` or `160`. Shown: `none`.
-   `contentMargin` on `ChartPopover` (Spacing): 0 to 32, in steps of 4. Shown: `12`.
-   `containerPadding` on `ChartPopover` (Spacing): 0 to 48, in steps of 4. Shown: `12`.

### Callbacks

`onOpenChange` is called with `true` when the popover opens and `false` when it closes. `onClick` on the mark is called with the clicked `datum`; on `Line` and `Bar` it fires along with the popover.

```tsx
<Chart data={interactionDownloadsData}>
  <Bar
    dimension="browser"
    metric="downloads"
    color="os"
    onClick={(datum) => setSelected(datum.id)}
  >
    <ChartPopover onOpenChange={(isOpen) => setIsPopoverOpen(isOpen)}>
      {(datum, close) => <DownloadsDetails datum={datum} onDone={close} />}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Bar>
</Chart>
```

### Legend popovers

`Legend` can have a `ChartPopover` too. Clicking an entry opens it, with the entry's series name in `datum.value` and `datum.rscSeriesId`. A legend with a click popover can't hide series on click.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import {
  Button,
  ButtonGroup,
  Content,
  Heading,
  Text,
} from '@react-spectrum/s2';

<Chart data={interactionVisitorsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Visitors" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Month" />
  <Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device" scaleType="point" />
  <Legend>
    <ChartPopover>
      {(datum, close) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.value}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>Open the {datum.value} report</Text>
          </Content>
          <ButtonGroup UNSAFE_style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>
            <Button variant="secondary" size="S" onPress={close}>Close</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
  </Legend>
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `rightClick` on `ChartPopover`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

## Using both together

A mark can have a `ChartInspect` and a `ChartPopover`. The inspect shows on hover, and clicking opens the popover and hides the inspect until the popover closes. Use the inspect for a quick read of the value and the popover for details and actions.

On `Line`, a click `ChartPopover` can't be combined with a [`ChartActionBar`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar): only the action bar renders. Use `rightClick` on the popover to have both.

## Supported marks

| Mark | ChartInspect | ChartPopover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line) | Yes | Yes |
| [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar) | Yes | Yes |
| [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#chartinspect-and-chartpopover) | Yes, with default content | Yes, with default content |
| [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend) | No | Yes |
| Area (lab) | Yes | Yes |
| Scatter (lab) | Yes | Yes |
| Bullet (lab) | Yes | No |
| Trendline (lab) | Yes | No |

Lab components are imported from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`. Some marks change how hovering works, like `interactionMode` on `Line`; see each chart's page.

## Highlighting

`ChartInspect` highlights what's under the pointer. To highlight from outside the chart, for example from a table row, use these `Chart` props:

-   `highlightedSeries`: a series value, like `'Mac'`. Other series fade.
-   `highlightedItem`: one row ID or a list of them. Other rows fade.
-   `idKey`: the field that uniquely identifies each row, used by `highlightedItem`. Set it to a field in your data, like `id`.

Hovering the chart overrides these while the pointer is over a mark. The controlled highlight returns when the pointer leaves.

In the example below, the table and the chart share state. Hovering a table row or selecting rows sets `highlightedItem` to that browser's bars. Hovering a bar calls `onMouseOver`, which bolds its value in the table, and clicking a bar calls `onClick`, which selects its browser's row. While a bar is hovered, the chart highlights that bar instead of `highlightedItem`.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart
  data={interactionDownloadsData}
  idKey="id"
  highlightedItem={['Safari-Windows', 'Safari-Mac', 'Safari-Linux']}
>
  <Axis position="left" grid title="Downloads" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline title="Browser" />
  <Bar
    dimension="browser"
    metric="downloads"
    color="os"
    onMouseOver={(datum) => setHoveredId(datum.id)}
    onMouseOut={() => setHoveredId(undefined)}
    onClick={(datum) => toggleBrowser(datum.browser)}
  >
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.browser} on {datum.os}: {datum.downloads} downloads
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
  </Bar>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The code panel shows only the chart. The table is a Spectrum 2 `TableView` that shares state with it:

```tsx
const [selectedBrowsers, setSelectedBrowsers] = useState(new Set(['Safari']));
const [hoveredBrowser, setHoveredBrowser] = useState();
const browsers = hoveredBrowser ? [hoveredBrowser] : [...selectedBrowsers];
const getIds = (browser) => ['Windows', 'Mac', 'Linux'].map((os) => `${browser}-${os}`);

<Chart
  data={interactionDownloadsData}
  idKey="id"
  highlightedItem={browsers.length ? browsers.flatMap(getIds) : undefined}
>
  …
</Chart>

<TableView
  aria-label="Downloads by browser"
  selectionMode="multiple"
  selectedKeys={selectedBrowsers}
  onSelectionChange={setSelectedBrowsers}
>
  <TableHeader>…</TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <Row
      id="Chrome"
      onMouseEnter={() => setHoveredBrowser('Chrome')}
      onMouseLeave={() => setHoveredBrowser(undefined)}
    >
      …
    </Row>
    …
  </TableBody>
</TableView>
```

> **Note:**
> 
> On `Line`, `highlightedItem` with a custom `idKey` marks the highlighted point but doesn't fade the other series.

## API

### ChartInspect

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Function that returns the inspect content for the hovered `datum`. | `InspectHandler` | – |
| `excludeDataKeys` — Data keys that turn off the inspect for rows with a truthy value in any of them. | `string[]` | – |
| `highlightBy` — What stays highlighted while the inspect is visible: the item, its series, its dimension value, or rows matching a list of keys. | `string[] \| "dimension" \| "series" \| "item"` | `'item'` |
| `targets` — What shows the inspect on stacked or dodged bars: single bars (`'item'`) and/or whole columns (`'dimensionArea'`). | `("item" \| "dimensionArea")[]` | `['item']` |

### ChartPopover

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Function that returns the popover content for the clicked `datum`; call `close` to close the popover. | `PopoverHandler` | – |
| `containerPadding` — Minimum space in pixels between the popover and the edge of the window. | `number` | `12` |
| `contentMargin` — Space in pixels between the popover's edge and its content. | `number` | `12` |
| `height` — Height of the popover in pixels, or `'auto'`; fits its content when unset. | `number \| "auto"` | – |
| `maxHeight` — Maximum height of the popover in pixels. | `number` | – |
| `maxWidth` — Maximum width of the popover in pixels. | `number` | – |
| `minHeight` — Minimum height of the popover in pixels. | `number` | – |
| `minWidth` — Minimum width of the popover in pixels. | `number` | `0` |
| `onOpenChange` — Called with `true` when the popover opens and `false` when it closes. | `((isOpen: boolean) => void)` | – |
| `rightClick` — Opens the popover on right-click instead of click. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `UNSAFE_highlightBy` — What stays highlighted while the popover is open, like `highlightBy` on ChartInspect; incomplete. | `string[] \| "dimension" \| "series" \| "item"` | `'item'` |
| `width` — Width of the popover in pixels, or `'auto'`; fits its content when unset. | `number \| "auto"` | `250` |

---

# ChartActionBar

**Stage:** Lab

`ChartActionBar` shows a toolbar of actions, like annotating or bookmarking, when a user clicks a point on a `Line`. Add it as a child of `Line`; click a point in the chart below to open it.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { ChartActionBar } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { ActionButton, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import StickyNote from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/StickyNote';
import Comment from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Comment';
import Bookmark from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Bookmark';

<Chart data={deviceVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartActionBar>
      {(datum, close) => [
        <ActionButton key="annotate" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <StickyNote />
          <Text>Annotate</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="comment" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Comment />
          <Text>Comment</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="bookmark" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Bookmark />
          <Text>Bookmark</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
      ]}
    </ChartActionBar>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `children` on `ChartActionBar`: 1 to 5, in steps of 1. Shown: `3`.
-   `maxActions` on `ChartActionBar`: 1 to 5, in steps of 1. Shown: `4`.
-   `isEmphasized` on `ChartActionBar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `false`.

`ChartActionBar` is a lab component. Import it from the `lab` subpath:

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { ChartActionBar } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

## Data

`ChartActionBar` doesn't need any data fields of its own. It passes the clicked point to your actions as `datum`, which holds every field of that row (here `datetime`, `device`, and `visits`). The examples on this page use `deviceVisitsData`:

```ts
const deviceVisitsData = [
  { datetime: 1791158400000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 4120 },
  { datetime: 1791158400000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 2980 },
  { datetime: 1791244800000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 4385 },
  { datetime: 1791244800000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 3105 },
  { datetime: 1791331200000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 4250 },
  { datetime: 1791331200000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 3340 },
  { datetime: 1791417600000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 4610 },
  { datetime: 1791417600000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 3220 },
  { datetime: 1791504000000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 4480 },
  { datetime: 1791504000000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 3560 },
  { datetime: 1791590400000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 2910 },
  { datetime: 1791590400000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 3890 },
  { datetime: 1791676800000, device: 'Desktop', visits: 2640 },
  { datetime: 1791676800000, device: 'Mobile', visits: 4010 },
];
```

## Actions

`children` is a function that takes the clicked `datum` and a `close` function and returns an array of action elements. Use React Spectrum `ActionButton`s with `isQuiet`, and give each one a `key`. Call `close` when an action finishes to dismiss the bar.

```tsx
import { ActionButton, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import StickyNote from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/StickyNote';

<Chart data={deviceVisitsData}>
  <Line metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartActionBar>
      {(datum, close) => [
        <ActionButton
          key="annotate"
          isQuiet
          onPress={() => {
            addNote(datum.device, datum.datetime);
            close();
          }}
        >
          <StickyNote />
          <Text>Annotate</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
      ]}
    </ChartActionBar>
  </Line>
</Chart>;
```

Actions can be any element, such as a `MenuTrigger` for a menu of related actions or a `ContextualHelp` with details about the point. If `children` isn't set, clicking a point doesn't open a bar.

### maxActions

The bar shows up to `maxActions` actions inline (default `4`). The rest move to a **More actions** (`···`) menu at the end of the bar. The bar is at most 800px wide, so it also moves actions into the menu when they don't fit.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { ChartActionBar } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { ActionButton, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import StickyNote from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/StickyNote';
import Comment from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Comment';
import Bookmark from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Bookmark';
import Export from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Export';
import Flag from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Flag';

<Chart data={deviceVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartActionBar maxActions={2}>
      {(datum, close) => [
        <ActionButton key="annotate" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <StickyNote />
          <Text>Annotate</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="comment" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Comment />
          <Text>Comment</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="bookmark" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Bookmark />
          <Text>Bookmark</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="export" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Export />
          <Text>Export</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="flag" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Flag />
          <Text>Flag</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
      ]}
    </ChartActionBar>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `maxActions` on `ChartActionBar`: 1 to 5, in steps of 1. Shown: `2`.

### isEmphasized

`isEmphasized` gives the bar an accent background. Set `staticColor="white"` on the actions so they stay readable on it.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { ChartActionBar } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { ActionButton, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import StickyNote from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/StickyNote';
import Comment from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Comment';
import Bookmark from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Bookmark';

<Chart data={deviceVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartActionBar isEmphasized>
      {(datum, close) => [
        <ActionButton key="annotate" isQuiet staticColor="white" onPress={close}>
          <StickyNote />
          <Text>Annotate</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="comment" isQuiet staticColor="white" onPress={close}>
          <Comment />
          <Text>Comment</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="bookmark" isQuiet staticColor="white" onPress={close}>
          <Bookmark />
          <Text>Bookmark</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
      ]}
    </ChartActionBar>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `isEmphasized` on `ChartActionBar`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

## Placement and dismissing

The bar opens just above the clicked point. When there isn't room above, it opens below, and it always stays inside the window. Users can move the bar by dragging the handle at its left end, or by focusing the handle and pressing the arrow keys.

Focus moves into the bar when it opens. The bar closes when the user presses Escape, clicks outside it, or runs an action that calls `close`. Focus then returns to where it was. `onClearSelection` is called each time the bar closes, for example to clear selection state you keep outside the chart.

```tsx
<ChartActionBar onClearSelection={() => setSelectedPoint(undefined)}>{actions}</ChartActionBar>
```

## Line

`ChartActionBar` works as a child of `Line` and opens on click; right-clicking a point doesn't open it. The clicked point stays marked while the bar is open.

### ChartInspect and ChartPopover

`ChartInspect` works alongside the action bar. Its tooltip is hidden while the bar is open.

A `Line` can't open both a `ChartPopover` and a `ChartActionBar` on click. To use both, set `rightClick` on `ChartPopover` so it opens on right-click and the action bar opens on click.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  ChartInspect,
  ChartPopover,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { ChartActionBar } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
import { ActionButton, Content, Heading, Text } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import StickyNote from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/StickyNote';
import Comment from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Comment';
import Bookmark from '@react-spectrum/s2/icons/Bookmark';

<Chart data={deviceVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" />
  <Line metric="visits" color="device">
    <ChartInspect>
      {(datum) => (
        <div>
          {datum.device}: {datum.visits.toLocaleString()} visits
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover rightClick width="auto">
      {(datum) => (
        <>
          <Heading level={4}>{datum.device}</Heading>
          <Content>
            <Text>{datum.visits.toLocaleString()} visits</Text>
          </Content>
        </>
      )}
    </ChartPopover>
    <ChartActionBar>
      {(datum, close) => [
        <ActionButton key="annotate" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <StickyNote />
          <Text>Annotate</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="comment" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Comment />
          <Text>Comment</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
        <ActionButton key="bookmark" isQuiet onPress={close}>
          <Bookmark />
          <Text>Bookmark</Text>
        </ActionButton>,
      ]}
    </ChartActionBar>
  </Line>
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `ChartInspect`: included or left out. Shown: included.
-   `ChartPopover`: included or left out. Shown: included.

> **Note:**
> 
> `ChartActionBar` is only supported on `Line`.

## API

### ChartActionBar

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` — Function that receives the clicked datum and a `close` callback and returns the action elements to show. | `((datum: Datum, close: () => void) => React<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>[])` | – |
| `isEmphasized` — Gives the bar an accent background; pair it with `staticColor="white"` on the actions. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `maxActions` — Most actions shown inline before the rest move to a "More actions" menu. | `number` | `4` |
| `onClearSelection` — Called when the action bar closes and the clicked point is deselected. | `(() => void)` | – |

---

# Getting started

## Install

Install the package and its peer dependencies:

**npm:**

```bash
npm install @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2 @react-spectrum/s2 react-aria-components vega vega-lite
```

**yarn:**

```bash
yarn add @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2 @react-spectrum/s2 react-aria-components vega vega-lite
```

**pnpm:**

```bash
pnpm add @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2 @react-spectrum/s2 react-aria-components vega vega-lite
```

### Requirements

| Package | Version |
| --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | `>= 19.0.0` |
| `@react-spectrum/s2` | `>= 1.0.0` |
| `react-aria-components` | `^1.14.0`, the same version `@react-spectrum/s2` uses |
| `vega` | `^6.2.0` |
| `vega-lite` | `^6.4.2` |

Since version 1.3.0, `@react-spectrum/s2` depends on an exact `react-aria-components` version. Install that same version so your app has a single copy, which charts need to share React Aria context with Spectrum 2 components. To find the version `@react-spectrum/s2` uses:

**npm:**

```bash
npm ls react-aria-components
npm install react-aria-components@<that version>
```

**yarn:**

```bash
yarn why react-aria-components
yarn add react-aria-components@<that version>
```

**pnpm:**

```bash
pnpm why react-aria-components
pnpm add react-aria-components@<that version>
```

## ES modules

The package is published as ES modules only (`"type": "module"` in its `package.json`), with one file per source module, so your bundler includes only the components you import.

-   Load it with `import`. There's no CommonJS build, so `require()` and UMD script-tag globals aren't supported.
-   There are two entry points: `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` and `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`. The package's `exports` map blocks deep imports into `dist`.
-   Type declarations are included for both entry points.
-   Like Spectrum 2, the modules import their own CSS files, so your bundler needs to handle CSS imports. Vite and Parcel do by default; webpack needs a CSS loader.
-   Node.js 22.12.0 or later is required.
-   Jest runs CommonJS by default, so it has to transform the package and stub its CSS. Vitest needs the package inlined. See [Testing and troubleshooting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/testing-and-troubleshooting#testing).

## Dark mode

`Chart` renders its own Spectrum 2 `Provider` and loads its own styles, so charts don't need any Spectrum 2 setup in your app. It also means `Chart` doesn't read the color scheme from your app. Its `colorScheme` prop defaults to `light`; if your app supports dark mode, pass the current color scheme to every chart:

```tsx
<Chart data={data} colorScheme={isDark ? 'dark' : 'light'}>
  {/* ... */}
</Chart>
```

See [Colors and theming](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/colors-and-theming).

## Your first chart

`Chart` takes the data as an array of objects, one per data point:

```ts
const guideVisitsData = [
  { date: '2026-03-02T00:00:00', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3120 },
  { date: '2026-03-03T00:00:00', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3480 },
  { date: '2026-03-04T00:00:00', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3360 },
  { date: '2026-03-05T00:00:00', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3710 },
  { date: '2026-03-06T00:00:00', device: 'Desktop', visits: 3940 },
  { date: '2026-03-02T00:00:00', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2280 },
  { date: '2026-03-03T00:00:00', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2410 },
  { date: '2026-03-04T00:00:00', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2650 },
  { date: '2026-03-05T00:00:00', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2590 },
  { date: '2026-03-06T00:00:00', device: 'Mobile', visits: 2870 },
];
```

Its children describe what to draw. In the chart below, `Line` plots `visits` for each `date`, with one line for each `device`. The two `Axis` components label the x and y scales, and `Legend` names each line.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={guideVisitsData}>
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Line dimension="date" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

`Chart` fills the width of its container and is 300px tall by default. See [Sizing](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/sizing).

## Imports

Import most components from the package root:

```tsx
import { Axis, Bar, Chart, Donut, Legend, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
```

Lab components come from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`: `Area`, `Bullet`, `Combo`, `Scatter`, `ScatterAnnotation`, `ScatterPath`, `Trendline`, and `TrendlineAnnotation`.

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

Lab components are experimental, so their APIs may change. See [Stages and lab](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/stages-and-lab).

## Next steps

-   [Data](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/data): field names, dates, missing values, and updates.
-   [Sizing](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/sizing): responsive charts and size-dependent styles.
-   [Chart](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart): every `Chart` prop.
-   Chart types: [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line), [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar), and [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut).
