# Localization

`locale` on `Chart` sets how the chart formats numbers and dates. It doesn't translate text: the strings you pass, like titles and labels, are shown as-is, and the chart's own strings are in English.

```jsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={guideMonthlyRevenueData} locale="de-DE">
  <Axis position="left" grid numberFormat="currency" />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline labelFormat="time" granularity="month" />
  <Line metric="revenue" />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   `locale` on `Chart`: `en-US`, `de-DE`, `fr-FR`, `ja-JP`, `pt-BR` or `zh-CN`. Shown: `de-DE`.
-   `numberFormat` on `Axis`: `shortNumber`, `standardNumber`, `currency` or `shortCurrency`. Shown: `currency`.

The example uses `guideMonthlyRevenueData`:

```ts
const guideMonthlyRevenueData = [
  { datetime: '2025-01-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1184500.5 },
  { datetime: '2025-02-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1092300.25 },
  { datetime: '2025-03-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1257800.75 },
  { datetime: '2025-04-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1310200 },
  { datetime: '2025-05-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1388900.5 },
  { datetime: '2025-06-01T00:00:00', revenue: 1452100.25 },
];
```

## Setting the locale

`locale` defaults to `en-US` and takes one of three forms.

**A locale code** sets both number and time formats:

```tsx
<Chart data={data} locale="de-DE">
```

See [`LocaleCode`](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum-charts/blob/main/packages/locales/src/locale.types.ts) for the supported codes. A code the chart doesn't have falls back to `en-US`.

**Separate number and time locales** let you mix them, or use a code that only has one of the two:

```tsx
<Chart data={data} locale={{ number: 'en-IN', time: 'en-GB' }}>
```

Some codes have only number formats or only time formats. See `NumberLocaleCode` and `TimeLocaleCode` in [the locale types](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum-charts/blob/main/packages/locales/src/locale.types.ts).

**Custom definitions** cover a locale that isn't listed, or a variation of one. Pass a [d3-format locale](https://d3js.org/d3-format#formatLocale) as `number`, a [d3-time-format locale](https://d3js.org/d3-time-format#timeFormatLocale) as `time`, or mix a definition with a code:

```tsx
<Chart
  data={data}
  locale={{
    number: { decimal: '.', thousands: "'", grouping: [3], currency: ['', '\u00a0CHF'] },
    time: 'de-CH',
  }}
>
```

> **Note:**
> 
> `shortNumber` uses the browser's [compact number format](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat#notation), not the d3 definition, for suffixes like K and M. With a custom `number` definition, it uses the browser's language for the suffixes and your definition's decimal symbol.

## What the locale formats

The locale applies wherever the chart formats a value itself:

-   Axis labels: number formats like `standardNumber`, `shortNumber`, and `currency`, duration labels, and month and day names on time axes. See [Label formats](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#label-formats).
-   Labels on marks, like `Bar` value labels and `Donut` segment labels.
-   Default `Donut` tooltip and popover content.

Content you render yourself in `ChartInspect`, `ChartPopover`, or custom axis labels isn't formatted by the chart. Format it with the same locale, for example with `Intl.NumberFormat` or `toLocaleString`:

```tsx
const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('de-DE', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

<ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{euros.format(datum.revenue)}</div>}</ChartInspect>;
```

Dates are shown in the browser's time zone, whatever the locale. Pass dates as epoch milliseconds or ISO strings.

## Currency

`numberFormat="currency"` and `numberFormat="shortCurrency"` on `Axis` use the locale's currency symbol and its position, so `de-DE` writes `1.200.000,00 €`. The symbol comes from the locale, not the data: switch `locale` and the symbol changes too.

To show a currency that doesn't match the locale, like euros with US number formatting, set `currencyCode` and `currencyLocale` on `Axis`. Both are required, and they only apply with `numberFormat="currency"` or a fixed-decimal format like `,.0f`:

```tsx
<Chart data={data} locale="en-US">
  <Axis position="left" numberFormat="currency" currencyCode="EUR" currencyLocale="de-DE" />
  <Line metric="revenue" />
</Chart>
```

`currencyLocale` sets where the symbol goes, and the chart's `locale` still sets the separators. Support for these props is limited; see [Number formats](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#number-formats).

## Translating text

The chart shows your strings as you pass them, so translate them before passing them in. These include `title` and `description` on `Chart`, axis and legend titles, legend labels and descriptions, and the content of `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover`.

The chart's own strings are in English:

-   The empty state says "No data found". Pass a translated `emptyStateText`:
    
    ```tsx
    <Chart data={[]} emptyStateText="Keine Daten gefunden">
    ```
    
-   The loading indicator's accessible label is "Loading", and `ChartActionBar` labels its toolbar, drag handle, and **More actions** menu in English. These strings can't be changed.
    

Data values, like series names, appear in legends and tooltips as they are in `data`. Translate them in the data, or map them with `labels` on [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#labels).

---

# Interactivity

Hover and click behavior comes from the interaction components you add to a mark. This guide explains which one to use, how highlighting and hiding work, and how to drive them from your own state. For props and examples, see [ChartInspect and ChartPopover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction), [ChartActionBar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar), and [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend).

## Choosing an interaction

Interaction components are children of a mark. They render nothing in the chart; they add behavior to the mark they're in.

| Use | When |
| --- | --- |
| [`ChartInspect`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartinspect) | Show details on hover. Content is read-only. |
| [`ChartPopover`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartpopover) | Show content on click that users interact with, like links or buttons. |
| [`ChartActionBar`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar) | Show a toolbar of actions for a clicked point on a `Line`. |
| Mark callbacks, like `onClick` | Run your own code, like navigating or selecting a row elsewhere. |

A mark can have a `ChartInspect` and a `ChartPopover`: the inspect gives a quick read on hover, and clicking opens the popover. On `Line`, a click popover and an action bar can't share the click; set `rightClick` on the popover to open it on right-click instead.

```tsx
import { Bar, Chart, ChartInspect, ChartPopover } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={data}>
  <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" color="os">
    <ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{datum.downloads} downloads</div>}</ChartInspect>
    <ChartPopover>{(datum, close) => <DownloadDetails datum={datum} onDone={close} />}</ChartPopover>
  </Bar>
</Chart>;
```

See [Supported marks](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#supported-marks) for which marks take each component.

## Highlighting

Highlighting keeps some data at full opacity and fades the rest. The chart highlights on its own in these cases:

-   **Hovering a mark with `ChartInspect`.** By default the hovered point stays highlighted; `highlightBy` widens it to the series, the dimension value, or rows that share fields. See [highlightBy](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#highlightby).
-   **Hovering a legend entry with `highlight`.** The entry's series stays highlighted. See [Legend highlighting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#highlighting).
-   **Hovering a category axis label** on an interactive `Bar`. See [Label clicks and hover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#label-clicks-and-hover).
-   **Opening a `ChartPopover`.** The clicked point stays highlighted until it closes.

The legend follows the chart: when a series is highlighted, the other legend entries fade too.

## Hiding series

Users can hide a series by clicking its legend entry. There are two ways to set this up:

-   **Uncontrolled:** `isToggleable` on `Legend`. The legend tracks hidden series itself, starting from `defaultHiddenSeries`. Use this when nothing outside the chart needs to know.
-   **Controlled:** `hiddenSeries` on `Chart`. Your app owns the list, and the legend's `onClick` updates it. Use this to keep the chart in sync with filters, URLs, or other charts.

Don't combine them: a toggleable legend ignores `hiddenSeries`. See [Hiding series](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#hiding-series).

## Controlled state

These `Chart` props let your app decide what's hidden and highlighted:

-   `hiddenSeries`: series to hide.
-   `highlightedSeries`: a series to highlight.
-   `highlightedItem`: one row ID, or a list of them, to highlight. Set `idKey` to a field that uniquely identifies each row, like `id`.

They're controlled: the chart shows what you pass and never changes them. To respond to the user, update your state from a callback and pass it back in. Below, hovering a table row highlights the matching bar, and clicking a bar selects the row:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Axis, Bar, Chart, ChartInspect } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

function DownloadsReport({ data }) {
  const [highlightedId, setHighlightedId] = useState<number | undefined>();
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<number | undefined>();

  return (
    <>
      <Chart data={data} idKey="id" highlightedItem={highlightedId}>
        <Axis position="left" grid />
        <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
        <Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads" color="os" onClick={(datum) => setSelectedId(datum.id)}>
          <ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{datum.downloads} downloads</div>}</ChartInspect>
        </Bar>
      </Chart>
      <table>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr
              key={row.id}
              aria-selected={row.id === selectedId}
              onMouseEnter={() => setHighlightedId(row.id)}
              onMouseLeave={() => setHighlightedId(undefined)}
            >
              <td>{row.browser}</td>
              <td>{row.os}</td>
              <td>{row.downloads}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </>
  );
}
```

Each mark shows highlighting a little differently; see [Highlighting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#highlighting) for the details and known limits.

## Callbacks

Callbacks tell your app what the user did. They don't change the chart themselves.

| Component | Callbacks | Receives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Line` | `onClick`, `onContextMenu` | The data point (`onContextMenu`: event first) |
| `Bar` | `onClick`, `onContextMenu`, `onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut` | The data point (`onContextMenu`: event first) |
| `Legend` | `onClick`, `onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut` | The series name |
| `Axis` | `onClick` | The event, label value, and label index |
| `ChartPopover` | `onOpenChange` | Whether the popover is open |
| `ChartActionBar` | `onClearSelection` | Nothing; called when the bar closes |

The data point passed to mark callbacks is the row from `data`, plus fields the chart adds, like `rscSeriesId`. See [Content](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#content).

## Linking charts

Charts don't share state with each other, but they can share yours. Keep the highlighted series in a parent component, set it from one chart's callbacks, and pass it to every chart:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Axis, Bar, Chart, Legend, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

function LinkedCharts({ trafficData, totalsData }) {
  const [highlightedSeries, setHighlightedSeries] = useState<string | undefined>();

  return (
    <>
      <Chart data={trafficData} highlightedSeries={highlightedSeries}>
        <Axis position="left" grid />
        <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
        <Line dimension="month" metric="visits" color="device" scaleType="point" />
        <Legend
          onMouseOver={(series) => setHighlightedSeries(series)}
          onMouseOut={() => setHighlightedSeries(undefined)}
        />
      </Chart>
      <Chart data={totalsData} highlightedSeries={highlightedSeries}>
        <Axis position="left" grid />
        <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
        <Bar dimension="device" metric="visits" color="device" />
      </Chart>
    </>
  );
}
```

Both charts must use the same values in their `color` field (here `device`) so the series names match. Use `hiddenSeries` the same way to hide a series in every chart at once.

---

# Animation

Charts have two animations: `hover` eases marks in and out of their faded state when a user hovers or you highlight a series, and `drawIn` animates marks in when the chart renders. Both are set on `Chart`. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#animation) on the Chart page for a playground with both.

## Choosing animations

`animationTypes` lists the animations to play. The default is `['hover', 'drawIn']`. To turn off draw-in only, list just `hover`.

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={data} animationTypes={['hover']}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="datetime" metric="value" color="series" />
</Chart>
```

`animations={false}` turns off every animation, whatever `animationTypes` says.

## Draw-in

Draw-in plays once each time the chart mounts. Re-renders, data updates, and resizing don't replay it; an update in the middle of draw-in continues from where it was. A chart draws in again when data arrives after a loading or empty state. Use **Replay** below to watch it again.

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Chart,
  Legend,
  Line,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={lineTrafficData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" labelFormat="time" baseline ticks />
  <Line color="series" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The interactive example has these controls. The code above uses the shown values.

-   **mark**: `Line`, `Bar` or `Donut`. Shown: `Line`.
-   `animationTypes` on `Chart`: `true` or `false`. Shown: `true`.

With **mark** set to `Bar`:

```jsx
import {
  Axis,
  Bar,
  Chart,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={barChannelDeviceData}>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Bar dimension="channel" metric="visits" color="device" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

With **mark** set to `Donut`:

```jsx
import {
  Chart,
  Donut,
  Legend,
} from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart data={browserData}>
  <Donut metric="count" color="browser" />
  <Legend />
</Chart>
```

The chart fades in over 150ms on first paint. Draw-in then waits until the page is rendering frames on time, for at most 300ms, so it doesn't start while other content is still loading. When a chart draws in more than one mark type, every mark uses the longest duration so they finish together.

## Which marks animate

| Mark | Hover | Draw-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#animation) | Yes | Sweeps in from left to right over 850ms. `time`, `linear`, and `point` scales only. |
| [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#animation) | Yes | Bars grow from the baseline over 700ms. |
| [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#animation) | Yes | Segments sweep in over 750ms. |
| [Combo](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/combo#animation) | Yes | Bars and lines draw in together over 850ms. |
| [Area](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/area#animation), [Scatter](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#animation), [Bullet](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bullet#animation) | No | No |

Hover animation applies to marks that respond to hover or highlighting: for example, a mark with a `ChartInspect` or `ChartPopover`, a chart with a `Legend` that has `highlight`, or a chart with `highlightedSeries` or `highlightedItem`. See [Highlighting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#highlighting).

## Reduced motion

When the user's system asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), the chart drops draw-in, because it moves and grows marks. Hover animation fades marks in place, so it still plays.

To turn off hover easing too, set `animations={false}`.

---

# Accessibility

Accessibility in data visualizations isn't fully supported yet and is a work in progress. This page covers what charts expose to assistive technology today and what's still missing.

> **Caution:**
> 
> Charts don't support keyboard navigation, data tables, or screen reader access to individual data points yet. Experimental keyboard navigation for basic bar charts is available behind the `accessibleNavigation` prop on `Chart`; it may change or be removed.

## Describe the chart

`description` on `Chart` is the chart's accessible name. The element that holds the chart's SVG or canvas gets `role="graphics-document"`, `aria-roledescription="visualization"`, and `aria-label` set to `description`.

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Chart
  data={data}
  description="Daily visits by device for March. Desktop leads; mobile overtakes it on weekends."
>
  <Axis position="left" grid />
  <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
  <Line dimension="datetime" metric="visits" color="device" />
</Chart>
```

Without `description`, the chart has no accessible name. Write it like alt text: say what the chart shows and the takeaway, not "line chart".

## Titles

`title` on `Chart`, or a [`Title`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title) child, draws a visible title. With the default `svg` renderer, the title, axes, and legends get their own labels for screen readers, such as "Title text 'Visits by device'" and "X-axis titled 'Month' …". With `renderer="canvas"`, only the chart's `description` is exposed, so use `svg` when accessibility matters.

A visible title and `description` do different jobs: the title names the chart for everyone, and `description` summarizes it for people who can't see it. Use both.

## Hover-only content

`ChartInspect` content, `ChartPopover` content, and legend [`descriptions`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#descriptions) appear only on pointer hover or click, so keyboard and screen reader users can't reach them yet.

## Reduced motion

When the user's system asks for reduced motion, charts skip the draw-in animation automatically. Hover fading still plays. Set `animations={false}` to turn off every animation. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation#reduced-motion).

---

# Exporting

Pass a `ref` to `Chart` to get a `ChartHandle`, which exports the chart as an image. See [Exporting images](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#exporting-images) on the Chart page for a live example.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { ActionButton } from '@react-spectrum/s2';
import { Axis, Chart, ChartHandle, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

function VisitsChart({ data }) {
  const chartRef = useRef<ChartHandle>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <Chart ref={chartRef} data={data} title="Visits by device">
        <Axis position="left" grid />
        <Axis position="bottom" baseline />
        <Line dimension="datetime" metric="visits" color="device" />
      </Chart>
      <ActionButton onPress={() => chartRef.current?.download()}>Download</ActionButton>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Methods

Every method returns a promise.

| Method | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `download(customFileName?)` | A status message, after starting a PNG download. |
| `copy()` | A status message, after writing a PNG to the clipboard. |
| `getBase64Png()` | The PNG as a data URL (`data:image/png;base64,…`). |
| `getSvg()` | The chart as an SVG string. |

The image is the chart at its rendered size, including axes, legend, and title.

### File name

`download()` names the file after the `title` prop on `Chart`, or `chart_export` if there's no `title`, and adds `.png`. A [`Title`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title) child doesn't set the file name. Pass a name to override it, without the extension:

```tsx
chartRef.current?.download('visits-march-2026'); // visits-march-2026.png
```

## When exports fail

The promise rejects with an `Error` when there's nothing to export:

-   The chart hasn't finished rendering yet. Wait for [`onVegaViewReady`](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#advanced) before exporting programmatically.
-   `loading` is `true`, or `data` is empty, so the chart shows a placeholder.
-   The chart has no size, for example because its container is 0px wide.

`copy()` also rejects if the browser refuses the clipboard write. The Clipboard API with images needs a secure context (HTTPS or `localhost`), and browsers usually only allow it in response to a user action, like a button press. Handle the rejection and tell the user:

```tsx
const handleCopy = async () => {
  try {
    await chartRef.current?.copy();
    showToast('Chart copied');
  } catch {
    showToast("Couldn't copy the chart");
  }
};
```

`copy()` and `getBase64Png()` read the rendered image with `fetch` on a `data:` URL. If your app has a Content Security Policy, its `connect-src` must allow `data:`, or both reject.

## Uploading or embedding an image

Use `getBase64Png()` to send a PNG to a server or put it in an `<img>`, and `getSvg()` when you need a vector image, for example in a PDF or a slide.

```tsx
const png = await chartRef.current?.getBase64Png();
await fetch('/api/reports/attachments', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ image: png }) });
```

---

# Testing and troubleshooting

## Testing

`@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` is an ES module package (`"type": "module"`) that imports a CSS file, and it depends on Vega and d3, which are ES modules too. Test runners that expect CommonJS need to transform them.

### Jest

This setup works with Jest 29 and 30 and `jest-environment-jsdom`:

1.  Transform the ES module packages instead of ignoring all of `node_modules`.
2.  Map CSS imports to an empty module. If you already test React Spectrum S2 components, you have this.
3.  Add `structuredClone`, which jsdom doesn't provide, with a custom environment.
4.  Add [`jest-canvas-mock`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jest-canvas-mock). Vega measures text with a canvas, and jsdom logs an error for every canvas it can't create.

```js
// Transforms use your babel.config.js; a .babelrc doesn't apply to node_modules.
module.exports = {
  testEnvironment: './jest.environment.js',
  transformIgnorePatterns: [
    'node_modules/(?!(@spectrum-charts|vega|vega-.*|d3-.*|internmap|json-stringify-pretty-compact|delaunator|robust-predicates)/)',
  ],
  moduleNameMapper: {
    '\\.css$': '<rootDir>/styleMock.js',
    // Jest 30 otherwise loads vega-canvas's Node build, which uses top-level await.
    '^vega-canvas$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/vega-canvas/build/vega-canvas.browser.js',
  },
  setupFiles: ['jest-canvas-mock'],
};
```

```js
const { TestEnvironment } = require('jest-environment-jsdom');

module.exports = class extends TestEnvironment {
  async setup() {
    await super.setup();
    this.global.structuredClone = structuredClone;
  }
};
```

`styleMock.js` is `module.exports = {};`. If Jest still reports `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`, add the package named in the stack trace to the `transformIgnorePatterns` list.

### Vitest

Vitest loads ES modules natively. Use the `jsdom` environment, and inline this package and `@react-spectrum/s2` so Vite handles their CSS imports. Otherwise Node fails with `Unknown file extension ".css"`.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    server: {
      deps: { inline: ['@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2', '@react-spectrum/s2'] },
    },
  },
});
```

### Writing tests

Charts render asynchronously. Wait for the chart element, which has the role `graphics-document` and is named by `description`:

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { Axis, Chart, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

test('renders the visits chart', async () => {
  render(
    <Chart data={data} description="Visits by device" animations={false}>
      <Axis position="bottom" />
      <Line dimension="datetime" metric="visits" color="device" />
    </Chart>
  );
  const chart = await screen.findByRole('graphics-document', { name: 'Visits by device' });
  expect(chart.querySelector('svg')).toBeTruthy();
});
```

-   **Size.** jsdom has no `ResizeObserver`, so the chart measures its container as 500 × 500 px. If your setup adds a `ResizeObserver` mock that never reports a size, the chart's width stays at 0 and nothing renders; pass a numeric `width` in tests.
-   **Animation.** Hover and draw-in update marks over several frames. Set `animations={false}` so the DOM reaches its final state right away, or wrap assertions in `waitFor`.
-   **Marks.** Each mark's elements are in an SVG group with the mark's `name` as a class (`line0`, `bar0`, and so on by default). Query them with `container.querySelectorAll('g.line0 > path')`.
-   **Reduced motion.** Mock `window.matchMedia` so `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` matches to test the reduced-motion path.

## Debugging

These `Chart` props help when a chart doesn't look the way you expect:

-   `debug`: logs the generated Vega spec, with your data merged in, to the console whenever it changes, plus each data row a `ChartInspect` shows. Paste the spec into the [Vega editor](https://vega.github.io/editor/) to explore it.
-   `onVegaViewReady(view)`: called with the [Vega view](https://vega.github.io/vega/docs/api/view/) each time a new view is created, for example when the children change. Data and size changes update the current view without calling it. Use it to read signals and data, or to know when the chart has first rendered.
-   `UNSAFE_vegaSpec`: renders a Vega spec you write instead of children. Use it to reproduce a problem with a hand-edited spec. You lose the defaults the components apply.

## Common problems

### The chart is blank

-   **The container has no width.** With the default `width="auto"`, the chart is as wide as its parent. If the parent is 0px wide, for example a flex item that can shrink to nothing or a hidden tab, nothing renders. `minWidth` doesn't apply in this case. Give the parent a width, or set a numeric `width`. The chart renders once the parent gets a size.
-   **A percentage height with no parent height.** `height="100%"` needs a parent with an explicit height. See [Sizing](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/sizing#height).
-   **`loading` is still `true`, or `data` is empty.** The chart shows a progress circle or `emptyStateText` instead. See [Data](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/data#empty-data-and-loading).

### Dates are wrong or missing

-   **`Date` objects.** The chart copies `data` with `JSON.stringify`, so `Date` objects become ISO strings. Pass dates as epoch milliseconds or ISO strings.
-   **Points land on the previous day.** Timestamps at UTC midnight, and date-only strings like `'2026-03-02'`, display in the user's local time zone, which is the previous day west of UTC.
-   **The mark isn't on a time scale.** `Line` and `Area` default to `scaleType="time"`; check that you haven't set it to another scale type.

See [Dates](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/data#dates).

### The chart doesn't follow dark mode

`Chart` renders its own Spectrum `Provider` and defaults to `colorScheme="light"`; it doesn't read the surrounding app's Provider. Pass `colorScheme` explicitly from your app's theme. See [Light and dark](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/colors-and-theming#light-and-dark).

### Exports reject

`copy()`, `download()`, `getBase64Png()`, and `getSvg()` reject until the chart has rendered, and while it shows a placeholder. See [When exports fail](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/exporting#when-exports-fail).

### Chart throws on render

`Chart` throws if it has no children and no `UNSAFE_vegaSpec`, or if it has both.

---

# Stages and lab

Each component has a stage. The stage tells you how much its API and visuals may still change. Components that aren't stable are exempt from semver, even after the package reaches 1.0.

| Stage | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Lab** | Usable, but has no finalized Spectrum 2 design and no commitment to graduate. Can change in any release. Imported from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`. |
| **Alpha** | The Spectrum 2 design is implemented, along with the core features. The design and API may still change based on feedback, and breaking changes can happen. Animation and accessibility support are in progress. |
| **Beta** | The planned features are complete. Breaking API changes are avoided, and any that are needed are called out in the changelog. Animation and accessibility are complete. |
| **RC** (release candidate) | Feature freeze. The component is validated in consumer environments, and only blocking issues are fixed. |
| **Stable** | Production ready. Follows semver. |

## Current stages

| Stage | Components |
| --- | --- |
| Lab | [Area](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/area), [Bullet](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bullet), [ChartActionBar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar), [Combo](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/combo), [Scatter](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter), [ScatterAnnotation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#scatterannotation), [ScatterPath](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#scatterpath), [Trendline](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#trendline), [TrendlineAnnotation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#trendlineannotation) |
| Alpha | [Chart](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart), [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line), [Bar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar), [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut), [DonutSummary](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#donutsummary), [SegmentLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#segmentlabel), [Axis](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis), [AxisThumbnail](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#axisthumbnail), [ReferenceLine](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#referenceline), [Legend](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend), [Title](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/title), [ChartInspect](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartinspect), [ChartPopover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartpopover), [LineDirectLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#linedirectlabel), [LineForecast](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#lineforecast), [BarDirectLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#bardirectlabel) |

## Lab

Every new chart type starts in lab. Lab components work, but their API and styling may change once a Spectrum 2 design exists.

Import them from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`, so their status is visible in your code. Everything else, including `Chart` and `Axis`, comes from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`:

```tsx
import { Axis, Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter, ScatterPath } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';

<Chart data={data}>
  <Axis position="bottom" />
  <Axis position="left" />
  <Scatter dimension="x" metric="y" color="series">
    <ScatterPath groupBy={['series']} />
  </Scatter>
</Chart>;
```

-   **Proposing one.** Anyone can open an issue or pull request for a new chart type. Maintainers decide whether it fits the library.
-   **Graduating.** A lab component moves to alpha once it has a finalized design and the maintainers commit to it. It's then exported from the main entry.
-   **Removal.** A lab component can be removed if it doesn't fit the project's goals and its usage is low. Removals are announced in the changelog.

If you use a lab component, [open an issue](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum-charts/issues) with your use case, bugs, or requests. Feedback shapes the component before it graduates.

## Release candidate period

RC confirms a component works in real apps; it isn't for adding features. Feature requests that come in during RC are scheduled after the stable release.

-   The first component to reach stable, which takes the package to 1.0, has a 3-week RC period. Later components have 1–2 weeks.
-   The period restarts when a blocking issue is found and fixed. Blocking issues are incorrect rendering, crashes, accessibility failures, and API defects that couldn't be fixed after stable without a breaking change.
-   Other bugs become known issues, fixed in patch releases after stable.

## How to tell a component's stage

-   **In your editor.** The component's documentation comment has an `@experimental` (lab), `@alpha`, or `@beta` tag. Release candidates use `@beta` and say "Release candidate." Stable components have no tag.
-   **In these docs and in Storybook.** Component pages and stories show a stage badge.
-   **In the changelog.** Stage changes are announced in the release notes.

---

# 0.11.0

This release raises the minimum Node version. To update your app, see [Upgrading](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/upgrading#from-0100).

## Breaking changes

-   **Node 22.12 or later.** The S2 packages require Node `>=22.12.0`. The `vega-lite` peer dependency now installs a version that needs Node 22.12, so installs on Node 20 failed with strict engine checks.

---

# 0.10.0

Donut is now an alpha component. This release also turns on animation by default and ships the package as ES modules for smaller bundles. It includes breaking changes; to update your app, see [Upgrading](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/upgrading#from-090).

## Breaking changes

-   **ESM only.** The package ships as ES modules and requires Node `>=20.19.0`.
-   **New peer dependency.** `react-aria-components` `^1.14.0`.
-   **Entry points.** `Donut`, `DonutSummary`, and `SegmentLabel` move to the package root. The `pre-alpha` entry point is renamed `lab`, and `ChartActionBar` is imported from `lab`.
-   **Donut.** `startAngle` and `otherItemColor` are removed.

## Highlights

-   **Donut is alpha.** `Donut`, `DonutSummary`, and `SegmentLabel` are imported from the package root and follow the alpha stage's stability rules. This release adds default `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` content, labels revealed on hover, size-based ring and label spacing, and many layout fixes. See [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut) and [Stages and lab](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/stages-and-lab).
-   **Animation on by default.** Lines, bars, donuts, and combos draw in when the chart mounts, and hover fades animate, following Spectrum 2 motion. Draw-in plays once per mount. When the user prefers reduced motion, draw-in is skipped and hover fades still play. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).
-   **Smaller bundles.** The package no longer bundles its own copies of React Spectrum S2, React Aria, or Vega, so it adds about half as much to an app that already uses React Spectrum S2.
-   **ChartActionBar (lab).** A floating toolbar of actions for a clicked line point. See [ChartActionBar](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart-action-bar).

## Changed defaults

-   Top and bottom legends align to the start of the chart instead of the center.
-   Donut segments are sorted largest first. Set `sortOrder="data"` to keep data order.
-   `Chart` props set to `undefined` fall back to their defaults.

## Donut

-   New semicircle variant: `variant="semicircle"`. See [Semicircle](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#semicircle).
-   `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` show the segment's color, name, share, and value when they have no children. See [Default content](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#default-content).
-   Hovering a segment shows its label, even when the label was hidden to avoid overlap. Hovering or clicking a label behaves like hovering or clicking its segment.
-   Ring thickness, label spacing, and donut size scale with the chart size, and side legends stay next to the donut.
-   Pie donuts have a 1px gap between segments.
-   Semicircle `DonutSummary` deltas sit inside the arc, and summary text that would truncate completely is hidden.
-   Fixed label overlap, tiny segments, and donuts growing or shifting on resize.

## Bar

-   `BarDirectLabel` follows each bar in stacked and dodged bars, and hides labels that overlap or don't fit. New `overflow` and `dataKey` props. See [BarDirectLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#bardirectlabel).
-   Better keyboard and screen reader support: dodged bars can be focused, focused bars and groups are described by their values, and Shift+Tab returns to the last focused bar.
-   Fixed `highlightedItem` (which now respects `idKey`), `ChartInspect` group highlighting, and short-number label formats.

## Line

-   Fixed hover with `interactionMode="item"`, series highlighting, single-series lines, and `interpolate="basis"`.
-   Fixed charts collapsing or flickering with fixed metric-axis ranges or when every series is hidden.
-   Fixed crashes with `highlightedItem` on a line without `ChartInspect` or `ChartPopover`, and with `MetricRange`.
-   Hovering a point at the chart edge no longer shifts the chart.

## Axis and reference lines

-   Reference lines outside the axis range no longer collapse the chart or flicker on hover.
-   A right axis lines up with a gridded left axis.

## Lab charts

-   **Area**: fixed a crash with `highlightedItem`, and band hover points sit on the band's upper edge.
-   **Bullet**: fixed hidden and missing targets, and value labels always use gray-900.
-   **Combo** respects the chart's `animations` and `animationTypes`.
-   **Scatter**: fixed `highlightedItem`, `stroke` set to a data field, and dotted outlines.
-   **Trendline**: dotted trendlines are visible again.

## Performance and stability

-   Charts render once when first displayed instead of twice, so they appear faster and no longer stay blank until hovered.
-   Hover animations stay smooth on charts with many points or series, and charts with many bars render faster.
-   Off-screen and idle charts do no animation work.
-   A chart with no children logs an error instead of throwing.

---

# Migrating from S1

This guide moves a chart from `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` (S1) to `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` (S2). It also applies if you used the S1 `s2` prop: S2 always uses Spectrum 2 styling, so that prop is gone.

Most chart code carries over unchanged. The work is in four places: packages and imports, `ChartTooltip` becoming `ChartInspect`, a few components and props with no S2 equivalent, and a few changed defaults. Each section below has a table to scan, and the [checklist](#checklist) at the end sums it up.

## Packages

S2 is a separate package. It's built on [React Spectrum S2](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/s2/) instead of React Spectrum v3, and it needs React 19.

| Dependency | S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chart package | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| React Spectrum | `@adobe/react-spectrum >=3.23.0` | `@react-spectrum/s2 >=1.0.0` |
| `react`, `react-dom` | `>=17.0.2` | `>=19.0.0` |
| `react-aria-components` | not needed | `^1.14.0` |
| `vega`, `vega-lite` | `^6.2.0`, `^6.4.2` | `^6.2.0`, `^6.4.2` (same) |
| Module format | `require` or `import` | ESM only (`import`) |
| Node | No requirement | `>=22.12.0` |

```bash
yarn remove @adobe/react-spectrum-charts
yarn add @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2 @react-spectrum/s2 react-aria-components
```

You can install both packages side by side and migrate one chart at a time.

S2 ships ESM only, so `require()` and deep imports into `dist` don't work. Jest needs to transform the package; see [Testing and troubleshooting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/testing-and-troubleshooting#jest).

## Imports

S1 split components across `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts`, `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/alpha`, and `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/rc`. S2 has two entry points: `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` for alpha and later components, and `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` for components still being designed. See [Stages and lab](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/stages-and-lab).

| Component | S1 import | S2 import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Chart`, `Axis`, `AxisThumbnail`, `Bar`, `ChartPopover`, `EmptyState`, `Legend`, `Line`, `LinePointAnnotation`, `ReferenceLine`, `Title` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| `ChartTooltip` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` | `ChartInspect` from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| `Donut`, `DonutSummary`, `SegmentLabel` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/rc` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| `Area`, `Scatter`, `ScatterAnnotation`, `ScatterPath`, `Trendline`, `TrendlineAnnotation` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` |
| `Bullet`, `Combo` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/alpha` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` |
| `Annotation`, `AxisAnnotation`, `BigNumber`, `MetricRange`, `Venn` | `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts`, `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/rc`, or `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/alpha` | Not in S2. See [Removed components](#removed-components). |
| `BarDirectLabel`, `LineDirectLabel`, `LineForecast`, `LoadingState` | Not in S1 | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| `ChartActionBar` | Not in S1 | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` |

```tsx
// Before
import { Axis, Chart, ChartTooltip, Line, Scatter } from '@adobe/react-spectrum-charts';
import { Donut, DonutSummary } from '@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/rc';

// After
import { Axis, Chart, ChartInspect, Donut, DonutSummary, Line } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

Type names follow the components: `ChartTooltipProps` is `ChartInspectProps`, and `TooltipHandler` is `InspectHandler`.

## Chart

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `s2` | Removed. S2 always uses Spectrum 2 styling. |
| `theme` | Removed. Use `colorScheme` and `backgroundColor`. |
| `colors` default `categorical16` | Default `s2Categorical20`, the same as S1 with `s2`. |
| Not available | `animations`, `animationTypes`. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#animation). |

Every other `Chart` prop, its default, and the `ChartHandle` ref methods are the same.

### theme and s2

S1 read colors from an `@adobe/react-spectrum` theme. S2 charts render their own S2 `Provider`, so pass the color scheme directly. See [Color and theme](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#color-and-theme).

```tsx
// Before
<Chart data={data} theme={darkTheme} colorScheme="dark" s2>

// After
<Chart data={data} colorScheme="dark">
```

S2 charts use the Spectrum 2 palette, `s2Categorical20`, by default. If you passed an S1 palette such as `categorical12` or `categorical16` to `colors`, remove it so the chart uses Spectrum 2 colors. See [Colors and theming](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/colors-and-theming).

### Popover and inspect content

Content you return from `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` renders inside an S2 `Provider`. Build it with `@react-spectrum/s2` components, not React Spectrum v3 components.

## ChartTooltip → ChartInspect

`ChartTooltip` is renamed `ChartInspect`. Its props are the same: `children`, `excludeDataKeys`, `highlightBy`, and `targets`. It works as a child of the same marks. See [ChartInspect](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartinspect).

```tsx
// Before
<Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device">
  <ChartTooltip>{(datum) => <div>{datum.visitors} visitors</div>}</ChartTooltip>
</Line>

// After
<Line dimension="month" metric="visitors" color="device">
  <ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{datum.visitors} visitors</div>}</ChartInspect>
</Line>
```

The children function no longer receives a second argument. S1's `TooltipHandler` was `(datum, hoverType) => ReactNode`; S2's `InspectHandler` is `(datum) => ReactNode`.

On `Line`, adding `ChartInspect` turns off the built-in [hover label](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#hover).

`ChartPopover` is unchanged. See [ChartPopover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartpopover).

## Removed components

| S1 component | Where it went in S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `ChartTooltip` | Renamed `ChartInspect`. See [above](#charttooltip--chartinspect). |
| `MetricRange` | `Line`'s `metricRanges` prop. See [Metric ranges](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#metric-ranges). |
| `Annotation` (Bar labels) | `BarDirectLabel`, for value labels. See [BarDirectLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#bardirectlabel). |
| `AxisAnnotation` | Not available. |
| `BigNumber` | Not available. |
| `Venn` | Not available. |

### MetricRange

`MetricRange` children become objects in `Line`'s `metricRanges` array. `metricStart` and `metricEnd` are required, and `color`, `lineType`, `lineWidth`, `rangeOpacity`, `metric`, `displayOnHover`, and `scaleAxisToFit` keep their S1 names. S2 doesn't support `lineOpacity`, `hoverPoint`, `displayOnHoverTrigger`, or the `'metric'` and `'range'` values of `displayOnHover`; `displayOnHover` is `true` or `false`.

```tsx
// Before
<Line dimension="datetime" metric="value">
  <MetricRange metricStart="low" metricEnd="high" displayOnHover />
</Line>

// After
<Line dimension="datetime" metric="value" metricRanges={[{ metricStart: 'low', metricEnd: 'high', displayOnHover: true }]} />
```

### Bar Annotation

S1's `Annotation` drew a label on each bar from a `textKey` field. S2's `BarDirectLabel` labels each bar with its value, formatted with `format`. Text from a separate field isn't supported.

```tsx
// Before
<Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads">
  <Annotation textKey="label" />
</Bar>

// After
<Bar dimension="browser" metric="downloads">
  <BarDirectLabel />
</Bar>
```

## Line

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut` | Removed. |
| `MetricRange` child | `metricRanges` prop. See [MetricRange](#metricrange). |
| `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |
| `Trendline` child | Not supported. `Trendline` only works inside `Scatter`. |
| Fixed stroke width | Width scales with the chart's width. See [Size](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#size). |
| No hover label | `showHoverLabel` defaults to `true`. See [Hover](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#hover). |

New in S2: `gradient`, `interpolate`, `lineCap`, `alternateSegmentKey`, `alternateSegmentLineType`, `primarySeries`, `otherSeriesColor`, `dimensionHover`, `hoverLabelKey`, and the `LineDirectLabel`, `LineForecast`, and `ChartActionBar` children. See [Line](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line).

## Bar

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `Annotation` child | `BarDirectLabel` child. See [Bar Annotation](#bar-annotation). |
| `Trendline` child | Not supported. See [Not supported yet](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#not-supported-yet). |
| `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |

`onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut`, and `onClick` still work. New in S2: `diverging`. See [Diverging](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#diverging).

## Donut, DonutSummary, and SegmentLabel

These moved from `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts/rc` to `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`.

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `startAngle` | Removed. Use `variant="semicircle"` for a half donut. See [Semicircle](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#semicircle). |
| `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |
| Empty inspect or popover shows nothing | Shows the segment's color, name, share, and value. |

New in S2: `Donut` `variant`, `sortOrder`, `emphasizedItems`, and `hideDeemphasizedLabels`; `DonutSummary` `delta`; `SegmentLabel` `labelMode`, `swatch`, `showValueRow`, and `showTotal`. See [Donut](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut).

## Area, Scatter, Bullet, and Combo

These are lab components in S2: import them from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`. Their APIs may change between releases.

| Component | S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Area` | `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |
| `Scatter` | `onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut` | Removed. |
| `Scatter` | `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |
| `Trendline` | `displayOnHoverTrigger` | Removed. |
| `Trendline` | Child of `Line`, `Bar`, `Scatter` | Child of `Scatter` only. See [Trendline](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/scatter#trendline). |
| `Bullet` | `ChartTooltip` child | `ChartInspect` child. |

## Axis

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `hasPopover` | Removed. |
| `AxisAnnotation` child | Not available. |
| `ChartTooltip` child | Removed. Use `hasTooltip` and `tooltipText`. See [Label tooltips](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#label-tooltips). |

New in S2: `onClick` for label clicks and `tooltipText`. See [Interaction](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#interaction).

## ReferenceLine

S2 reference lines use a fixed Spectrum 2 style, so most styling props are gone. `value`, `position`, and `label` are unchanged.

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `color`, `lineType` | Removed. Use `secondary` for the lighter style. |
| `icon`, `iconColor` | Removed. |
| `labelColor`, `labelFontWeight`, `labelPosition` | Removed. |
| `layer` | Removed. |
| Not available | `size`, `secondary`. |

```tsx
// Before
<ReferenceLine value={100} label="Target" color="gray-500" lineType="dashed" icon="date" />

// After
<ReferenceLine value={100} label="Target" secondary />
```

See [ReferenceLine](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#referenceline).

## Legend

| S1 | S2 |
| --- | --- |
| `_labelWrap`, `_preferredColumns`, `_maxRows` | Removed. |
| Top and bottom legends centered by default | Left-aligned by default (`align="start"`). |

Spectrum 2 aligns top and bottom legends to the start of the chart. Left and right legends are still centered. See [Position and alignment](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#position-and-alignment).

## Title

`Title` is unchanged. New in S2: `fontSize`.

## Changed defaults

The S2 defaults are the recommended Spectrum 2 behavior. Don't keep an S1 default just to avoid a visual change. The last column says whether the S1 behavior can be kept.

If you're an agent applying this guide:

-   If a changed default can be turned off, tell the user what changed and ask whether to adopt the S2 default (recommended) or keep the S1 behavior. Change the code only to match their answer.
-   If a changed default can't be turned off, tell the user what changed. Don't ask, and don't try to recreate the S1 behavior.

| Prop | S1 | S2 | Keep the S1 behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Chart` `colors` | `categorical16` | `s2Categorical20` | Not possible. Remove S1 palettes. |
| `Legend` `align` (top and bottom) | `middle` | `start` | `align="middle"` on `Legend`. |
| `Line` stroke width | Fixed | Scales with chart width | Not possible. |
| `Line` hover label | None | Shown (`showHoverLabel`) | `showHoverLabel={false}`. |
| Draw-in animation | None | On (`animationTypes`) | `animationTypes={['hover']}`. To turn off all animation, `animations={false}`. |
| `Donut` inspect and popover content | Empty | Default segment details | Not possible. Pass children to show your own content. |
| `Donut` segment order | Data order | Largest first | `sortOrder="data"`. |

Charts with `s2` already used `s2Categorical20`.

## Behavior changes

-   `Chart` props explicitly set to `undefined` fall back to their defaults instead of overriding them.
-   Charts render their own S2 `Provider` with the chart's `colorScheme`, so they don't read an outer React Spectrum v3 `Provider`.
-   Hover fades and draw-in animate by default. Draw-in plays once per mount and is skipped when the user prefers reduced motion. See [Changed defaults](#changed-defaults) and [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).

## Checklist

-   [ ]  Install `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`, `@react-spectrum/s2`, and `react-aria-components`, and upgrade to React 19 and Node 22.12 or later.
-   [ ]  Change imports to `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`, and import `Area`, `Scatter`, `Bullet`, `Combo`, `Trendline`, and their children from `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`.
-   [ ]  Configure Jest to transform the package. See [Testing and troubleshooting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/testing-and-troubleshooting#jest).
-   [ ]  Remove `s2` and `theme` from `Chart`.
-   [ ]  Remove S1 palettes such as `categorical16` from `colors`.
-   [ ]  Rename `ChartTooltip` to `ChartInspect`, and drop any use of the `hoverType` argument.
-   [ ]  Rebuild popover and inspect content with `@react-spectrum/s2` components.
-   [ ]  Replace `MetricRange` with `metricRanges` on `Line`.
-   [ ]  Replace bar `Annotation` with `BarDirectLabel`.
-   [ ]  Remove `AxisAnnotation`, `BigNumber`, `Venn`, and `Trendline` under `Line` or `Bar`.
-   [ ]  Remove `onMouseOver` and `onMouseOut` from `Line` and `Scatter`.
-   [ ]  Remove `ReferenceLine` styling props; use `secondary` or `size`.
-   [ ]  Replace Donut `startAngle` with `variant="semicircle"` or remove it.
-   [ ]  Remove Legend `_labelWrap`, `_preferredColumns`, and `_maxRows`.
-   [ ]  Check line widths at your chart sizes.
-   [ ]  For each [changed default](#changed-defaults), ask the user whether to adopt the S2 default (recommended) or keep the S1 behavior where that's possible. Otherwise, tell them what changed.

---

# Upgrading

This page lists the code changes that keep your charts building and working when you upgrade `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`: breaking changes, removed or renamed props, and peer dependency and Node version bumps. It also lists changed defaults. Bug fixes and new features that need no code changes are left out; see the release notes ([0.11.0](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/release-notes/0-11-0), [0.10.0](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/release-notes/0-10-0)) for those.

Find the section for the version you're on, then apply it and every section above it. For example, from 0.8.0, apply [From 0.8.0](#from-080), [From 0.9.0](#from-090), and [From 0.10.0](#from-0100).

Coming from `@adobe/react-spectrum-charts` instead? See [Migrating from S1](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/migrating-from-s1).

## Changed defaults

Each changed default is marked **Changed default** and says what's new, what it was, and whether you can keep the old behavior. The new defaults are the recommended Spectrum 2 behavior. Don't override them just to keep a chart looking the same as before.

If you're an agent applying this guide:

-   Don't keep an old default on your own.
-   If a changed default can be turned off, tell the user what changed and ask whether to adopt the new default (recommended) or keep the old behavior. Change the code only to match their answer.
-   If a changed default can't be turned off, tell the user what changed. Don't ask, and don't try to work around it.

## From 0.10.0

### Node version

Node `>=22.12.0` is required. Installs on Node 20 fail with an engine error. No code changes are needed.

```bash
yarn add @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2@latest
```

## From 0.9.0

### ESM only

The package ships as ES modules only (`"type": "module"`). `require()`, the UMD global, and imports from inside `dist/` no longer work. Import from the package entry points instead.

```ts
// Before
const { Chart } = require('@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2');

// After
import { Chart } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
```

Jest must transform `@spectrum-charts/*` and stub CSS imports. See [Testing and troubleshooting](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/testing-and-troubleshooting#jest).

### Node and peer dependencies

-   Node `>=20.19.0` is required.
-   `react-aria-components` `^1.14.0` is a new peer dependency.

```bash
yarn add @spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2@latest react-aria-components@^1.14.0
```

### Entry points

The `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/pre-alpha` entry point is renamed `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab`, and `Donut`, `DonutSummary`, and `SegmentLabel` move to `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2`. The `alpha` and `beta` subpaths are removed; they never pointed at published files. See [Stages and lab](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/stages-and-lab).

| Component | 0.9.0 import | 0.10.0 import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Donut`, `DonutSummary`, `SegmentLabel` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/pre-alpha` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2` |
| `Area`, `Bullet`, `Combo`, `Scatter`, `ScatterAnnotation`, `ScatterPath`, `Trendline`, `TrendlineAnnotation` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/pre-alpha` | `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` |

```ts
// Before
import { Donut, DonutSummary, Scatter, ScatterPath } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/pre-alpha';

// After
import { Donut, DonutSummary } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';
import { Scatter, ScatterPath } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab';
```

### Donut

`startAngle` and `otherItemColor` are removed. For a half donut, use `variant="semicircle"`. See [Semicircle](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#semicircle).

```tsx
// Before
<Donut metric="count" color="browser" startAngle={-Math.PI / 2} otherItemColor="gray-300" />

// After
<Donut metric="count" color="browser" />
```

**Changed default: segment order.** Segments are sorted largest-first. They were in data order. Boolean donuts still use data order. See [Semicircle](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/donut#semicircle).

-   Keep the old behavior: set `sortOrder="data"`, for example for ordered categories like survey responses.

```tsx
<Donut metric="count" color="response" sortOrder="data" />
```

**Changed default: inspect and popover content.** `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` on a `Donut` show the segment's color, name, share, and value when they have no children. They were empty. See [Default content](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#default-content).

-   Keep the old behavior: not possible. To show your own content instead, pass children.

### Bar

**Changed default: hover animation.** Bar hover fades animate, like Line and Donut. They were instant.

-   Keep the old behavior: leave `'hover'` out of `animationTypes`, or set `animations={false}`. Either one also turns off hover animation for the other marks in the chart.

**Changed default: BarDirectLabel visibility.** Labels outside the bar are hidden when they would overlap a bar or another label. Labels inside the bar that don't fit are hidden, except at `position="start"`, where they move outside the bar tip. All labels used to show. See [BarDirectLabel](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/bar#bardirectlabel).

-   Keep the old behavior for labels inside the bar: set `overflow="spill"` to move them outside instead of hiding them.
-   Keep the old behavior for labels outside the bar: not possible.

### Legend alignment

**Changed default.** Top and bottom legends align to the start of the chart, matching Spectrum 2. They were centered. See [Position and alignment](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/legend#position-and-alignment).

-   Keep the old behavior: set `align="middle"` on `Legend`.

### Undefined Chart props

`Chart` props explicitly set to `undefined` now fall back to their defaults instead of overriding them. Code like `height={settings.height}` now gets the default `height` when `settings.height` is missing. If you relied on `undefined` overriding a default, pass the value you want instead.

### Draw-in

**Changed default.** `animationTypes` defaults to `['hover', 'drawIn']`, so lines, bars, donuts, and combos animate in when the chart mounts. Draw-in plays once per mount; re-renders and data updates don't replay it. Charts used to appear without drawing in. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation).

-   Keep the old behavior: set `animationTypes={['hover']}`.

```tsx
<Chart data={data} animationTypes={['hover']}>
```

### Reduced motion

**Changed default.** Charts now honor the user's reduced-motion setting: draw-in is skipped and hover animation still plays. The setting used to be ignored. See [Animation](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/guides/animation#reduced-motion).

-   Keep the old behavior: not possible. To turn off hover animation as well, set `animations={false}`.

## From 0.8.0

No changes need action.

## From 0.7.0

No changes need action.

## From 0.6.0

No changes need action.

## From 0.5.0

No changes need action. 0.6.0 added the `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/pre-alpha` entry point; it's `@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2/lab` in 0.10.0. See [From 0.9.0](#entry-points).

## From 0.4.0

No changes need action. 0.5.0 added `animationTypes`; its default, `['hover']`, keeps the hover animation and leaves draw-in off.

## From 0.3.0

### Peer dependencies

0.4.0 replaced `@adobe/react-spectrum` with `@react-spectrum/s2` `>=1.0.0`. Charts render their own S2 `Provider`, so build `ChartInspect` and `ChartPopover` content with `@react-spectrum/s2` components.

```bash
yarn remove @adobe/react-spectrum
yarn add @react-spectrum/s2
```

### ChartTooltip → ChartInspect

`ChartTooltip` is renamed `ChartInspect`. Props and the children function are the same. Types are renamed too: `ChartTooltipProps` → `ChartInspectProps`, `ChartTooltipElement` → `ChartInspectElement`, and `TooltipHandler` → `InspectHandler`. See [ChartInspect](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/interaction#chartinspect).

```tsx
// Before
import { ChartTooltip } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Line dimension="datetime" metric="value">
  <ChartTooltip>{(datum) => <div>{datum.value}</div>}</ChartTooltip>
</Line>

// After
import { ChartInspect } from '@spectrum-charts/react-spectrum-charts-s2';

<Line dimension="datetime" metric="value">
  <ChartInspect>{(datum) => <div>{datum.value}</div>}</ChartInspect>
</Line>
```

### Chart theme

The `theme` prop on `Chart` is removed. Use `colorScheme`. See [Color and theme](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/chart#color-and-theme).

```tsx
// Before
<Chart data={data} theme={darkTheme} colorScheme="dark">

// After
<Chart data={data} colorScheme="dark">
```

### Line size

**Changed default.** Line stroke width, point size, and hover rings scale with the chart's width. They were fixed. Check your charts at the sizes you use. See [Size](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/line#size).

-   Keep the old behavior: not possible.

## From 0.2.0

### React 19

0.3.0 raised the `react` and `react-dom` peer dependencies to `>=19.0.0`. Upgrade React before upgrading the package.

Skip 0.3.0 itself, which was published without its build output. Use 0.3.2 or later.

## From 0.1.0

### ReferenceLine

0.2.0 removed `ReferenceLine`'s `color`, `icon`, `iconColor`, `layer`, `labelColor`, `labelFontWeight`, and `lineType`. Reference lines use a fixed Spectrum 2 style. 0.4.0 added `secondary` for a lighter line and `size`. See [ReferenceLine](/react-spectrum-charts/s2/docs/docs/axis#referenceline).

```tsx
// Before
<ReferenceLine value={100} label="Target" color="gray-500" lineType="dashed" />

// After
<ReferenceLine value={100} label="Target" />
```
